## Q16 — SubModule.xml and MBSubModuleBase lifecycle

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer

**(a) The `SubModule.xml` format as the game parses it.** Two things make a module: a folder **directly** under `<install>/Modules/` that contains a file literally named `SubModule.xml` (`ModuleHelper._pathPrefix` = `BasePath.Name + "Modules/"`, enumerated one level deep by `GetPhysicalModules`), and an `Id` that the launcher hands the game on the command line (`ModuleHelper.InitializeModules` registers only modules whose id is found in `Utilities.GetModulesNames()` = native `IUtil.GetModulesCode().Split('*')`; a folder nobody asked for is never opened). The folder name is decorative — identity is `<Id>` (`GetModuleInfo`/`GetModuleFullPath` key the registry on `Id.ToLower()`, which is why the vanilla folder `SandBox` carries the id `Sandbox`). Root element is `Module`; `ModuleInfo.LoadWithFullPath` is plain `XmlDocument` + XPath and every scalar is read as `SelectSingleNode("<X>").Attributes["value"].InnerText`, so **each scalar is a value-attribute element** and indentation, spacing around `=`, child order and `<!-- comments -->` are all irrelevant (vanilla `Native` writes `<Id value = "Native"/>`). Nothing schema-validates this file: `xmlschemas/` holds only object schemas (`NPCCharacters.xsd` …), `ModuleHelper.GetXsdPath` is consulted for object-XML ids only, and there is no `SubModule.xsd`.

```xml
<Module>
  <Name value="…" /><Id value="…" /><Version value="v0.1.0" /><ModuleType value="Community" />
  <DependedModules><DependedModule Id="Native" /><DependedModule Id="SandBoxCore" /><DependedModule Id="Sandbox" /></DependedModules>
  <SubModules><SubModule><Name value="Core" /><DLLName value="My.dll" /><SubModuleClassType value="Ns.MySubModule" /><Tags><Tag key="DedicatedServerType" value="none" /></Tags></SubModule></SubModules>
  <Xmls><XmlNode><XmlName id="NPCCharacters" path="MyCompanions" /><IncludedGameTypes><GameType value="Campaign" /></IncludedGameTypes></XmlNode></Xmls>
</Module>
```

Hard-required (dereferenced with no null check): `Name`, `Id`, `Version`; inside a `<SubModule>`: `Name`, `DLLName`, `SubModuleClassType`. A throw anywhere in `LoadWithFullPath` is caught by `GetPhysicalModules`, which shows the modal *"Module <folder> can't be loaded, there are some errors."* and drops the module entirely — so one typo in `<Version>` costs the module, not just the field. Optional scalars: `RequiredBaseVersion` (only ever compared for NavalDLC), `DefaultModule` (`"true"` → `IsDefault`), `ModuleType` ∈ `Community|Official|OfficialOptional` — missing means the enum default `Community`, i.e. `IsOfficial == false`, which changes error reporting (below) — and `ModuleCategory` ∈ `Singleplayer|Multiplayer|MultiplayerOptional|Server` (default `Singleplayer`). `Version` grammar comes from `ApplicationVersion.FromString`: split on `.` into **exactly 3 or 4** parts; part 0 = a type letter glued to the major (`v` Release, plus `a`, `b`, `e`, `d`; any other letter → `ApplicationVersionType.Invalid`), the rest go through `Convert.ToInt32`, and a 4th part is the changeSet (otherwise official modules get `ApplicationVersion.DefaultChangeSet = 119303` stamped in by `ModuleInfo.UpdateVersionChangeSet`). `v0.1.0` and `v1.4.8` parse, `v2.4.2.248` is the legal 4-part form; `0.1.0`, `v0.1` and `v1.2.3.4.5` throw `"Wrong version as string"`; a wildcard (`v1.3.4.*`) throws a `FormatException` out of `Convert.ToInt32`, caught only for `DependentVersion`, where the dependency then keeps `ApplicationVersion.Empty`.

`DependedModules/DependedModule` carries attributes `Id` (required), `DependentVersion` (optional, lenient) and `Optional` (`bool.TryParse`, default false) into the struct `DependedModule(ModuleId, Version, IsOptional)`; `ModulesToLoadAfterThis/Module Id=` and `IncompatibleModules/Module Id=` reuse the same struct with an empty version. What the game actually does with them: `GetDependentModulesOf(X)` = X's own `DependedModules` **plus** every module that lists X in its `ModulesToLoadAfterThis`, and `GetSortedModules` feeds that to `MBMath.TopologySort` (post-order DFS, dependencies emitted first), so `DependedModules` = "load these before me" and `ModulesToLoadAfterThis` = "load me before these" — Harmony lists Native/SandBoxCore/Sandbox/StoryMode/CustomBattle under `ModulesToLoadAfterThis` precisely so it sorts *before* everything it patches. But the **game process never sorts**: `_loadedModules` insertion order is the launcher's command-line order, that order drives `Module.LoadSubModules`, `Module.CollectSubModules` and every hook fan-out, and `GetSortedModules` has no caller anywhere in `decomp`. Likewise `IncompatibleModules` is parsed and then never read, no managed code compares a `DependedModule`'s version with the depended module's `Version` (`UpdateVersionChangeSet` is the only touch), `IsOptional` has no consumer, and `DependedModuleMetadatas`, `Url`, `UpdateInfo` and the BUTR `xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation` occur nowhere in `decomp` — they are community/tooling conventions for the launcher and mod managers (see Uncertain). Note the id-matching asymmetry: module lookup is case-insensitive, but `GetDependentModulesOf` compares with `==`, so a dependency line must spell `Sandbox` (lowercase b) exactly as vanilla's `<Id>` does.

`SubModules/SubModule` children: `Name` (label, appears in load-error text `"<module>.<submodule>"`), `DLLName` (**file name including extension**), `SubModuleClassType` (fully qualified type name), optional `Assemblies/Assembly value="X.dll"` (preloaded before the main DLL — how `SandBox.GauntletUI` gets its `…AutoGenerated.0.dll` into the AppDomain before instantiation) and optional `Tags/Tag key= value=`. A `<SubModule>` missing `Name`/`DLLName`/`SubModuleClassType` throws inside `SubModuleInfo.LoadFrom`, but `ModuleInfo` swallows the exception **and still appends the half-built entry** (`SubModules.Add` is outside the `catch`) — the failure then resurfaces far away as a `Path.Combine` null-argument crash or a *"Cannot find: …"* box, so an attribute typo in a `<SubModule>` is a hard failure, not a warning. `Tag key` must parse as `SubModuleInfo.SubModuleTags` (`RejectedPlatform`, `ExclusivePlatform`, `DedicatedServerType`, `IsNoRenderModeElement`, `DependantRuntimeLibrary`, `PlayerHostedDedicatedServer`, `EngineType`; unknown keys are dropped), and `Module.CheckIfSubmoduleCanBeLoadable`/`GetSubModuleValiditiy` silently skips the whole sub-module when a tag does not fit: platform names for the platform tags; `DedicatedServerType` ∈ `none|both|all|custom|matchmaker|community` (`none` = ordinary client only, which is what every vanilla client module declares); `IsNoRenderModeElement` valid only when the value is literally `false`; `DependantRuntimeLibrary` compared with `ApplicationPlatform.CurrentRuntimeLibrary`; `PlayerHostedDedicatedServer` compared with the startup flag; `EngineType` never validated (falls through the `switch` → true). Any `DedicatedServerType` value other than `none` also forces `SubModuleInfo.IsTWCertifiedDLL = true`; otherwise certification is Authenticode-based (`GetIsTWCertified` compares the DLL certificate's `CertHashString`/`CertSerialNumber` with hardcoded TaleWorlds constants).

`Xmls` is **not** part of `ModuleInfo` at all: `Module.LoadSubModules` registers it per module, in load order, *before any DLL is touched* — `XmlResource.GetMbprojxmls(module.Id)` (reads `ModuleData/project.mbproj`, `base/file`) then `XmlResource.GetXmlListAndApply(module.Id)`, which parses `Xmls/XmlNode` entries: `XmlName` attributes `id` (object-list id whose XSD must accept the file — install `XmlSchemas/<id>.xsd`, overridable per module by `ModuleData/XmlSchemas/<id>.xsd`) and `path` (resolved by `ModuleHelper.GetXmlPath` to `<module>/ModuleData/<path>.xml`, or every `*.xml` inside a folder of that name), plus optional `IncludedGameTypes/GameType value=` filters (`Campaign`, `CampaignStoryMode`, `CustomGame`, `EditorGame` …). Registration order is also the merge order used later by `MBObjectManager.GetMergedXmlForManaged` (Q5/Q14), so a module listed later can override an earlier module's rows for the same `id`. A data-only module needs no DLL: vanilla `SandBoxCore` ships an empty `<SubModules />` and all of its content as `Xmls`.

**(b) The exact ids.** From the local 1.4.8 copy (`~/bannerlord/moduledata_win/<folder>/SubModule.xml`): `Native` (folder `Native`, `ModuleType Official`, `Version v1.4.8`, empty `<DependedModules/>`; `ModuleInfo.IsNative` compares the id OrdinalIgnoreCase and `Module.DeactiveModule` refuses to deactivate it), `SandBoxCore` (folder `SandBoxCore`, Name "SandBox Core", deps `Native`, no sub-modules), **`Sandbox`** (folder `SandBox`, lowercase **b**; deps `Native` + `SandBoxCore` with `DependentVersion="v1.4.8" Optional="false"`; three sub-modules `SandBox`/`SandBox.dll`/`SandBox.SandBoxSubModule`, `SandBox.View` (+`SandBox.ViewModelCollection.dll` as an `Assembly`), `SandBox.GauntletUI` (+two auto-generated assemblies)), `StoryMode` (deps `Native`, `SandBoxCore`, `Sandbox`), `CustomBattle` (deps `Native`, `SandBoxCore`), `NavalDLC` (`ModuleType OfficialOptional`, `Version v1.2.8`, `RequiredBaseVersion v1.4.8`, `DefaultModule true`), plus `Multiplayer`, `BirthAndDeath`, `FastMode` — the complete official set is `ModuleHelper.GetOfficialModuleIds()`. Harmony is a `ModuleType Community` module with **`Id value="Bannerlord.Harmony"`**, `Name value="Harmony"`, `Version value="v2.4.2.248"`, an empty `<DependedModules />` next to a `ModulesToLoadAfterThis` block (Native, SandBoxCore, Sandbox, StoryMode, CustomBattle) and a BUTR `DependedModuleMetadatas` block, sub-module `Harmony`/`Bannerlord.Harmony.dll`/`Bannerlord.Harmony.SubModule` with `Assemblies` `0Harmony.dll`, `Mono.Cecil*.dll`, `MonoMod.*.dll`. So this mod's `DependedModules` should be `Native`, `SandBoxCore`, `Sandbox` (add `Bannerlord.Harmony` only if it patches, and `StoryMode` only if it hooks story content — vanilla itself *deactivates* StoryMode for saves without story data, see `StoryModeViewSubModule.OnBeforeGameStart`).

**(c) `MBSubModuleBase` overrides in call order.** Fan-outs iterate `_subModuleBases.Values` / `Module.CollectSubModules()` (module insertion order × `<SubModule>` XML order, inactive modules skipped), and every member is `protected internal virtual` or `public virtual` on `MBSubModuleBase`.
1. Boot (native bridge `CoreManaged.OnInitialize` → `Module.CreateModule`, then `Module.Initialize`, which like `Module.LoadSingleModule` carries the `[MBCallback(null, false)]` attribute and is therefore invoked straight from native code): `ProcessApplicationArguments` → `ModuleHelper.InitializeModules(Utilities.GetModulesNames())` → localization + `GlobalTextManager.LoadDefaultTexts` → `ModuleHelper.GetModules()` → `LoadSubModules(modules, loadNewModules: false)`.
2. Per module (launcher order): all `Xmls` registration first, then per `<SubModule>` in XML order: tag check → `AssemblyLoader.LoadFrom` of each `Assemblies` entry then the `DLLName` assembly → `Module.AddSubModule` (`GetType` + parameterless constructor + `Managed.AddTypes`). Static constructors and field initializers run here — keep them side-effect-light (Q15).
3. `Module.InitializeSubModuleBases()` → **`OnSubModuleLoad()`** for every instance, no try/catch (a throw kills boot, Q15). Modules activated at runtime (`Module.LoadSingleModule` → `ModuleHelper.InitializeSingleModule` + `LoadSubModules(…, loadNewModules: true)`) instead get `OnSubModuleLoad()` on the new instances only, followed by **`OnNewModuleLoad()`** on *all* sub-modules (vanilla `SandBoxSubModule.OnNewModuleLoad` re-runs `SaveManager.InitializeGlobalDefinitionContext`).
4. `Module.SetInitialModuleScreenAsRootScreen()` → **`OnBeforeInitialModuleScreenSetAsRoot()`** for all — the last hook before the main menu; vanilla `SandBoxSubModule` initializes `MBSaveLoad` here behind an `_initialized` guard. Then the splash video → `OnInitialModuleScreenActivated` → re-activates inactive modules → `OnInitialState()` fan-out.
5. Starting a game: `MBGameManager.StartNewGame` → `Module.OnBeforeGameStart` → **`OnBeforeGameStart(MBGameManager, List<string> disabledModules)`**; ids a sub-module appends to that list are `DeactiveModule`d → **`OnSubModuleDeactivated()`** (vanilla `StoryModeViewSubModule.OnBeforeGameStart` drops `"StoryMode"` when the save/game has no story content), and `Module.OnGameEnd` re-activates them later → **`OnSubModuleActivated()`**.
6. `Game.CreateGame(GameType, GameManagerBase)` (or `Game.LoadSaveGame`) → `Game.RegisterTypes` → **`RegisterSubModuleTypes()`** fan-out, sandwiched between `GameType.BeforeRegisterTypes` and `GameType.OnRegisterTypes`.
7. `Game.Initialize()` → `GameType.OnInitialize()` → for a campaign, `Campaign.OnInitialize`: `new CampaignGameStarter(...)` → `SandBoxManager.Initialize(campaignGameStarter)` (vanilla's core behavior + model roster, `gameStarter.AddBehavior(new PartyUpgraderCampaignBehavior())` …) → **`InitializeGameStarter(Game, IGameStarter)`** fan-out ← *this is where vanilla adds campaign behaviors and where this mod must add them*: cast `gameStarterObject` to `CampaignGameStarter` when `game.GameType is Campaign` and call `AddBehavior(new MyCampaignBehavior())` / `AddModel` (precedents `SandBoxSubModule.InitializeGameStarter`, `StoryModeSubModule.InitializeGameStarter` → `AddBehaviors(campaignGameStarter)`). It runs *after* `SandBoxManager.Initialize`, so a mod's behaviors are appended to vanilla's list, and the finished list is handed to `CampaignBehaviorManager` later in the same method (behavior semantics in Q8).
8. Same method, in order: scene setup → **`OnGameStart(Game, IGameStarter)`** → `SetBasicModels` → **`BeginGameStart(Game)`** → **`OnCampaignStart(Game, object starter)`** → `SandBoxManager.OnCampaignStart` fans out **`RegisterSubModuleObjects(bool isSavedCampaign)`** then **`AfterRegisterSubModuleObjects(bool isSavedCampaign)`**; then the branch: new campaign → `CampaignBehaviorManager` created + **`OnAfterCampaignStart(Game)`**; saved campaign → **`OnGameLoaded(Game, object)`** then `InitializeCampaignBehaviors`/`LoadBehaviorData`/`RegisterEvents` → **`OnGameInitializationFinished(Game)`**; both paths end with **`OnAfterGameInitializationFinished(Game, object)`**. **`OnNewGameCreated(Game, object)`**, **`OnAfterGameLoaded(Game)`** and `InitializeSubModuleGameObjects(Game)` (from `Game.InitializeDefaultGameObjects`) fire in the same bootstrap window.
9. Steady state: native `CoreManaged.OnApplicationTick` → **`OnApplicationTick(float dt)`**; mission-scoped **`OnBeforeMissionBehaviorInitialize(Mission)`** then **`OnMissionBehaviorInitialize(Mission)`**; **`OnConfigChanged()`** on `EngineController.ConfigChange`; `OnNetworkTick(float)` for networked games; `AfterAsyncTickTick(float)` from `Mission`.
10. End of game: `MBGameManager.OnGameEnd` → **`OnGameEnd(Game)`** per sub-module, then `Module.OnGameEnd()` re-activates what step 5 disabled. **`OnSubModuleUnloaded()`** runs only at shutdown (`CoreManaged.Finalize` → `Module.FinalizeCurrentModule` → `FinalizeSubModulesBases`).
Practical split for this mod: Harmony patching and reflection setup in `OnSubModuleLoad` (no `Game` exists yet), campaign behaviors in `InitializeGameStarter`, per-session state in `OnGameStart`/`OnGameEnd`.

**(d) Where the DLL sits and how the class is found.** `SubModuleInfo.LoadFrom` computes the probe path as `Path.Combine(moduleFolderPath, "bin\\Win64_Shipping_Client", DLLName)` and sets `DLLPath`/`DLLExists` from `File.Exists` (a miss only logs `Couldn't find .dll: …`). The actual load in `Module.LoadSubModules` uses `Path.Combine(module.FolderPath, "bin", Common.ConfigName)` where `Common.ConfigName` is the **name of the current working directory** — `Win64_Shipping_Client` when the game runs from its own `bin/Win64_Shipping_Client`, which is why the two spellings agree (Q15: `BasePath.Name` is the relative `"../../"` seen from there); the fallback `ManagedDllFolder.Name + DLLName` is console-only (`ManagedDllFolder.Name` is `""` on PC). So: `Modules/<folder>/bin/Win64_Shipping_Client/<DLLName>`, and every `Assemblies` entry must sit in the *same* folder. The class is then located inside that assembly — never in an `Assemblies` DLL — by `Module.AddSubModule`: `subModuleAssembly.GetType(<SubModuleClassType>).GetConstructor(BindingFlags.Instance | Public | NonPublic | CreateInstance, null, new Type[0], null)` then `(MBSubModuleBase)constructor.Invoke(new object[0])`, i.e. the type must be **in the `DLLName` assembly**, must derive from `MBSubModuleBase`, and must have a **parameterless constructor** (private is acceptable, `NonPublic` is included). A wrong `SubModuleClassType` therefore yields a `NullReferenceException` that `Module.Initialize` does not catch. Failure modes: missing DLL → modal *"Cannot find: <path>"*, the game continues and the module's hooks are simply never called; `AssemblyLoader` `CriticalError` → box (community modules only) then an unconditional `throw new Exception()`; `LoadedWithErrors` (dependency conflict) → box for community modules, execution continues.

**Orchestrator verification.** Checked against the live 1.4.8 files in `~/bannerlord/moduledata_win`: ids `Native`, `SandBoxCore`, `Sandbox` (folder `SandBox`, lowercase b), `NavalDLC`; `Bannerlord.Harmony` (v2.4.2.248, `Bannerlord.Harmony.dll`, class `Bannerlord.Harmony.SubModule`) lists Native, SandBoxCore, Sandbox, StoryMode, CustomBattle under `ModulesToLoadAfterThis`; `SandBoxSubModule.InitializeGameStarter` adds behaviors via `CampaignGameStarter.AddBehavior`. Mod SubModule.xml: `DependedModules` = Native, SandBoxCore, Sandbox, Bannerlord.Harmony; no StoryMode dependency (the mod must work in sandbox; StoryMode is optional). Harmony patches in `OnSubModuleLoad`, behavior in `InitializeGameStarter`, template XML in `AfterRegisterSubModuleObjects` (Q11).

## Q17 — In-game notifications

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer
**API.** `InformationManager.DisplayMessage(InformationMessage)` (TaleWorlds.Library, static) only raises the static event
`DisplayMessageInternal`; it does nothing itself and never throws for a missing listener (`?.Invoke`). The message type has
`InformationMessage(string information, Color color)`; `Colors.Red` / `Colors.Yellow` are static `Color` fields of
TaleWorlds.Library. This is the vanilla way mods print a line in the bottom-left message log; no new dependency.

**Who shows it, and when it is safe.** The only singleplayer listener is the chat-log view model `MPChatVM`, which
subscribes in its constructor. It is created by `GauntletChatLogView` (Native's GauntletUI module), whose static
`Initialize` runs in `GauntletUISubModule.OnBeforeInitialModuleScreenSetAsRoot` — after every `OnSubModuleLoad`. A message
sent from `OnSubModuleLoad` (where companions are loaded and validated) is therefore lost: nobody listens yet. Messages must
be queued and sent once a campaign runs; the mod's behavior hooks `OnSessionLaunchedEvent` (new game and load, Q8) and
`OnGameLoadFinishedEvent` are both after UI initialization. `MPChatVM.OnDisplayMessageReceived` drops the message when
`IsChatAllowedByOptions()` is false (singleplayer: the player turned the chat box off, or a mission with battle UI hidden) —
the log file stays the authoritative record.

### Evidence
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.Library/TaleWorlds.Library/InformationManager.cs` — `InformationManager.DisplayMessage` — `public static void DisplayMessage(InformationMessage message)` invokes `DisplayMessageInternal?.Invoke(message)` only.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.Library/TaleWorlds.Library/InformationManager.cs` — `DisplayMessageInternal` — `public static event Action<InformationMessage> DisplayMessageInternal`.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.Library/TaleWorlds.Library/InformationMessage.cs` — `InformationMessage` — constructor `InformationMessage(string information, Color color)`.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.Library/TaleWorlds.Library/Colors.cs` — `Colors` — `public static readonly Color Red`, `Yellow`.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade.ViewModelCollection/TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade.ViewModelCollection.Multiplayer/MPChatVM.cs` — `MPChatVM` — constructor subscribes `InformationManager.DisplayMessageInternal += OnDisplayMessageReceived`, the only subscriber in the game DLLs.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade.ViewModelCollection/TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade.ViewModelCollection.Multiplayer/MPChatVM.cs` — `IsChatAllowedByOptions` — singleplayer: `BannerlordConfig.EnableSingleplayerChatBox`, and in a mission `!BannerlordConfig.HideBattleUI`.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade.GauntletUI/TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade.GauntletUI/GauntletChatLogView.cs` — `GauntletChatLogView` — `_dataSource = new MPChatVM()` in its constructor; static `Initialize`.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade.GauntletUI/TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade.GauntletUI/GauntletUISubModule.cs` — `OnBeforeInitialModuleScreenSetAsRoot` — calls `GauntletChatLogView.Initialize()` (after sub-module load).

### Uncertain
None. (ViewModelCollection and Native GauntletUI were decompiled with ilspycmd into `~/bannerlord/decomp` for this section.)

## Q18 — Vanilla wanderer/companion dialog points

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer

Every point below is registered through the API and matched by the selection rules described in Q7, in the
`OnSessionLaunched`/`OnNewGameCreated` hook of the behavior named above each table. `CompanionsCampaignBehavior` (Q1)
receives the `CampaignGameStarter` but registers **no** dialog line at all — it only spawns and culls wanderer
templates — and SandBox `CompanionDismissCampaignBehavior` has no dialog either, only encounter cleanup.

**The two population gates.** *Wanderer gate* = `conversation_wanderer_on_condition()`: `Hero.OneToOneConversationHero != null`
and `Occupation == Occupation.Wanderer` and `HeroState != Hero.CharacterStates.Prisoner`. *Hired-companion gate* =
`Hero.IsPlayerCompanion` (`CompanionOf == Clan.PlayerClan`), `Hero.OneToOneConversationHero.CompanionOf`, or
`Clan == Clan.PlayerClan`. Hiring does **not** move a hero out of the first gate: `AddCompanionAction.ApplyInternal`
only re-points `companion.CompanionOf` (firing a previous employer first) and never touches the occupation, and
`WandererTag.IsApplicableTo` is `character.HeroObject.IsWanderer` — so a hired companion keeps being a wanderer and
keeps picking up `WandererTag`-weighted variations.

Firing is permanent: `HeroSpawnCampaignBehavior.OnCompanionRemoved` teleports a removed companion back to a suitable
settlement only when he is not fugitive/dead and the detail is neither `ByTurningToLord` nor `Death`, while the Fire
detail makes the hero fugitive and resets his equipment — so the fired hero is then removed by
`KillCharacterAction.ApplyByRemove` and never comes back.

**Which points apply to whom.** *Not-yet-hired wanderers*: the whole meet chain (`start_wanderer_unmet` →
`wanderer_meet_player_response1/2` → the backstory chain → `wanderer_job_status_2` job offer), the generic-backstory
fallback once the same template has been met before, `wanderer_job_status_1_2` when he already serves an NPC clan, the
hire block of Table 3 (`conversation_hero_hire_on_condition` rejects anyone already in the player clan or in any
party), and the re-ask option `{=Ymgbv2gV}What's your story again?`. *Companions already in the player clan*: they are
still wanderers, so they keep `wanderer_job_status_1` ("orders for your alley"), the `WandererTag`-weighted greetings
and the `hero_leave` variations, but their conversation is dominated by the `IsPlayerCompanion`/`CompanionOf`/
`Clan.PlayerClan`-gated points: roles and role re-assignment, NPC-initiated missions, the fire chain, enfeoffment,
rejoin after imprisonment, rescue and prison-break return, grievances, follow/gather orders, caravan business. Once
met, a wanderer never sees the meet chain again because `ConversationUseMeetingDialogs()` requires `!HasMet`, so he
gets `{SHORT_ABSENCE_GREETING}` (< 24 h) or `{VOICED_LINE}` from a `MetBeforeTag`-weighted `str_context_line`
variation instead.

**Excluded from the tables** (checked, and either not companion/wanderer dialog or out of scope):
`RecruitmentCampaignBehavior`, `WorkshopsCharactersCampaignBehavior`, `IssuesCampaignBehavior`
(`{=Zx5Nw…}I am thinking of a different companion.` is an issue-screen line), `PerkResetCampaignBehavior` (the arena
master retrains a `{COMPANION.NAME}`), StoryMode `TrainingFieldCampaignBehavior`, `LesserNobleRevoltIssueBehavior`,
`CaravanConversationsCampaignBehavior` (a magistrate asks the player to hand over a free companion:
`{=otVPaR6T}Actually I do not have a free companion right now.`), and every `NavalDLC` behavior — DLC assemblies are
off-limits per the project rules.

**Orchestrator note (verified; spot checks: `companion_fire_condition` needs `Settlement.CurrentSettlement == null`,
`HeroSpawnCampaignBehavior.OnCompanionRemoved` skips fugitives, `start_wanderer_unmet` priority 110, `CompanionRelationLimit = -10`).**
Consequence for mod companions: the relation break-up in Table 5 removes a hero through `KillCharacterAction.ApplyByRemove`
exactly like the dismissal; it is not a player dismissal, so the mod leaves it alone (SPEC_CORE_GAPS T4.2). How NPC texts
can be replaced per mod companion without touching conditions or tokens: `ConversationManager.UpdateCurrentSentenceText`
copies `_sentences[_currentSentence].Text` into `_currentSentenceText`, which is what both the display
(`CurrentSentenceText`, via `FindMatchingTextOrNull(text.GetID(), …)` → null for an unknown id → the text itself) and the
voice lookup (`ProcessSentence` → `TryGetVoiceObject(_currentSentenceText)`) read; a postfix there can swap the text of a
vanilla NPC sentence (`ConversationSentence.Id`, `IsPlayer == false`) after the vanilla condition already set its variables.

## Q19 — Companion dismissal

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer
**(a) What dismissal does.** The player dismisses a companion only through the conversation option
`companion_talk_fire` ("I no longer have need of your services.", token `companion_role` → `companion_fire`), whose
consequence `CompanionRolesCampaignBehavior.companion_fire_on_consequence` calls, in order:
1. `RemoveCompanionAction.ApplyByFire(hero.CompanionOf, hero)` → `ApplyInternal(..., Fire)`: `CompanionOf = null`; the hero
   leaves its mobile party (a led party is held and disbanded/destroyed); for `Fire` a prisoner escapes
   (`EndCaptivityAction.ApplyByEscape`), otherwise `MakeHeroFugitiveAction.Apply` (leaves party and settlement,
   `ChangeState(Fugitive)`); a wanderer's equipment is reset to its template; a governor post is removed; finally
   `CampaignEvents.CompanionRemoved(hero, Fire)` fires.
2. `KillCharacterAction.ApplyByRemove(hero)` — detail `Lost`, forced: **the hero is removed from the game**. That is why
   a dismissed mod companion vanished from the map. Vanilla never brings a dismissed companion back.
3. `PlayerEncounter.LeaveEncounter = true` when an encounter is open.

**(b) Telling player dismissal apart.** `RemoveCompanionDetail` has `Fire`, `Death`, `AfterQuest`, `ByTurningToLord`;
death, quests and becoming a lord use their own `Apply…` methods. `ApplyByFire` has exactly three callers: the dialog
consequence above, `AddCompanionAction.Apply` (a companion that already belongs to another clan is "fired" from it just
before joining the new one — not a player dismissal) and a cheat. So the `CompanionRemoved` event with `Fire` is ambiguous,
but the dialog consequence is not: a Harmony prefix on `companion_fire_on_consequence` sees player dismissals only.
Captivity, release and kingdom events do not go through `RemoveCompanionAction` at all.

**(c) Back to an unhired wanderer.** Vanilla spawns a wanderer with `HeroCreator.CreateSpecialHero`, then
`hero.ChangeState(Hero.CharacterStates.Active)` and `EnterSettlementAction.ApplyForCharacterOnly(hero, settlement)`
(Q3: the only writer of `StayingInSettlement`), in `CompanionsCampaignBehavior.CreateCompanionAndAddToSettlement`. After
`ApplyByFire` a mod hero is a partyless fugitive with `CompanionOf == null` and still `Occupation.Wanderer`; skipping step 2
and repeating the vanilla spawn steps makes it an unhired wanderer in a tavern again (our hire option checks
`!IsPlayerCompanion && PartyBelongedTo == null`). The mod's prefix does exactly that for mod heroes only and returns
`false` (original skipped); every other hero runs vanilla code.

**Interaction with the M8 guards (SPEC_VANILLA_GUARDS V5, checked).** Player dismissal of a mod companion runs only the
T4 prefix on `companion_fire_on_consequence`: `RemoveCompanionAction.ApplyByFire` (clan/party removal, fugitive, equipment
reset, `CompanionRemoved` event) and the mod's tavern placement. It changes no relation, so the V1 guard on
`OnHeroRelationChanged` is not involved; it calls no grievance member (V2); and it never reaches
`KillCharacterAction.ApplyByRemove`, whose V3 guard is active only inside `PerkResetCampaignBehavior.RemoveACompanionFromPlayerParty`.
The `CompanionRemoved` listeners stay vanilla: the "left your clan" toast (Q34: keep) and `PlayerTrackCompanionBehavior.CompanionRemoved`,
which only drops the hero from its scattered-companions list. A grievance row the
dismissed hero may still carry is dropped by the V2 hourly prefix. Conversely, none of the guards calls into the dismissal
path. Result: dismissal → tavern → rehire is unchanged.

### Evidence
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors/CompanionRolesCampaignBehavior.cs` — `companion_fire_on_consequence` — `ApplyByFire`, then `KillCharacterAction.ApplyByRemove`, then `PlayerEncounter.LeaveEncounter = true`.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors/CompanionRolesCampaignBehavior.cs` — `companion_talk_fire` — player line `companion_role` → `companion_fire`, "{=pRsCnGoo}I no longer have need of your services.".
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.Actions/RemoveCompanionAction.cs` — `RemoveCompanionAction.ApplyInternal` — CompanionOf = null, leaves party, Fire → escape or fugitive, wanderer ResetEquipments, governor removed, `OnCompanionRemoved(companion, detail)`.

## Q20 — Authored conversations (entry points, return tokens, effects, persistence)

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer
Self-verified for M6 (companion conversations in dialogs.json). Builds on Q7 (token graph, priority, selection) and Q18.

**Entry from the menu.** Player options of the companion's conversation menu are player lines on `hero_main_options`
(Q7/Q18: the hub used by wanderers and hired companions alike). Every passing player line there is listed and priority only
orders the list, so a conversation's start option is added with priority 105: above the vanilla 100 options (hire,
roles), below story quests (125+). **Entry as a greeting.** Every conversation begins at token `start` and only the first
passing NPC line fires (Q7). Vanilla greetings are 100 (`start_default`) and 110 (`start_wanderer_unmet`); the mod's intro
is 120 and needs a companion not met yet. A greeting conversation is registered at 119 and always needs a met
companion, so it beats the vanilla greetings and never competes with the intro. Story-quest lines at higher priority still win.

**Returning and ending.** `hero_pretalk_2` (`lord_pretalk` → `hero_main_options`, no condition, "Is there anything
else?") is how vanilla returns to the menu after a player line, so a player node with next "hub" outputs `lord_pretalk`
and the companion speaks before the menu reappears. An NPC node with next "hub" outputs `hero_main_options` directly (like
the mod's `hire_decline`). Next "end" outputs `close_window`, which ends the conversation after an NPC or a player line (Q7).
NPC → NPC chains are vanilla practice (`wanderer_introduction_a` → `_b` → `_c`). Equal-priority NPC lines keep
registration order, so the first listed alternative whose condition holds is said.

**Effects.** `ChangeRelationAction.ApplyPlayerRelation(hero, change)`: the game clamps the result to −100..100, and a
positive change is first scaled by `DiplomacyModel.GetRelationIncreaseFactor` and randomly rounded, so the shown gain can
differ from the authored number. The condition side reads `Hero.GetRelationWithPlayer()` (a float of the integer relation).
Gold: `GiveGoldAction.ApplyBetweenCharacters(giver, recipient, amount)` caps the amount at the giver's gold, and a null
giver creates the gold, so "the player receives" uses giver null and "the player pays" uses the main hero as giver after
a gold check. Joining uses the hire actions of Q6 (`AddCompanionAction.Apply`, `AddHeroToPartyAction.Apply`) without payment.

**Persistence.** Flags and "once" markers are a `List<string>` field synced in the mod behavior's `SyncData` (Q8). `List<string>`
is registered by `SaveableBasicTypeDefiner`, so no `SaveableTypeDefiner` of our own is needed. A save without the key leaves
the field untouched (Q9), so it starts empty.

### Evidence
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors/LordConversationsCampaignBehavior.cs` — `hero_pretalk_2` — `lord_pretalk` → `hero_main_options`, "{=DQBaaC0e}Is there anything else?", no condition.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.Conversation/ConversationManager.cs` — `ConversationManager.SortLastSentence` — equal priority keeps registration order.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.Conversation/ConversationManager.cs` — `ConversationManager.ProcessPartnerSentence` — first passing NPC line wins.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.Actions/ChangeRelationAction.cs` — `ChangeRelationAction.ApplyPlayerRelation` — `ApplyInternal`: positive change scaled by `GetRelationIncreaseFactor`, result clamped to −100..100.

## Behavior system (SPEC_BEHAVIOR_FOUNDATION Track R)

Q21–Q31 answer the research questions R1–R11. Nothing here is used in mod code until it has an API index row.

## Q21 — Hero-to-hero relations

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer

Cross-references instead of repetition: Q2 (wanderers, `Occupation`), Q6/Q19 (hire/fire, `AddCompanionAction`, `RemoveCompanionAction`, `KillCharacterAction.ApplyByRemove`), Q17 (quick notifications), Q18 (break-up on relation, the −10 companion threshold), Q20 (`ApplyPlayerRelation` in authored conversations), Q8/Q9 (behavior `SyncData`, where saves live). SPEC_BEHAVIOR_FOUNDATION §0 puts companion↔companion relation, morale and leaving out of implementation scope — the rest of this section is research only.

**Yes — arbitrary pairs, one undirected value.** Vanilla tracks one `int` per *unordered pair of any two heroes*, not only player↔hero. One `CharacterRelationManager` per campaign (`Campaign.CharacterRelationManager`, created in the `Campaign` constructor) holds a nested `internal class HeroRelations` whose only state is a `Dictionary<long, Dictionary<long, int>>`: outer key = `hero1.Id.GetHashCode()`, inner key = `hero2.Id.GetHashCode()`, value = the relation. The private `GetHashCodes` canonicalises the pair (`if (hero1.Id > hero2.Id)`), so there is exactly one row per unordered pair and the relation is **symmetric in storage** — writing for (a, b) is also what b reads. A pair with no row reads as 0, and writing 0 *deletes* the row (and prunes the outer key when it becomes empty), so "0" and "never related" are indistinguishable. The store itself places no restriction on which heroes may be keyed.

**Two different numbers: stored and effective.** `Hero.GetRelation(otherHero)` is *not* the row; it returns `DiplomacyModel.GetEffectiveRelation`, which (1) maps both heroes through `GetHeroesForEffectiveRelation` — `hero.Clan != null ? hero.Clan.Leader : hero` — falling back to the original two heroes when both map to the same leader or when one is `IsPlayerCompanion` and the other `IsHumanPlayerCharacter`; (2) applies `GetPersonalityEffects`, ±2/±1/±1 for Honor/Valor/Mercy when the product of the two trait levels is positive/negative; (3) clamps the result to the model limits. Consequences: player↔hired-companion works only because `Hero.Clan` returns `CompanionOf ?? _clan`, i.e. the companion's leader is the main hero and the pair would otherwise collapse to (MainHero, MainHero) — that is exactly what the fallback exists for; two companions of the player clan collapse to the *same* leader and therefore fall back to the heroes themselves, so companion↔companion keeps its own row; an unhired wanderer has `Clan == null` (wanderer templates carry no clan and `DefaultHeroCreationModel.GetClan` returns null for a parentless hero), so it stands for itself and can be related to anyone; but a companion paired with anyone *outside* the player clan is redirected to (MainHero, that hero's clan leader), so vanilla never keeps a per-companion opinion of a lord — every such row is the player's own number, shared by all companions of the clan (`Clan.PlayerClan.Leader` is the main hero, from `owner="Hero.main_hero"` on `player_faction`). Because the personality term is computed from the *calling* hero against the effective counterpart, `a.GetRelation(b)` can differ from `b.GetRelation(a)` although the row is shared; `GetBaseHeroRelation` cannot differ. `Hero.IsEnemy`, `IsFriend` and `IsNeutral(Hero)` skip the effective path entirely and compare the *raw* row to −50/+50.

**Read API (all public).** `public static int CharacterRelationManager.GetHeroRelation(Hero hero1, Hero hero2)` (raw row, 0 when unset); `public int Hero.GetRelation(Hero otherHero)` (effective; 0 when the argument is the hero itself); `public int Hero.GetBaseHeroRelation(Hero otherHero)` (raw); `public float Hero.GetRelationWithPlayer()` = `MainHero.GetRelation(this)` (Q20); `public float Hero.GetUnmodifiedClanLeaderRelationshipWithPlayer()` (raw player row); `public bool Hero.IsEnemy(Hero otherHero)` / `IsFriend(Hero otherHero)` / `IsNeutral(Hero otherHero)`. Model layer: `public abstract int DiplomacyModel.GetBaseRelation(Hero hero, Hero hero1)`, `public abstract int GetEffectiveRelation(Hero hero, Hero hero1)`, `public abstract void GetHeroesForEffectiveRelation(Hero hero1, Hero hero2, out Hero effectiveHero1, out Hero effectiveHero2)`.

**Write API.** `public void Hero.SetPersonalRelation(Hero otherHero, int value)` — clamps to `DiplomacyModel.MinRelationLimit..MaxRelationLimit` and writes the row directly: **no event, no notification, no side effect whatsoever**; vanilla only uses it for new-game seeding, notable logic, clan-leader inheritance and tutorial quests. `public static void CharacterRelationManager.SetHeroRelation(Hero hero1, Hero hero2, int value)` — public, **unclamped** (a caller can store a value outside the model range; it stays visible to `GetBaseRelation` and to `IsEnemy`/`IsFriend`), and a write where both arguments are the same hero is skipped with a `Debug.FailedAssert`. The only paths that fire events are on `ChangeRelationAction`: `public static void ApplyPlayerRelation(Hero gainedRelationWith, int relation, bool affectRelatives = true, bool showQuickNotification = true)` (Q20 — `affectRelatives` is *unused* in 1.4.8), `public static void ApplyRelationChangeBetweenHeroes(Hero hero, Hero gainedRelationWith, int relationChange, bool showQuickNotification = true)` for two arbitrary heroes, `public static void ApplyEmissaryRelation(Hero emissary, Hero gainedRelationWith, int relationChange, bool showQuickNotification = true)`, with `public enum ChangeRelationDetail { Default, Emissary }` carried through the event.

**Value range, scaling, clamping.** Stored values are `int`. Private `ApplyInternal` (a) rescales a *positive* change with `DiplomacyModel.GetRelationIncreaseFactor(Hero, Hero, float)` — charm skill bonus plus charm perks of one hero of the pair, and when neither hero is the human player that hero is picked with `MBRandom.RandomFloat < 0.5f`, so AI↔AI gains are not reproducible — then `MBRandom.RoundRandomized`; (b) resolves the effective pair; (c) writes `stored + change` clamped by `MBMath.ClampInt(value, -100, 100)` with literals, not the model limits; (d) skips everything when the change is 0. The model limits are `MaxRelationLimit => 100` / `MinRelationLimit => -100`, applied again inside `GetEffectiveRelation`; `MaxNeutralRelationLimit => 50` / `MinNeutralRelationLimit => -50` define the friend/enemy band; the two hard −10 thresholds that matter here are `CompanionRolesCampaignBehavior.CompanionRelationLimit = -10` (companion leaves, Q18) and `MinimumRelationWithConversationCharacterToJoinKingdom => -10` (mercenary/vassal offer gate).

**Who actually has non-zero rows.** New game: `CharacterRelationCampaignBehavior.UpdateFriendshipAndEnemies` iterates pairs of `Hero.IsLord` heroes only (never MainHero), with a distance-weighted chance per pair, magnitude ~`RandomFloat * 2 - 1` scaled by 30 and clamped to ±100, sign shaped by `HeroHelper.NPCPersonalityClashWithNPC(Hero, Hero)`, and same-culture kingdom leaders forced to −35..−100. Notables get rows through `NotablesCampaignBehavior` (successor notables inherit the dead notable's rows with `Math.Abs(relation) >= 20`). Nothing seeds companions or wanderers: `AddCompanionAction.ApplyInternal` only sets `companion.CompanionOf = clan` and fires `OnNewCompanionAdded` (Q6), and the wanderer hire check (Q2/Q20) does not look at relation. So every wanderer/companion row starts at 0 and stays 0 until a conversation, a mod or the pair-marriage path writes it — and the store accepts any pair.

**Side effects of a change.** Only the `ChangeRelationAction` path fires `CampaignEvents.HeroRelationChanged`, an `IMbEvent<Hero, Hero, int, bool, ChangeRelationAction.ChangeRelationDetail, Hero, Hero>` whose arguments are (effectiveHero, effectiveHeroGainedRelationWith, relationChange, showNotification, detail, originalHero, originalGainedRelationWith) — note listeners see *effective* heroes first and the original pair only last. Five vanilla listeners: (1) `CompanionRolesCampaignBehavior.OnHeroRelationChanged` — the leaving check: the effective pair must be MainHero ↔ a player companion, `relationChange < 0`, and the resulting `GetRelation` < −10 → `KillCharacterAction.ApplyByRemove` (Q18/Q19), which routes a companion through `RemoveCompanionAction.ApplyByDeath`, i.e. `RemoveCompanionDetail.Death`, so the "left your clan" toast (shown for `RemoveCompanionDetail.Fire`) never appears; because the trigger needs `relationChange < 0`, a plain `SetPersonalRelation` to −50 does *not* make anyone leave. (2) `CharacterRelationCampaignBehavior.OnHeroRelationChanged` → `SkillLevelingManager.OnGainRelation(originalHero, effectiveHeroGainedRelationWith, relationChange, detail)`; `DefaultSkillLevelingManager.OnGainRelation` gives the *actor* Charm XP (party XP if they lead a party, otherwise personal) only when `relationChange > 0` and they are with a party or the detail is `Emissary`, and the amount is `DiplomacyModel.GetCharmExperienceFromRelationGain` = base 20 × relationChange scaled ×10/×20/×30 by the *target's* standing (notable / faction leader / clan leader) — this runs for AI↔AI changes too. (3) SandBox `DefaultNotificationsCampaignBehavior.OnRelationChanged` — quick information only when `showNotification` and MainHero is one of the two *effective* heroes (Q17), so a companion↔companion change is silent. (4) `MarriageOfferCampaignBehavior.OnHeroRelationChanged` — an in-flight NPC marriage proposal is cancelled when the change breaks `MarriageModel.ShouldNpcMarriageBetweenClansBeAllowed`. (5) `VassalAndMercenaryOfferCampaignBehavior.OnHeroRelationChanged` — an in-flight mercenary/vassal offer to the player is cancelled when MainHero is in the effective pair and the offer conditions no longer hold. Vanilla writers on that path include marriage itself (`OnHeroesMarried` → `ApplyRelationChangeBetweenHeroes(firstHero, secondHero, 30, showQuickNotification: false)`), a clan leaving a kingdom (−20, or −40 for a rebellion, toward every former co-league leader), a new clan leader inheriting the dead leader's rows at ×0.7 (`GetRelationChangeAfterClanLeaderIsDead` + `ChangeClanLeaderAction`), executions (`ApplyPlayerRelation` on the victim's clan leader), marriage/barter/siege/claim actions, and cheats.
Nothing is recomputed when the value is read: consumers re-read it when they run. Daily clan influence drift uses `DefaultClanPoliticsModel.CalculateRelationshipChangeWithSponsor` (`MathF.Lerp(-2f, 2f, clamp(relation / 60f))` between *clan leaders*); kingdom decision support weights, alliance scoring (`DefaultAllianceModel.GetRelationshipEffect`) and trade-agreement scoring (`DefaultTradeAgreementModel.GetRelationEffectBetweenRulers`) all use ruler/leader pairs; lord defection weights persuasion arguments on `IsEnemy`/`IsFriend` (raw rows); executions consult `DefaultExecutionRelationModel` (`victim.IsFriend(hero)`); the mercenary offer gate is `offerKingdom.Leader.GetRelationWithPlayer() >= -10` in `FactionHelper`. Every one of those is a lord↔lord pair because of the leader substitution — so per-companion rows have **no vanilla AI consumer at all**: they only mean something to code that reads them explicitly.

**Persistence.** The relation map is part of the campaign save graph, not a separate file: `[SaveableField(1)] private readonly HeroRelations _heroRelations` and, inside the nested class, `[SaveableField(1)] private Dictionary<long, Dictionary<long, int>> _relations`, with `AddClassDefinition(typeof(CharacterRelationManager), 31)` and `AddClassDefinition(typeof(CharacterRelationManager.HeroRelations), 186)` in `SaveableCampaignTypeDefiner`, and the manager added to the collected object graph by `Campaign.AutoGeneratedInstanceCollectObjects` (save location: Q9). Behavior-side sync is empty — `CharacterRelationCampaignBehavior.SyncData` writes nothing (Q8), so there is no mod-visible per-behavior state for relations. Cleanup: `Campaign.OnGameLoaded` calls `CharacterRelationManager.AfterLoad()`, which prunes keys missing from `CampaignObjectManager.AliveHeroes` **only** for saves whose `MBSaveLoad.LastLoadedGameVersion < ApplicationVersion.FromString("v1.1.0")`; `CampaignEvents.OnHeroUnregisteredEvent` → `CharacterRelationCampaignBehavior.OnHeroUnregistered` → `RemoveHero(Hero)`, which deletes the hero's outer key and its occurrences in every inner map (so a dead/dismissed hero's rows vanish, Q19). Keys are id hashes (`MBGUID.GetHashCode` returns the guid's `_internalValue`), and runtime-created heroes get `Id = new MBGUID(32u, nextSubId)` in `CampaignObjectManager.AddHero` while `InitializeOnLoad` re-seeds the per-type counter from the max loaded sub-id, so rows keyed by a saved hero's id survive a save/load cycle.

**Mod guard (SPEC_VANILLA_GUARDS V1).** The only vanilla code that removes a companion because of its relation is the
private `CompanionRolesCampaignBehavior.OnHeroRelationChanged(Hero effectiveHero, Hero effectiveHeroGainedRelationWith,
int relationChange, bool showNotification, ChangeRelationAction.ChangeRelationDetail detail, Hero originalHero, Hero
originalGainedRelationWith)`, a `HeroRelationChanged` listener whose whole body is the removal check (main hero ↔ player
companion, `relationChange < 0`, `GetRelation < CompanionRelationLimit` (−10) → `KillCharacterAction.ApplyByRemove`). The mod
prefixes this method and skips it when either hero of the pair is a mod companion; the relation was already written by
`ChangeRelationAction` before the event, so it is unaffected. `KillCharacterAction` is not patched: it also serves deaths,
executions and other removals, which stay vanilla.

**Raw companion ↔ companion relation (SPEC_VANILLA_GUARDS V4).** The mod reads with **one** API:
`public static int CharacterRelationManager.GetHeroRelation(Hero hero1, Hero hero2)` — the stored row itself (0 when unset).
Reason: `Hero.GetBaseHeroRelation` returns the same number today but goes through the replaceable
`DiplomacyModel.GetBaseRelation` (the default model's private `GetBaseRelationBetweenHeroes` just calls `GetHeroRelation`),
so another mod's diplomacy model could change it; `Hero.GetRelation` is the *effective* value. For two companions of the
player clan `GetHeroesForEffectiveRelation` maps both to the clan leader (the main hero), sees the same hero and falls back to
the two companions themselves, so `GetRelation` = stored row **plus** `GetPersonalityEffects` (Honor/Valor/Mercy ±1/±2),
clamped — not the personal value, and possibly different in each direction. Writes use `public void
Hero.SetPersonalRelation(Hero otherHero, int value)`: it clamps to `DiplomacyModel.MinRelationLimit..MaxRelationLimit` and
calls `CharacterRelationManager.SetHeroRelation`, which writes the row (`HeroRelations.SetRelation`) and **fires no event**:
no `HeroRelationChanged`, no notification, no Charm XP, no vanilla removal check (verified: neither method dispatches
anything). Only `ChangeRelationAction` fires the event.

- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.Election/KingdomDecision.cs` — `KingdomDecision` — support weight derived from `clan.Leader.GetRelation(decisionOutcome.SponsorClan.Leader)` and `GetRelation(ProposerClan.Leader)`.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.GameComponents/DefaultAllianceModel.cs` — `DefaultAllianceModel.GetRelationshipEffect` — alliance score from `querierKingdom.Leader.GetRelation(queriedKingdom.Leader)`.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.GameComponents/DefaultTradeAgreementModel.cs` — `DefaultTradeAgreementModel.GetRelationEffectBetweenRulers` — trade-agreement score = ruler relation × 0.1.

- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/SaveableCampaignTypeDefiner.cs` — `AddClassDefinition` — registers the manager as id 31 and `CharacterRelationManager.HeroRelations` as id 186.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/Campaign.cs` — `AutoGeneratedInstanceCollectObjects` — adds `CharacterRelationManager` to the saved campaign object graph; the accessor is `Campaign.CharacterRelationManager`.

### Uncertain

- **UNCERTAIN**: whether rows keyed by an *XML-defined* hero's id survive a mod that adds or reorders injected heroes of the same object type. `MBObjectManager.GetNewId` hands out `new MBGUID(_typeNo, ++_objCount)` in module load order, so sub-ids of base-game heroes can shift between sessions and orphan saved rows. Resolve by saving before adding a mod hero, reloading, and comparing `Hero.GetBaseHeroRelation` for a lord pair before/after.
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether Charm XP from `OnGainRelation` is ever awarded for a pure AI↔AI relation gain in practice — the code path allows it (`relationChange > 0` and an actor with a party), but no vanilla call site with a party-leading AI actor was isolated. Resolve by listing `ApplyRelationChangeBetweenHeroes` callers whose first hero leads a party (`BarterManager`, `SiegeEvent`, `Clan`, `KingdomManager`).
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether the DLC assemblies add further `HeroRelationChanged` listeners or companion-relation rules; this section deliberately cites only non-DLC decompilates. Resolve by auditing the DLC CampaignBehaviors assemblies if they are ever needed.

## Q22 — Morale

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer

**Cross-references instead of repetition:** Q16 (`InitializeGameStarter` → `AddModel` / `AddBehavior` — how every model and behavior cited here is installed), Q12 (`BaseModel` delegation when overriding a game model), Q14 (`TextObject` / `GameTexts`, `{=id}` keys — every tooltip label below is a text id), Q17 (quick notifications), Q18 + Q21 (companion grievances and hero↔hero relation — the hero-level dissatisfaction systems, which are *not* morale), Q8/Q9 (`CampaignBehaviorBase.SyncData` for save-safe mod state), Q29 (party inventory / `ItemRoster`, food).

**A. Morale is party-level; there is no per-hero satisfaction or mood in vanilla.** The whole morale system is one float per `MobileParty`. The saved state is a single field, `_moraleDueToEvents` (`[SaveableField(1200)]`), exposed only through the public property `public float RecentEventsMorale { get; set; }`, whose setter clamps to ±100. The number the player sees is *not* stored: `public float Morale { get; }` recomputes `Campaign.Current.Models.PartyMoraleModel.GetEffectivePartyMorale(this).ResultNumber` on every read and clamps the result to 0…100, and `public ExplainedNumber MoraleExplained` is the same call with `includeDescription: true`. `PartyBase` has no morale member at all (grep for `Morale` in `PartyBase.cs` → zero hits, despite the task hint), and `Hero.cs` has no `Morale`, `Mood` or `Satisfaction` member (zero hits; `grep -rn "Satisfaction" decomp/` → zero hits game-wide). What vanilla offers at hero level instead: relation via `Hero.GetRelationWithPlayer()` (Q21), grievance *flags* in `CompanionGrievanceBehavior` whose internal `GrievanceType { Invalid, NoWage, Starvation, VillageRaided, DesertedBattle }` only changes Relation — it never writes morale (it *reads* `MobileParty.MainParty.HasUnpaidWages` and `PartyBase.MainParty.IsStarving` as triggers), and the closest "feels bad" numeric model in the game belongs to a settlement, not a hero: `Town.Loyalty` with `SettlementLoyaltyModel` / `DefaultSettlementLoyaltyModel`. A hero influences party morale only indirectly, as the party's leader (Leadership skill) or as a role-holder whose perk counts (see C). Battle-layer morale (`CommonAIComponent.Morale`, 0…100 per agent, `MoraleThresholdForPanicking = 0.01f`) is a separate Mount&Blade system reached through `BattleMoraleModel`, not a per-hero party stat.

**B. The model: `PartyMoraleModel` → `DefaultPartyMoraleModel`.** The game-model interface is `public abstract class PartyMoraleModel : MBGameModel<PartyMoraleModel>` with exactly seven members: `public abstract float HighMoraleValue { get; }`, `public abstract int GetDailyStarvationMoralePenalty(PartyBase party);`, `public abstract int GetDailyNoWageMoralePenalty(MobileParty party);`, `public abstract float GetStandardBaseMorale(PartyBase party);`, `public abstract float GetVictoryMoraleChange(PartyBase party);`, `public abstract float GetDefeatMoraleChange(PartyBase party);`, `public abstract ExplainedNumber GetEffectivePartyMorale(MobileParty party, bool includeDescription = false);`. It is reached as `Campaign.Current.Models.PartyMoraleModel` (resolved in `GameModels` via `GetGameModel<PartyMoraleModel>()`) and registered by vanilla inside `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.SandBoxManager.Initialize(CampaignGameStarter gameStarter)` as `gameStarter.AddModel(new DefaultPartyMoraleModel());` — the *non-generic* overload, so vanilla's own model has no `BaseModel` (see Q16 for where a mod's `AddModel` call lands relative to this one). Note two members are vestigial in 1.4.8: `GetStandardBaseMorale` (returns 50) and `GetVictoryMoraleChange` (returns 20) have **no call site anywhere** in the decompiled non-DLC sources — the default implementation hardcodes `new ExplainedNumber(50f, includeDescription)` instead of calling the first, and victory morale is actually computed by `BattleRewardModel.CalculateMoraleGainVictory`. `GetDefeatMoraleChange` *is* used (`MapEvent.ApplyMoraleAndBehaviorUpdatesOfDefeatedParties`). There is also a dead legacy `public abstract class MobilePartyMoraleModel : MBGameModel<MobilePartyMoraleModel>` (`CalculateMoraleChange(MobileParty party)`, `GetMoraleTooltipText(MobileParty party)`) that is never registered, never referenced and has no `GameModels` property — do not subclass it.

**C. Factor table, in the order `DefaultPartyMoraleModel.GetEffectivePartyMorale(MobileParty mobileParty, bool includeDescription = false)` applies them.** Nothing in the model clamps; the 0…100 clamp lives in the `MobileParty.Morale` getter, and there is no clamp on the `ExplainedNumber` (so `MoraleExplained.ResultNumber` can leave 0…100 while `Morale` cannot).

| # | factor | vanilla magnitude | tooltip line label |
|---|---|---|---|
| base | `new ExplainedNumber(50f, includeDescription)` | +50, hardcoded (not `GetStandardBaseMorale`) | built-in `Base` |
| 1 | `mobileParty.RecentEventsMorale` | the saved float, clamped ±100 at write time | `str_recent_events` ("Recent Events") |
| 2 | Leadership skill of the party's effective leader (`SkillHelper.GetEffectivePartyLeaderForSkill` → `DefaultSkillEffects.LeadershipMoraleBonus`) | `+0.1 × LeadershipLevel` (`SkillEffect.GetSkillEffectValue` = `BaseValue + Bonus * skillLevel`), `PartyRole.Personal` only — an army commander's Lead does **not** help attached parties | `GameTexts.FindText("role", role)` — a *role* name, not "Leadership" |
| 3 | starvation | −30 (`GetStarvationMoralePenalty`); militia checks `HomeSettlement.IsStarving`, garrisons `SettlementHelper.IsGarrisonStarving`, otherwise `mobileParty.Party.IsStarving` | `str_starvation_morale` |
| 4 | unpaid wages | `mobileParty.HasUnpaidWages * (−20)` when `HasUnpaidWages > 0f` (fraction 0…1, `[SaveableField(1006)]`) | `str_no_wage_morale` |
| 5 | perks (`GetMoraleEffectsFromPerks`, resolved through `MobileParty.HasPerk(PerkObject, bool checkSecondaryRole = false)` which dispatches on the perk's party role — quartermaster, surgeon, party leader, …) | `Crossbow.PeasantLeader` `AddFactor(0.1 × share-of-troops-tier-≤3)`; `Charm.SelfPromoter` +1 (`SecondaryBonus`) while `party.CurrentSettlement?.SiegeEvent != null`; `Steward.Logistician` +4 when `Party.NumberOfMounts > foot soldiers` and the party is not at sea | the perk's own `Name` |
| 6 | food variety (`CalculateFoodVarietyMoraleBonus`, input `party.ItemRoster.FoodVariety` = number of distinct food types; skipped entirely while `party.Party.IsStarving`) | 0/1 → −2, 2 → −1, 3 → 0, 4 → +1, 5 → +2, 6 → +3, 7 → +5, 8 → +6, 9 → +7, 10 → +8, 11 → +9, ≥12 → +10; `Steward.WarriorsDiet` on the leader hero zeroes a negative (not at sea); `Steward.Gourmet` adds the same positive again (halved at sea) | `str_food_bonus_morale` + perk name |
| 7 | over-cap (`GetPartySizeMoraleEffect`, skipped for `IsMilitia` / `IsVillager`) | `-1f * MathF.sqrt(NumberOfAllMembers - PartySizeLimit)` when positive | `str_party_size_morale` |

`HighMoraleValue => 70f` is the shared "high morale" constant (used by `DefaultPartyHealingModel` for the `Medicine.BestMedicine` perk gate). A dead private helper, `CheckPerkEffectOnPartyMorale`, computes a +10 that no code consumes.

**D. Permanent vs temporary: there is no duration API.** Every "morale event" in the game is a one-shot `+=` into `RecentEventsMorale` (all 13 non-DLC writers do exactly that). The float then decays unconditionally every in-game day in `internal void MobileParty.DailyTick()` → `RecentEventsMorale -= RecentEventsMorale * 0.1f;`, driven by `CampaignPeriodicEventManager._mobilePartyDailyTicker` over `MobileParty.All`. That is exponential, not linear: 10 % of the *current* value per day, half-life ≈ 6.6 days, so +20 reads as 20 → 18 → 16.2 → … and the tooltip row disappears after ≈ 73 days (the 0.01 filter in E). Nothing in the campaign layer stores an expiry, a buff list or a per-source breakdown — sources are irreversibly merged into one number, and there is no morale-changed campaign event (`grep -i morale` in `CampaignEvents.cs` / `CampaignEventDispatcher.cs` → zero hits). Separately, starvation and unpaid wages are **both** daily pushes into `RecentEventsMorale` (`FoodConsumptionBehavior` uses `GetDailyStarvationMoralePenalty` = −30; `DefaultClanFinanceModel.ApplyMoraleEffect` uses `GetDailyNoWageMoralePenalty` = −20 scaled by the unpaid fraction and also writes `HasUnpaidWages`) **and** standing factors in C (#3, #4) — a starving party therefore loses ≈ 30/day of decaying "recent events" morale *plus* a flat 30 for as long as it starves. Full list of vanilla event writers: starvation, unpaid wages, defeat (`GetDefeatMoraleChange` −20), battle victory (`MapEventParty.CommitMoraleChanges` commits `GainedMorale`, produced by `BattleRewardModel.CalculateMoraleGainVictory` = `0.5f + renown × contribution × 0.5f`, plus `DefaultBattleRewardModel.CalculateMoraleChangeOnRoundVictory` = −3 / −1 on retreat per lost round), prisoner recruitment (`PrisonerRecruitmentCalculationModel.GetPrisonerRecruitmentMoraleEffect`), siege aftermath (`SiegeAftermathCampaignBehavior.GetSiegeAftermathPartyMoraleBonus`: devastate +20, pillage +10, show mercy −15 — the latter two only when the attacker's culture differs from the settlement's; these values are private to the behavior, not model hooks), buying a round of drinks (`TavernEmployeesCampaignBehavior.can_buy_tun_on_consequence` +2), `IncidentEffect.MoraleChange(float amount)` (incidents, main party only) and the debug command below.

**E. How the explanation tooltip is built.** `MobileParty.MoraleExplained` → `GetEffectivePartyMorale(this, includeDescription: true)` → `CampaignUIHelper.GetPartyMoraleTooltip(MobileParty mainParty)`, which starts with `GetTooltipForgProperty(string propertyName, float currentValue, ExplainedNumber explainedNumber)` (the game's own typo "Forg" is in the public API name) for the header row — title `str_party_morale` plus the current value — then separators (`TooltipAddPropertyTitleWithValue`, `TooltipAddDoubleSeperator`) and finally `private static void TooltipAddExplanation(List<TooltipProperty> properties, ref ExplainedNumber explainedNumber)`, which iterates `ExplainedNumber.GetLines()` (`List<(string name, float number)>`) and **skips every line whose |value| < 0.01**, so small factors silently never show. The lines exist only because the model was called with `includeDescription: true`: `public void ExplainedNumber.Add(float value, TextObject description = null, TextObject variable = null)` returns immediately for `value ≈ 0` and records the description only when the internal `StatExplainer` was created; `AddFactor(float value, TextObject description = null)` adds a percentage row instead. Consequence for modders: **one** `result.Add(myValue, new TextObject("{=...}My reason"))` inside a model override feeds both the number and the tooltip, with no extra plumbing. UI wiring: the map bar registers `new MapInfoItemVM("morale", () => CampaignUIHelper.GetPartyMoraleTooltip(MobileParty.MainParty))` and sets `MapInfoVM.HasWarning` when `Morale < Campaign.Current.Models.PartyDesertionModel.GetMoraleThresholdForTroopDesertion()` — i.e. the map-bar warning lights up exactly when desertion becomes possible; the party screen uses `PartyVM.MoraleHint` / `MainPartyTotalMoraleLbl` / `MoraleChangeText` and subscribes `OnPartyMoraleChanged` to `PartyScreenLogic.PartyMoraleChange`, an internal UI-only preview delegate fed by `SetMoraleChangeAmount(int newAmount)` (`PartyScreenData.PartyMoraleChangeAmount`, used for the "+X morale" recruitment preview) — it is *not* a campaign event. Clan list rows: `ClanPartiesVM.MoraleText`. `CampaignUIHelper.GetEncounterPartyMoraleTooltip(List<MobileParty> parties)` returns an empty list in 1.4.8, so the encounter overlay shows the number with no breakdown.

**F. How a mod applies a change.** Read: `MobileParty.Morale` (float, 0…100), `MobileParty.MoraleExplained` (`ExplainedNumber`), or `Campaign.Current.Models.PartyMoraleModel.GetEffectivePartyMorale(party, includeDescription)`. Write (state): `mobileParty.RecentEventsMorale += 5f;` — public, no other write path, clamped ±100, decays 10 %/day, shows up merged into the single "Recent Events" row, and the mod's reason text can never appear on it. Write (tooltip-visible, self-labelled, no decay): own factor in the model — either subclass and register a model (Q16: in `InitializeGameStarter`, `gameStarter.AddModel<PartyMoraleModel>(new MyMoraleModel());` — the generic overload `public void AddModel<T>(MBGameModel<T> gameModel) where T : GameModel` fetches the currently registered model, calls `gameModel.Initialize(model)` and appends, and `GameModelsManager.GetGameModel<T>()` scans the list **backwards**, so the last registration wins; the previous model is then available as `protected T BaseModel { get; private set; }` (Q12)), or Harmony-postfix `DefaultPartyMoraleModel.GetEffectivePartyMorale` with `ref ExplainedNumber __result`. Canonical shape (signatures only, no body copied):

```csharp
// inside an override of GetEffectivePartyMorale(MobileParty, bool includeDescription)
ExplainedNumber result = base.GetEffectivePartyMorale(party, includeDescription);
result.Add(bonus, new TextObject("{=xxxxxx}Albocarius: disgruntled companions"));
return result;
```

`base.` works when deriving from `DefaultPartyMoraleModel`; when deriving from the abstract `PartyMoraleModel`, use `BaseModel.GetEffectivePartyMorale(party, includeDescription)` instead (see Q12 for the same distinction). A *temporary* modifier should be expressed as a factor driven by the mod's own state (behavior + `SyncData`, Q8/Q9) evaluated per read — then expiry is free and the tooltip row simply disappears — because there is no API to remove a previously added `RecentEventsMorale` amount cleanly: the daily decay has already eaten part of it, so subtracting the original amount double-penalises. Model hooks worth overriding instead of patching behaviors: `GetDailyStarvationMoralePenalty(PartyBase)` and `GetDailyNoWageMoralePenalty(MobileParty)` (they change both the daily push and — for wages only — the standing factor), `HighMoraleValue` (healing/speed gates), `GetDefeatMoraleChange(PartyBase)`; overriding `GetStandardBaseMorale` / `GetVictoryMoraleChange` changes nothing (B). Periodic hooks for bookkeeping: `CampaignEvents.DailyTickPartyEvent` (what `DesertionCampaignBehavior` uses; raised by `CampaignPeriodicEventManager._dailyTickPartyTicker` per party per day — a *different* daily pass from the decay ticker) and `CampaignEvents.HourlyTickPartyEvent`. There is no morale-changed event, so a mod that needs notifications polls or patches the `RecentEventsMorale` setter. Debug console: `campaign.add_morale_to_party [HeroName] | [Number]` (`CampaignCheats.AddMoraleToParty`; `Campaign.add_morale_to_party` with no number defaults to 100, and with no hero name it applies to every lord party) — see Q30 for the console plumbing. `ItemRoster` food is a lever a mod can reuse deliberately: `TradeItemComponent.MoraleBonus` (parsed from the item XML attribute `morale_bonus`, shown as "Morale Bonus" in food tooltips by `TooltipRefresherCollection`) is **never read by the morale model** — only the count of distinct food types (`FoodVariety`) matters, so vanilla's per-item morale data is inert.

**G. What happens at low morale.** The only morale-driven *behavior* is desertion. `DesertionCampaignBehavior.DailyTickParty(MobileParty mobileParty)` gates on `mobileParty.IsActive && !mobileParty.IsCurrentlyAtSea && !mobileParty.IsDisbanding && mobileParty.Party.MapEvent == null && (mobileParty.IsLordParty || mobileParty.IsCaravan || mobileParty.IsGarrison) && mobileParty.MemberRoster.TotalRegulars > 0` — the player's main party qualifies, because `Campaign` turns it into a lord party via `LordPartyComponent.ConvertPartyToLordParty(MainParty, Hero.MainHero, Hero.MainHero)`. Then `CheckDesertionForParty` calls `Campaign.Current.Models.PartyDesertionModel.GetTroopsToDesert(mobileParty)`, removes the result with `mobileParty.MemberRoster.AddToCounts(item.Character, -item.Number, insertAtFront: false, -item.WoundedNumber)`, prints `[High Desertion Alert]` when the deserted count exceeds 40 % of members (and the party had > 10), raises `CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance.OnTroopsDeserted(...)` — exposed as `public static IMbEvent<MobileParty, TroopRoster> CampaignEvents.OnTroopsDesertedEvent` — and calls `DestroyPartyAction.Apply(null, mobileParty)` if nothing is left. Thresholds and formulas, from the model interface (`GetTroopsToDesert(MobileParty)`, `GetDesertionChanceForTroop(MobileParty, in TroopRosterElement)`, `GetMoraleThresholdForTroopDesertion()`) and `DefaultPartyDesertionModel`: the threshold is **10**, and `CalculateDesertionChanceFromTroopLevel(partyMorale, level)` = `1f - MathF.pow(level * 0.01f, 0.1f * ((threshold - min(morale, threshold)) / threshold))`, which is **exactly 0 while morale ≥ 10** — so at morale 10 nobody deserts for morale reasons at all, and morale 1…10 is the whole danger band. At morale 0 the chance is ≈ 0.149 for a level-20 troop and ≈ 0.206 for level 10 (higher-tier troops desert less). The daily *count* cap is computed with a fixed `AverageTroopLevel = 20` against `Party.NumberOfRegularMembers`, then `SelectTroopsForDesertion` rolls per roster element with that element's own level, seeded by `mobileParty.RandomFloatWithSeed(...)` (deterministic per save/hour), and only touches elements with `Character.HeroObject == null` — **named companions never desert**, wounded troops are rolled before healthy ones. A second, morale-independent path in the same model removes troops for wage and size pressure (wage gap `MathF.min(20, MathF.max(1, (TotalWage - PaymentLimit) / Campaign.Current.AverageWage * 0.25f))`, over-cap `MathF.max(1, (int)(over * 0.25f))`, garrisons with unpaid wages add ≤ 5 more), deterministically (`useProbability: false`). Two private consts in the default model, `MaxAcceptableDesertionCountForNormal = 20` and `MoraleThresholdForParty = 10`, are unused, and there is **no** `GetMoraleThresholdForParty()` member on `PartyDesertionModel` in 1.4.8 (newer game versions have one — do not assume it). Everything else that "happens" at low morale is a mechanical gate, not an event: `MobilePartyHelper.CanPartyAttackWithCurrentMorale(MobileParty)` = `Morale > 0f` disables the player's re-join/attack menu option (tooltip "Your men lack the courage to continue the battle without you. (Low Morale)"), forces the surrender option when the hero is wounded (`EncounterGameMenuBehavior.game_menu_encounter_surrender_on_condition`), stops AI parties from considering an attack *and* marks the party itself as an easy target (`DefaultMobilePartyAIModel.ShouldConsiderAttacking`), `DefaultPartySpeedCalculatingModel` adds `AddFactor(0.05f * ((morale - 70f) / 30f))` above 70 and `AddFactor(-0.1f * (1f - Morale / 30f))` below 30 (up to −10 %), `DefaultMilitaryPowerModel.GetPowerOfParty` scales estimated strength by `MBMath.Map(Morale, 20f, 40f, 0.7f, 1f)` (×0.7 flat when morale < 30), `DefaultPrisonerRecruitmentCalculationModel.ShouldPartyRecruitPrisoners` refuses at morale ≤ 30 unless the leader has the `Leadership.Presence` perk, `DefaultPartyHealingModel` gates `Medicine.BestMedicine` on `Morale >= PartyMoraleModel.HighMoraleValue` (70), `DefaultPartyTrainingModel` and the Scouting `ForcedMarch` speed bonus need `Morale > 75f`, and `DefaultArmyManagementCalculationModel.CalculateCohesionChangeInternal` counts attached parties with `Morale <= 25f` and adds `-(lowMoraleCount + 1) / 2f` cohesion per day (all cohesion terms ×0.25 for AI armies; `CohesionThresholdForDispersion => 10` dissolves the army). `Army.Morale` is only an aggregate — `RecalculateArmyMorale()` averages member parties on the army's hourly `MBCampaignEvent`, and `MapEventSide.GetSideMorale()` reports the strength-weighted side morale shown on the battle scoreboard; `CampaignMusicHandler.GetMoodOfMainParty()` maps party morale to the battle-music mood.

**H. Party morale → battle morale bridge (SandBox).** Agent battle morale is initialised in `CommonAIComponent.InitializeMorale()` from `35f + MBRandom.RandomInt(30) + Σ AgentComponent.GetMoraleAddition()`, then handed to `MissionGameModels.Current.BattleMoraleModel.GetEffectiveInitialMorale(Agent, baseMorale)` and clamped to 15…100; the only campaign contribution is SandBox's `CampaignAgentComponent.GetMoraleAddition()`, which returns `(OwnerParty.MobileParty.Morale - 50f) / 2f` (plus a relative-strength term) when the owner is in a battle. So party morale 100 ≈ +25 initial agent morale, party morale 0 ≈ −25 (i.e. clamped to the 15 floor). Battle-side writes use the extension methods `Agent.GetMorale()`, `Agent.SetMorale(float)`, `Agent.ChangeMorale(float)` on `AgentComponentExtensions`; those never touch party morale. For this project that means a companion's "mood" can only ever be expressed as (i) relation/grievance mechanics (Q18/Q21), (ii) a factor the mod adds in its own `PartyMoraleModel` override, or (iii) a one-shot `RecentEventsMorale` push — never as a per-hero field the vanilla UI would show.

### Evidence

- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.Party/MobileParty.cs` — `MobileParty.Morale` — public getter that recomputes `PartyMoraleModel.GetEffectivePartyMorale(this).ResultNumber` per read and clamps to 0…100; there is no stored morale float.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.Party/MobileParty.cs` — `MobileParty.MoraleExplained` — `GetEffectivePartyMorale(this, includeDescription: true)`; the only explained view of morale.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.Party/MobileParty.cs` — `_moraleDueToEvents` — `[SaveableField(1200)]` private float: the entire saved morale state of a party is one number.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.Party/MobileParty.cs` — `RecentEventsMorale` — public get/set property; the setter clamps to ±100 and is the only write path vanilla uses.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.Party/MobileParty.cs` — `DailyTick` — `RecentEventsMorale -= RecentEventsMorale * 0.1f;` — exponential 10 %/day decay, unconditional, no expiry field.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.Party/MobileParty.cs` — `HasUnpaidWages` — `[SaveableField(1006)] public float`, the 0…1 wage fraction the morale model multiplies by −20.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.Party/MobileParty.cs` — `HasPerk(PerkObject perk, bool checkSecondaryRole = false)` — dispatches on the perk's `PartyRole` (Quartermaster/Surgeon/PartyLeader/…), i.e. which companion's perk feeds the morale factors.
