## Q23 — Game events

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer

All the hooks below are `public static IMbEvent<…>` properties on `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignEvents` (all confirmed `public static` in the decompiled source). Subscribe exactly as in **Q8** (`CampaignBehaviorBase.RegisterEvents()` + `AddNonSerializedListener(this, handler)`); the same names also exist as `virtual` methods on `CampaignEventReceiver` and are fanned out by `CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance`, whose methods are `public override`, so a `CampaignEventReceiver` subclass sees every one of them. Two facts that dominate the "timing" column: the campaign state of an engagement is decided when `MapEvent.BattleState` is set, and the results (casualties, loot, prisoners, renown) are committed by `MapEvent.CalculateAndCommitMapEventResults()`, which the player path calls *after* `OnPlayerBattleEndEvent` and the AI path calls *inside* `MapEvent.OnBattleWon()`.

| event | `CampaignEvents` member | args (types) | is the player/clan the subject? | timing vs the state change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| battle won / lost — **the player's own battle** | `OnPlayerBattleEndEvent` | `(MapEvent mapEvent)` | by construction the player's battle (fired only from `PlayerEncounter`); win test: `mapEvent.WinningSide == PartyBase.MainParty.Side` | **after** the winner is fixed, **before** casualties / loot / prisoners / renown are committed |
| battle won / lost — **any map event, NPC battles included** | `MapEventEnded` | `(MapEvent mapEvent)` | `mapEvent.IsPlayerMapEvent`; otherwise scan `mapEvent.InvolvedParties` (`MobileParty.IsMainParty`, `MobileParty.ActualClan == Clan.PlayerClan`) or compare `mapEvent.AttackerSide.MapFaction` / `DefenderSide.MapFaction` with `Clan.PlayerClan.MapFaction`; outcome via `WinningSide`, `Winner`, `DefeatedSide` | **after** the outcome and after the results were committed; fires exactly once per engagement (`IsFinalized` guard), but *before* raid/siege component finalization (so before `RaidCompletedEvent` and `SiegeCompletedEvent` effects) |
| engagement started (whole map event) | `MapEventStarted` | `(MapEvent mapEvent, PartyBase attackerParty, PartyBase defenderParty)` | `attackerParty == PartyBase.MainParty`; `defenderParty.IsSettlement && defenderParty.Settlement.OwnerClan == Clan.PlayerClan`; `defenderParty.IsMobile && defenderParty.MobileParty.IsMainParty` | **before** any fighting or outcome — fired at the end of `MapEvent.Initialize` |
| single battle inside an engagement started | `BattleStarted` | `(PartyBase attackerParty, PartyBase defenderParty, object subject, bool showNotification)` (`subject` = the `Settlement` or `null`) | same checks as `MapEventStarted` | after the `MapEvent` already exists (`StartBattleAction.ApplyInternal` creates/joins it, then fires), before any outcome |
| player fled / retreated ("leave your soldiers behind") | `PlayerDesertedBattleEvent` | `(int sacrificedMenCount)` — number of men sacrificed to escape | player-only by construction (fired from the encounter game-menu callback) | **after** the sacrificed troops/items were already removed from the player party, before the debrief menu; `MapEventEnded` comes later when the event finalizes. A plain withdraw/retreat has **no** event — read `MapEvent.EndedByRetreat` / `MapEvent.RetreatingSide` inside `MapEventEnded` |
| companion wounded in battle | `HeroWounded` | `(Hero woundedHero)` | `woundedHero.IsPlayerCompanion` (= `CompanionOf == Clan.PlayerClan`); own party: `woundedHero.PartyBelongedTo?.IsMainParty`; player himself: `woundedHero == Hero.MainHero` | **during** the fight, at the instant `Hero.HitPoints` drops to/below `Hero.WoundedHealthLimit` (battle knock-out: `PartyAgentOrigin.SetWounded()` → `Hero.MakeWounded()`), long before `MapEventEnded`. Not battle-specific, so gate on `woundedHero.PartyBelongedTo?.MapEvent != null` for "wounded in this battle"; there is **no** heal/unwound event (poll `Hero.IsWounded`) |
| village raid started | `VillageStateChanged` + `VillageBeingRaided` | `(Village village, Village.VillageStates oldState, Village.VillageStates newState, MobileParty raiderParty)` / `(Village village)` | attacker: `raiderParty.IsMainParty` or `raiderParty.ActualClan == Clan.PlayerClan`; victim: `village.Settlement.MapFaction == Clan.PlayerClan.MapFaction` or `village.Bound.OwnerClan == Clan.PlayerClan` | `Normal → BeingRaided`, fired from `RaidEventComponent.OnInitialize()` while the `MapEvent` is still being built — i.e. **before** `MapEventStarted` and before any outcome. `VillageBeingRaided` (the single-`Village` variant) fires a moment earlier than `VillageStateChanged` for the same transition |
| village looted / burned (raid finished) | `VillageStateChanged` + `VillageLooted` / `VillageBecomeNormal`, `RaidCompletedEvent` | `(Village, Village.VillageStates, Village.VillageStates, MobileParty)`; `(Village village)`; `(BattleSideEnum winnerSide, RaidEventComponent raidEvent)` | `raiderParty.IsMainParty` ⇒ the player burned it; `newState == Village.VillageStates.Looted` ⇒ the village is deserted (`Village.IsDeserted`); `RaidEventComponent.RaidDamage` and `settlement.SettlementHitPoints` say how far the burning got | **after** `MapEventEnded`: `RaidEventComponent.OnBeforeFinalize()` (called from the tail of `MapEvent.FinalizeEventAux`) sets `Looted` when hit points hit 0, else back to `Normal`, then fires `RaidCompleted`. 1.4.8 has **no** separate "burned" `VillageStates` member — burning is `Settlement.SettlementHitPoints` damage that ends in `Looted` |
| goods taken during a raid | `ItemsLooted` | `(MobileParty raiderParty, ItemRoster items)` | `raiderParty.IsMainParty` | repeatedly during the raid's looting phase, i.e. before the `Looted` state change above |
| caravan party attacked | `MapEventStarted` (no caravan-specific event exists) | `(MapEvent, PartyBase attackerParty, PartyBase defenderParty)` | `defenderParty.IsMobile && defenderParty.MobileParty.IsCaravan` → `defenderParty.MobileParty.CaravanPartyComponent.Owner` (a `Hero`; owner clan: `.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan`); the player's own caravan is never `PartyBase.MainParty`, use the owner/`MapFaction` test | before any fighting or outcome; `mapEvent.EventType` (`MapEvent.BattleTypes`) says raid / field battle / etc. |
| villager party attacked | `MapEventStarted` (no villager-specific event exists) | same as above | `defenderParty.IsMobile && defenderParty.MobileParty.IsVillager` → `defenderParty.MobileParty.VillagerPartyComponent.Village` (target village; `VillagerPartyComponent.HomeSettlement`) | same — before any outcome; a villager party is also a common `AttackerSide`/`DefenderSide` member of a raid |
| town/castle sacked (aftermath chosen) | `OnSiegeAftermathAppliedEvent` | `(MobileParty attackerParty, Settlement settlement, SiegeAftermathAction.SiegeAftermath aftermathType, Clan previousSettlementOwner, Dictionary<MobileParty, float> partyContributions)` | player did it: `attackerParty.IsMainParty` or `attackerParty.ActualClan == Clan.PlayerClan`; player lost it: `settlement.OwnerClan == Clan.PlayerClan` or `previousSettlementOwner == Clan.PlayerClan`; `aftermathType` ∈ `Devastate`, `Pillage`, `ShowMercy` — 1.4.8 has **no** `Sack` member, the pillage menu entry is the sack | **before** the sack is applied: `SiegeAftermathAction.ApplyAftermath` only fires this event, and the prosperity / loyalty / building / gold / relation losses are done by listeners of the very same event (`SiegeAftermathCampaignBehavior.OnSiegeAftermathApplied`) |
| settlement changed owner (siege result) | `OnSettlementOwnerChangedEvent` | `(Settlement settlement, bool openToClaim, Hero newOwner, Hero oldOwner, Hero capturerHero, ChangeOwnerOfSettlementAction.ChangeOwnerOfSettlementDetail detail)` | `newOwner.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan` / `oldOwner.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan`; siege test: `detail == ChangeOwnerOfSettlementAction.ChangeOwnerOfSettlementDetail.BySiege` | after the ownership transfer inside `ChangeOwnerOfSettlementAction.ApplyInternal`; happens during the siege-assault finalization, i.e. **before** the aftermath choice above |
| siege battle won / lost for the settlement | `SiegeCompletedEvent`, `AfterSiegeCompletedEvent` | `(Settlement siegeSettlement, MobileParty attackerParty, bool isWin, MapEvent.BattleTypes battleType)` | `attackerParty.IsMainParty` / `attackerParty.ActualClan == Clan.PlayerClan`; `settlement.OwnerClan == Clan.PlayerClan` | both fire inside `MapEvent.FinalizeEventAux`: `SiegeCompleted` right after `MapEventEnded`, `AfterSiegeCompleted` at the very end of the method — i.e. after the outcome, before the aftermath menu |
| prisoner lord executed | `BeforeHeroKilledEvent`, `HeroKilledEvent` | `(Hero victim, Hero killer, KillCharacterAction.KillCharacterActionDetail detail, bool showNotification)` — filter `detail == KillCharacterAction.KillCharacterActionDetail.Executed` or `.ExecutionAfterMapEvent` | player executed them: `killer == Hero.MainHero`; player's side lost a lord: `victim.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan` (then usually `Murdered` / `DiedInBattle`); `victim.IsPrisoner` for the pre-execution state | `BeforeHeroKilledEvent`: victim still alive, nothing applied yet. `HeroKilledEvent`: after `MakeDead` **and** after the clan-leader change / clan destruction / kingdom handling ran, so `victim.Clan` may already be eliminated. Deferred case: if the victim is currently in a `MapEvent`/`SiegeEvent`, `KillCharacterAction.ApplyByExecution` only stamps `Hero.DeathMark` and fires nothing; the real kill (and both events) happen later via `KillCharacterAction.ApplyByDeathMark`, driven by the daily hero tick in `AgingCampaignBehavior` |
| prisoner lord released | `HeroPrisonerReleased` | `(Hero prisoner, PartyBase capturerParty, IFaction capturerFaction, EndCaptivityDetail detail, bool showNotification)` | player was the captor: `capturerParty == PartyBase.MainParty` (args 2/3 carry the *former* captor even though the hero is already free); player's companion freed: `prisoner.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan`; player released them: `capturerParty == PartyBase.MainParty && detail == EndCaptivityDetail.ReleasedByChoice` | **after** the release is applied (removed from the prison roster, `Hero.ChangeState(Released)`), so `prisoner.IsPrisoner` is already false. `detail` ∈ `Ransom`, `ReleasedAfterPeace`, `ReleasedAfterBattle`, `ReleasedAfterEscape`, `ReleasedByChoice`, `Death`, `ReleasedByCompensation`. Non-hero troops released at the same time are reported by `OnPrisonerReleasedEvent(FlattenedTroopRoster)` (and `OnPrisonerTakenEvent`), which are troop rosters, not lords; the capture side is `HeroPrisonerTaken(PartyBase capturer, Hero prisoner)`, fired after `AddPrisoner` |

Notes:
- Fan-out order, in one line (mechanism in Q8, listener order in Q9): `CampaignEventDispatcher` loops its registered `CampaignEventReceiver` array in registration order, and the `CampaignEvents` receiver's override is what invokes the `IMbEvent` above; `MbEvent.AddNonSerializedListener` prepends to a linked list, so listeners run in **reverse** registration order — a behavior registered after vanilla therefore handles `OnSiegeAftermathAppliedEvent` *before* vanilla applies the sack, and sees the pre-sack prosperity/loyalty numbers.
- There is no `BattleWon` / `BattleLost` member and no "player lost the battle" member: the pair `OnPlayerBattleEndEvent` (outcome known, results pending) + `MapEventEnded` (results applied) is the closest hook, and `MapEvent.WinningSide` / `DefeatedSide` / `BattleState` is how you classify win vs loss in either one.
- There is no dedicated "player retreated" event other than `PlayerDesertedBattleEvent`; the retreat state is only readable as `MapEvent.RetreatingSide` / `MapEvent.EndedByRetreat` (true when the side ran with `PursuitRoundNumber == 0`).
- Subject checks on parties use `MobileParty.IsMainParty`, `MobileParty.ActualClan`, `PartyBase.MapFaction`, `MobileParty.IsCaravan` / `IsVillager` / `IsMilitia` / `IsGarrison` and the public component getters `MobileParty.CaravanPartyComponent` / `MobileParty.VillagerPartyComponent`.
- The two sibling village engagements (`MapEvent.BattleTypes.IsForcingVolunteers` / `IsForcingSupplies`) work exactly like a raid: `ForceVolunteersEventComponent.OnInitialize()` sets `Village.VillageStates.ForcedForVolunteers`, `OnBeforeFinalize()` fires `ForceVolunteersCompletedEvent (BattleSideEnum winnerSide, ForceVolunteersEventComponent forceVolunteersEvent)` after `MapEventEnded`, and `OnFinalize()` returns the village to `Normal`.

- **UNCERTAIN**: whether the naval encounter paths (disengage / ship loss) fire the same hooks — all of the above was read from `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem`, `SandBox` and `StoryMode` only, and NavalDLC sources are excluded by project rules; the only naval-aware code seen here is `MapEvent` reading `PlayerEncounter.IsNavalEncounterFinishedWithDisengage`, which shows a naval encounter can end without a battle victory. Resolve by disassembling the NavalDLC assemblies under `~/bannerlord/dlls` with `ilspycmd` and looking for `OnPlayerBattleEnd`, `OnPlayerDesertedBattle` and `OnMapEventEnded` call sites.
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether `HeroWounded` fires when the player hero is knocked out inside a battle (the `HitPoints` setter has no hero filter, but `Hero.MainHero` may be taken by the mission/`DeathMatch` path instead) — the non-combat paths (`PayForCrimeAction`, `IssueBase`) do fire it. Resolve by logging `HeroWounded` with `woundedHero.PartyBelongedTo?.MapEvent` in a live session for one player knock-down and one issue-driven wound.
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether `MapEventEnded` also fires for the intermediate battles of a multi-round siege assault/blockade sequence, or only once per `MapEvent` object — the `IsFinalized` guard guarantees once per object, but each assault round creates its own `MapEvent`. Resolve by logging `MapEvent.StringId`/`EventType` at `MapEventEnded` across one scripted siege.
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether a `MapEvent` whose component is a `ForceVolunteersEventComponent` / `ForceSuppliesEventComponent` ever reaches `Village.VillageStates.Looted` — the components only set the `Forced*` state and restore `Normal`, but the shared `MapEvent` finalization path was not traced for those two `BattleTypes` values. Resolve by logging `OnVillageStateChanged` for a scripted levying/foraging run and checking that no `Looted` transition appears.

## Q24 — Player traits

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer

**Where trait XP/level changes happen — there is a single funnel for the player.** For `Hero.MainHero`, every runtime trait change in vanilla 1.4.8 goes through one private pipeline in `TraitLevelingHelper` (static class): all of its public `On*` methods → `AddPlayerTraitXPAndLogEntry(TraitObject trait, int xpValue, ActionNotes context, Hero referenceHero)` → `AddTraitXp(TraitObject trait, int xpAmount)`. `AddTraitXp` is the only code in the game that writes trait XP: it read-modify-writes `Campaign.Current.PlayerTraitDeveloper` (a save-stable `PropertyOwner<PropertyObject>` bucket of per-trait int XP), converts XP→level through the `CharacterDevelopmentModel` policy, and calls `Hero.MainHero.SetTraitLevel` only when the level changed. `AddPlayerTraitXPAndLogEntry` then fires `CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance.OnPlayerTraitChanged(trait, previousLevel)` **iff the level changed**, and appends a `PlayerReputationChangesLogEntry` to the player's encyclopedia log whenever `|xpValue| >= 10`. Everything else in the game is just a *call site* into the public `TraitLevelingHelper.On*` entry points (~35 files: campaign behaviors, `KillCharacterAction`, `BeHostileAction`, `QuestHelper`, `IncidentEffect`, and ~40 `*IssueBehavior` classes in `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.Issues` + `SandBox.Issues`). The `On*` methods are hard-coded to `Hero.MainHero` — they never move another hero's traits.

```csharp
// the whole pipeline, signatures only
private static void AddPlayerTraitXPAndLogEntry(TraitObject trait, int xpValue, ActionNotes context, Hero referenceHero)
private static void AddTraitXp(TraitObject trait, int xpAmount)
public static void OnIncidentResolved(TraitObject trait, int xpValue) // public, trait-agnostic XP entry
public static void UpdateTraitXPAccordingToTraitLevels()              // snaps XP to current level's threshold
```

`TraitLevelingHelper.OnIncidentResolved(TraitObject, int)` is a de-facto public general-purpose "give the player trait XP (full pipeline: XP store + level + event + log)" API despite its incident-specific name — it is just the incident effect's entry point and accepts any `TraitObject`/xp. `Hero.SetTraitLevel(TraitObject, int)` is the *other*, separate write path: public, clamps to `TraitObject.MinValue..MaxValue`, touches `_heroTraits` only — it fires **no event** and never touches the XP store, so after direct writes (character creation, `campaign.set_player_trait`) the XP bucket is stale until something calls `TraitLevelingHelper.UpdateTraitXPAccordingToTraitLevels()` (vanilla calls it at new-game and on player-character change, and both trait cheats call it). To change the XP↔level *rules* rather than grant XP, replace the `CharacterDevelopmentModel` policy via the `GameComponent` model-substitution pattern already documented in Q4.

**The event.** The only trait event is level-boundary, not XP: `CampaignEvents.PlayerTraitChangedEvent` — `public static IMbEvent<TraitObject, int>` with payload `(trait, previousLevel)` — invoked from the dispatcher method `CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance.OnPlayerTraitChanged(TraitObject trait, int previousLevel)` (public override on `CampaignEventDispatcher`, the `CampaignEventReceiver` fan-out documented in Q23; the default `CampaignEventReceiver.OnPlayerTraitChanged` is a public virtual hook). Subscribe exactly as in Q8/Q23: inside a `CampaignBehaviorBase.RegisterEvents()`, `CampaignEvents.PlayerTraitChangedEvent.AddNonSerializedListener(this, handler)` (listeners are auto-cleared when the behavior is disabled). Caveats: fires once per level crossing (a 0→2 jump fires once with `previousLevel = 0`), never for XP-only moves, and never for direct `Hero.SetTraitLevel` writes unless something calls the dispatcher manually (the `campaign.set_hero_trait` cheat does; `campaign.set_player_trait` does not).

**Reading the player's current trait levels and XP (public APIs).**

| What | Call | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Current level (−2..+2 for personality traits, see Q4) | `Hero.MainHero.GetTraitLevel(TraitObject trait)` → `int` (0 when unset) | public instance method on `Hero` |
| Current trait XP | `Campaign.Current.PlayerTraitDeveloper.GetPropertyValue(TraitObject trait)` → `int` (0 when unset) | `PlayerTraitDeveloper` is a public get-only property of `Campaign`; `PropertyOwner<T>.GetPropertyValue(T attribute)` / `SetPropertyValue(T attribute, int value)` are public in `TaleWorlds.Core` (zero removes the key) |
| XP→level mapping | `Campaign.Current.Models.CharacterDevelopmentModel.GetTraitLevelForTraitXp(Hero hero, TraitObject trait, int newValue, out int traitLevel, out int traitXp)` | public abstract (`CharacterDevelopmentModel`); default bands: xp ≤ −4000 → −2, ≤ −1000 → −1, ≥ 1000 → +1, ≥ 4000 → +2, else 0; xp clamped ±6000 for range ±2 traits (±2500 for range ±1, 0 for 0..1 traits) and level clamped to the trait's bounds |
| Level→XP threshold | `…CharacterDevelopmentModel.GetTraitXpRequiredForTraitLevel(TraitObject trait, int traitLevel)` → −4000 / −1000 / 0 / 1000 / 4000 | public abstract; this is what `UpdateTraitXPAccordingToTraitLevels` snaps the XP to |
| Trait range / id | `TraitObject.MinValue` / `TraitObject.MaxValue` (public props), `TraitObject.All`; traits are the `DefaultTraits` ids from Q4 — the runtime-changing set is exactly the 5 `DefaultTraits.Personality` traits (Mercy, Valor, Honor, Generosity, Calculating, range ±2) | public |
| Quick debug view | console `campaign.print_player_traits` prints level **and** XP for every trait | see Q30-style `campaign.*` cheat functions |

Only those 5 personality traits change at runtime: persona traits (curt/earnest/…), profession traits (Commander, Trader, …) and companion traits come from templates at creation (Q4/Q5) and no XP path writes them; `AgingCampaignBehavior` re-rolls personality traits when NPC heroes reach teen age but explicitly returns early for `Clan.PlayerClan`, so the player hero never drifts.

**Which player actions change which trait (action → trait → where in decomp).** All values are 1.4.8 constants from `TraitLevelingHelper` unless noted; "−1000" etc. is XP, a level only moves at the ±1000/±4000 bands above.

| Player action | Trait | XP | Where in decomp |
|---|---|---|---|
| A player battle ends **and** the player side's `MapEventSide.StrengthRatio > 9` (the side was heavily outnumbered — the method is named `OnBattleWon` but is called from `OnPlayerBattleEndEvent` unconditionally, see Q23) | Valor | `+Map(ratio 9→10 ⇒ 5→20) × GetPlayerBattleContributionRate()` | `PlayerVariablesBehavior.OnPlayerBattleEnd` → `TraitLevelingHelper.OnBattleWon(MapEvent, float)` |
| Player fled a battle (deserted men) | Valor | −30 | `PlayerVariablesBehavior.OnPlayerDesertedBattle` → `OnTroopsSacrificed()` (event `PlayerDesertedBattleEvent`, Q23) |
| Player raids a village and it is looted (player is attacker) | Mercy | −30 | `PlayerVariablesBehavior.OnVillageLooted` → `OnVillageRaided()` (event `VillageLooted`, Q23) |
| Player executes a lord whose own Honor ≥ 0 | Honor | −1000 | `KillCharacterAction.ApplyInternal` (detail `Executed`/`ExecutionAfterMapEvent`, killer `== Hero.MainHero`) → `OnLordExecuted()` |
| Attacking a caravan / robbing villagers / raiding a village **while at peace** (`BeHostileAction` values: encounter 6, major coercion 2, minor coercion 1) | Honor **and** Mercy | −25 × value each (−150 / −50 / −25) | `BeHostileAction.ApplyGeneralConsequencesOnPeace` → `OnHostileAction(int)` (also issue code, e.g. `NotableWantsDaughterFoundIssueBehavior.StartConversationAfterFight` passes −50) |
| Player declares war breaking a trade agreement | Honor | −1000 | `TradeAgreementsCampaignBehavior.ApplyBrokenTradeAgreementPenalty` → `OnTradeAgreementBroken()` |
| Player declares war breaking an alliance | Honor | −1000 | `AllianceCampaignBehavior.ApplyBrokenAlliancePenalty` → `OnAllianceBrokenThroughHostility()` |
| Main party starving (checked every 3 game days, party > 1 man) | Generosity | −20 | `FoodConsumptionBehavior.PartyConsumeFood` → `OnPartyStarved()` |
| Main party fed, morale ≥ 90, ≥ 20 regulars (checked every 10 game days) | Generosity | +20 | `FoodConsumptionBehavior.PartyConsumeFood` → `OnPartyTreatedWell()` |
| Releasing a captive lord by choice in conversation | Calculating | +20 | `LordConversationsCampaignBehavior.conversation_talk_lord_freed_to_lord_release_on_consequence` → `OnLordFreed(Hero)` |
| Persuading a lord to defect (barter accepted) | Calculating | +20 | `LordDefectionCampaignBehavior.defection_successful_on_consequence` → `OnPersuasionDefection(Hero)` |
| Post-siege aftermath choice, attacker is the main party and not Pillage | Mercy | ShowMercy +10 (village) / +20 (town); Devastate −30 / −50 | `SiegeAftermathCampaignBehavior.OnSiegeAftermathApplied` → `OnSiegeAftermathApplied(Settlement, SiegeAftermathAction.SiegeAftermath, TraitObject[])`; xp from `DefaultSiegeAftermathModel.GetSiegeAftermathTraitXpChangeForPlayer` |
| Incident popup options (hard-coded incidents, e.g. "Rooster theft": Honor +100 / Generosity −50) | any of the 5 | ±50..200 per option | `IncidentsCampaignBehaviour.InitializeIncidents` → `IncidentEffect.TraitChange(TraitObject, int)` → `OnIncidentResolved(TraitObject, int)` |
| Completing an issue through the quest line (trait+xp arrays are per-issue, spot-checked only) | per issue, e.g. Honor +50 | `EscortMerchantCaravanIssueBehavior.SuccessConsequences` → `OnIssueSolvedThroughQuest(Hero, Tuple<TraitObject,int>[])` |
| Issue alternative-solution failure / coercion quest botched | e.g. Honor −20 / −50 | `EscortMerchantCaravanIssueBehavior.AlternativeSolutionEndWithFailureConsequence` → `OnIssueFailed`; `QuestHelper.ApplyGenericMinorMajorCoercionConsequences` → `OnIssueSolvedThroughAlternativeSolution(Hero.MainHero, …)` |
| Issue betrayal route | e.g. Honor −50 | `ArtisanOverpricedGoodsIssueBehavior.LordSolutionConsequenceWithAcceptCounterOffer` → `OnIssueSolvedThroughBetrayal(Hero, Tuple<TraitObject,int>[])` |
| Character-creation narrative options (final review) | any of the 5 | direct **level** `+n`, no XP, no event — XP bucket then snaps via `CharacterCreationManager.ApplyFinalEffects` → `UpdateTraitXPAccordingToTraitLevels()` | `CharacterCreationContent.ApplySkillAndAttributeEffects` (`Hero.MainHero.SetTraitLevel(trait, GetTraitLevel(trait) + traitLevelToAdd)`) |
| Console `campaign.set_player_trait [Trait] \| [Number]` | any | sets **level** directly + resyncs XP to the new level's threshold, fires **no** event | `CampaignCheats.SetPlayerReputationTrait` — the precedent for "direct write then resync" |

- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CharacterDevelopment/TraitLevelingHelper.cs` — `AddTraitXp` — `private static void AddTraitXp(TraitObject trait, int xpAmount)`: `xpAmount += Campaign.Current.PlayerTraitDeveloper.GetPropertyValue(trait)`, then `Models.CharacterDevelopmentModel.GetTraitLevelForTraitXp(...)`, `PlayerTraitDeveloper.SetPropertyValue(trait, traitXp)`, and `Hero.MainHero.SetTraitLevel` only on change — the only trait-XP writer in the game.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CharacterDevelopment/TraitLevelingHelper.cs` — `OnIncidentResolved` — `public static void OnIncidentResolved(TraitObject trait, int xpValue)` routing straight into the funnel with `ActionNotes.DefaultNote` and `Hero.MainHero`; the trait-agnostic public XP entry a mod can reuse.

### Uncertain

- **UNCERTAIN**: whether Valor XP is also granted for a *lost* battle — `OnBattleWon` is actually invoked from `OnPlayerBattleEndEvent` for every player battle and gated only on the player side's `StrengthRatio > 9f`; the exact inputs of the `StrengthRatio` formula (`x`, `num` multipliers) in `MapEvent`'s post-battle computation were not traced. ## Q25 — Companion-initiated conversation

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer

**Yes — a conversation with a party companion can be opened programmatically on the campaign map. There are two distinct mechanisms.**

**(A) Map conversation — a 2D dialogue overlay drawn on the map screen.** Entry point `CampaignMapConversation.OpenConversation(ConversationCharacterData playerCharacterData, ConversationCharacterData conversationPartnerData)` (public static void, `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.Conversation`) — a one-liner that forwards to `Campaign.Current.ConversationManager.OpenMapConversation(playerCharacterData, conversationPartnerData)` (public instance void, same two params). What it does: (1) `(GameStateManager.Current?.ActiveState as MapState).OnMapConversationStarts(...)` — the cast is unchecked, so this is where the game-state constraint lives: if `ActiveState` is not `MapState` the call throws `NullReferenceException` (no decompiled source declares a `MapState` subclass, so "is `MapState`" is literal — not during a battle mission, not in a settlement/conversation mission scene, not while a fullscreen panel GameState such as the clan screen is on top of the map); (2) `ConversationManager.SetupAndStartMapConversation(party, IAgent, IAgent)` with two dummy `MapConversationAgent` objects, which starts the normal dialog machinery at token 0 (`StartNew(0, setActionsInstantly: true)` — same token/priority graph as Q20; vanilla grievance lines are registered via `AddDialogLine` at priority 120), sets `NeedsToActivateForMapConversation = true` and runs `OnConversationActivate()`, but does **not** call `BeginConversation()` — that deferred call happens only from `MissionConversationLogic.OnMissionTick` (guarded by `NeedsToActivateForMapConversation && !GameNetwork.IsReplay`); (3) `MapState` forwards to its `IMapStateHandler` (implemented by `MapScreen`), which initializes `MapConversationView`: the Gauntlet movie `MapConversation` plus a 2D tableau backdrop is loaded, a fake `MapConversationMission : ICampaignMission` is installed so `CampaignMission.Current` exists, and layers such as the map bar are suspended (`OnMapConversationStarted`/`Over`). Teardown: `ConversationManager.EndConversation()` (public; called when the dialog reaches its end line) finishes with `Handler?.OnConversationUninstall()` → `GauntletMapConversationView` finds the `MapState` in the GameState stack and calls `MapState.OnMapConversationOver()` → MapScreen restores views, cursor and menu.

**(B) Conversation mission — a real 3D scene mission.** `CampaignMission.OpenConversationMission(ConversationCharacterData playerCharacterData, ConversationCharacterData conversationPartnerData, string specialScene = "", string sceneLevels = "", bool isMultiAgentConversation = false)` — public static returning `IMission`; SandBox implements it as `SandBoxMissions.OpenConversationMission` → `MissionState.OpenNew("Conversation", ...)` with `MissionConversationLogic` + `ConversationMissionLogic` behaviors; the scene comes from `SceneModel.GetConversationSceneForMapPosition` unless `specialScene` is passed. Vanilla picks (B) when (A) is impossible — at sea (`CompanionGrievanceBehavior`, `PlayerEncounter` set `conversationPartnerData.Party` and switch APIs at sea).

**Where it is allowed.** The only hard constraint of (A) is `GameStateManager.Current.ActiveState is MapState`. Being in *menu mode* on the map (radial context menu open, `Campaign.Current.CurrentMenuContext != null`) or inside a settlement (`LocationComplex.Current != null`) is still `MapState` — vanilla `GameMenuOverlay` deliberately opens map conversations exactly in those cases. The API itself checks nothing about battles, sieges or encounters; vanilla callers guard themselves: `CompanionGrievanceBehavior.OnHourlyTick` bails when `MobileParty.MainParty.MapEvent != null` (a battle simulation is running — field battle or siege battle on the map), `PlayerEncounter.Current != null`, `!(ActiveState is MapState)` or at sea; StoryMode quest triggers additionally check `!ConversationManager.IsConversationFlowActive`. To talk from a panel GameState, vanilla pops the panel first (`Game.Current.GameStateManager.PopState()` in `ClanMembersVM`) and only then opens the conversation.

**Companion in the player's party as partner.** `new ConversationCharacterData(grievingHero.CharacterObject)` — the struct's constructor is `ConversationCharacterData(CharacterObject character, PartyBase party = null, bool noHorse = false, bool noWeapon = false, ...)`; vanilla passes no party for the land case and only sets `.Party = MobileParty.MainParty.Party` for the at-sea mission variant; player data is `new ConversationCharacterData(Hero.MainHero.CharacterObject, MobileParty.MainParty.Party)`.

**Vanilla examples of programmatic opening** (all without the player pressing talk): companion grievance conversation auto-triggered on an hourly tick — the closest analogue to companion-initiated conversation; StoryMode quest conversations (`RescueFamilyQuestBehavior`); issue counter-offers (`IssueBase`); map radial-menu quick talk (`GameMenuOverlay`) and clan-panel talk (`ClanMembersVM`); pre-battle meeting conversations (`PlayerEncounter.DoMeetingInternal`).

**Does it pause time? Not by itself.** Neither entry point writes `Campaign.TimeControlMode`: an enumeration of every `TimeControlMode =` / `SetTimeControlModeLock` write site in TaleWorlds/SandBox/StoryMode shows no hit anywhere in the map-conversation path (ConversationManager, MapState conversation hooks, MapScreen handler, both conversation views, MapConversationVM). The campaign clock is driven solely from `MapState.OnMapModeTick` (`Campaign.RealTick(dt)` / `Campaign.Tick()`, executed only while `MapState` is the active state), and `Campaign.TickMapTime(float realDt)` maps the current `CampaignTimeControlMode` to `_dt` — zero only for Stop/FastForwardStop, or StoppablePlay while `IsMainPartyWaiting` — so during a map conversation the clock keeps advancing at whatever speed it had; vanilla stops time through other systems that co-occur (game menus set `CampaignTimeControlMode.Stop`; inquiry popups stop and lock via `SetTimeControlModeLock(true)`), and a mod can do the same before opening a conversation. What vanilla *does* gate while `MapConversationActive`: auto-save is skipped (`SaveHandler` requires `ActiveState is MapState { MapConversationActive: false }`) and the escape menu's save/load/quit options are disabled — vanilla treats an active map conversation as save-unsafe, not as a time freeze. By contrast (B) freezes campaign time as a side effect: `MissionState.OpenNew` leaves `MapState`, and since only `MapState` drives the campaign tick, the simulation stands still for the whole 3D conversation mission.

## Q26 — Inquiry pop-ups

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer

**The pop-up ("query") system is a fire-and-forget static event plus a plain data object — there is no screen or GameState to open and no campaign/mission precondition. The two entry points R6 needs are `InformationManager.ShowInquiry` (title + text + at most **two** buttons) and `MBInformationManager.ShowMultiSelectionInquiry` (title + text + **N** selectable rows + one confirm/cancel pair). Both are `public static void` on public static classes in `TaleWorlds.Library` / `TaleWorlds.Core`, both are used by vanilla campaign behaviors, mission UIs, fullscreen panels and the launcher/main-menu path alike, and vanilla ships the prefabs (`SingleQueryPopup`, `MultiSelectionQueryPopup`, `TextQueryPopup`) — a mod needs no XML of its own.**

**1. Two-option pop-up — `TaleWorlds.Library.InformationManager` (public static class).**

```csharp
public static void ShowInquiry(InquiryData data, bool pauseGameActiveState = false, bool prioritize = false)
public static void ShowTextInquiry(TextInquiryData textData, bool pauseGameActiveState = false, bool prioritize = false)
public static void HideInquiry()
public static bool IsAnyInquiryActive()
```

`ShowInquiry` is literally `OnShowInquiry?.Invoke(data, pauseGameActiveState, prioritize)` for a `public static event Action<InquiryData, bool, bool>`; the only subscriber in the shipped game is `GauntletQueryManager` (item 4). With no subscriber the call is a **silent no-op** — no exception, nothing drawn. `HideInquiry()` closes the current pop-up **and immediately shows the next queued one**; `IsAnyInquiryActive()` reports only the *displayed* pop-up (`_activeDataSource != null`), never queued ones.

Payload — `TaleWorlds.Library.InquiryData` (public class, single 13-parameter ctor):

```csharp
new InquiryData(string titleText, string text, bool isAffirmativeOptionShown, bool isNegativeOptionShown,
  string affirmativeText, string negativeText, Action affirmativeAction, Action negativeAction,
  string soundEventPath = "", float expireTime = 0f, Action timeoutAction = null,
  Func<(bool, string)> isAffirmativeOptionEnabled = null, Func<(bool, string)> isNegativeOptionEnabled = null)
```

- **At most two options.** There are exactly two button slots (`…OptionShown` + `Action`); the dominant vanilla form for one-button notices is `isNegativeOptionShown: false` with null negative text/action. A three-way choice cannot be expressed here — vanilla either chains pop-ups (they queue, item 6) or uses item 2.
- Optional `Func<(bool, string)>` getters are re-evaluated **every frame** while the pop-up is open; the returned string becomes the disabled button's hover hint (`ButtonOkHint` / `ButtonCancelHint` in the prefab).
- `expireTime > 0` shows a draining bar and at expiry runs `timeoutAction` and closes by itself; `soundEventPath` is a 2D FMOD path played on show.
- Only `TitleText` and `Text` are writable (plus `SetText`/`SetTitleText`); every callback/flag/timer field is `readonly`, so a pop-up's behaviour cannot be mutated after construction, and since the view copies the strings at `SetData`, mutating `Text` after the pop-up is on screen changes nothing.
- An empty `titleText` auto-hides the title block; the body is rich text inside a scrollable region clipped to 480 px, so `{newline}` and markup work.

**2. N-option pop-up — `TaleWorlds.Core.MBInformationManager` (public static class).**

```csharp
public static void ShowMultiSelectionInquiry(MultiSelectionInquiryData data, bool pauseGameActiveState = false, bool prioritize = false)
```

```csharp
new MultiSelectionInquiryData(string titleText, string descriptionText, List<InquiryElement> inquiryElements,
  bool isExitShown, int minSelectableOptionCount, int maxSelectableOptionCount, string affirmativeText,
  string negativeText, Action<List<InquiryElement>> affirmativeAction, Action<List<InquiryElement>> negativeAction,
  string soundEventPath = "", bool isSeachAvailable = false) // the shipped parameter/property really is misspelled
```

- Rows are `new InquiryElement(object identifier, string title, ImageIdentifier imageIdentifier)` or the 5-arg overload `…, bool isEnabled, string hint`. `Identifier` is `object` and is the natural payload carrier (vanilla passes a string key, a `CharacterObject`, or a `TroopObject`); `ImageIdentifier` may be `null` for a text-only row, portraits use `new CharacterImageIdentifier(CharacterCode.CreateFrom(obj))`; a greyed-out row puts its reason in `hint`.
- There is **one** affirmative `Action<List<InquiryElement>>` receiving every selected row — no per-row callbacks, no timer/timeout on this type. For a mutually exclusive N-way choice use `min = max = 1`: the view clears the other rows on selection (radio behaviour) and OK is enabled only when `MinSelectableOptionCount <= selected` and (`MaxSelectableOptionCount <= 0` — unlimited — `|| selected <= Max`); dispatch on `selected[0].Identifier`.
- `isExitShown` gates the cancel/Esc affordance, `isSeachAvailable` adds a search field for long lists. The element list is snapshotted into view-model rows at `SetData`, so mutating the `List<InquiryElement>` afterwards does nothing.

**3. Text-entry variant.** `ShowTextInquiry(TextInquiryData)` mirrors item 1 but takes `Action<string> affirmativeAction`, `bool shouldInputBeObfuscated`, a `Func<string, Tuple<bool, string>> textCondition` validator re-run per frame (its string is the rejection hint) and `defaultInputText`; vanilla uses it for naming a save file.

**4. Who renders it, hence where it may be shown.** The single subscriber for all three kinds is `GauntletQueryManager : GlobalLayer` (`TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade.GauntletUI`), constructed once from `GauntletUISubModule.OnBeforeInitialModuleScreenSetAsRoot` (`Initialize()` + `InitializeKeyVisuals()`; the whole block is skipped only under `--VisualTests`). `Initialize()` subscribes `OnShowInquiry`/`OnShowTextInquiry`/`MBInformationManager.OnShowMultiSelectionInquiry`/`OnHideInquiry`, supplies `IsAnyInquiryActiveInternal`, builds the three pop-up VMs, creates `new GauntletLayer("QueryManager", 19501, false)`, `ScreenManager.AddGlobalLayer(this, true)` and then `ScreenManager.SetSuspendLayer(Layer, true)` — idle until a pop-up arrives. Consequences:
 - It is a **global layer, not a GameState or a screen**, so it is available in the main menu, on the campaign map, over a map conversation, over the map escape menu, over fullscreen panels and inside missions; the decompiled layer orders put it at 19501, above `ClanScreen` (1), `MapConversation` (205), `MapMenuView` (100), `MapEscapeMenu` (4400), `ChatLog` (15300), `FullScreenNotice` (15010) and `GameNotification` (19007), below `SceneNotification` (19600), `Tooltip` (115000) and `LoadingWindow` (115003).
 - It starts suspended and unfocused; on show `SetLayerFocus(true)` unsuspends it, `TrySetFocus`es it and calls `InputRestrictions.SetInputRestrictions(true, (InputUsageMask)7)` — `All` = mouse buttons + wheels + keyboard — so the pop-up is **input-modal**; the screen underneath keeps ticking and rendering but receives no input. `OnEarlyTick` re-grabs focus whenever a layer of order ≤ 19501 takes it.
 - Keyboard/gamepad come from `GenericPanelGameKeyCategory`: `Confirm` runs the affirmative action only when the OK button is shown **and** enabled, `Exit` the negative action only when the cancel button is shown; the same commands are wired to the prefab buttons `SingleQueryOkButton` / `SingleQueryCancelButton` / `DoneButtonWidget`.
 - Guard your own UI with `InformationManager.IsAnyInquiryActive()` the way vanilla does (`MapScreen.OnFocusChangeOnGameWindow` skips the auto escape-menu/pause, `HeirSelectionPopupVM` hides its hotkeys).

**5. Does it pause the game? Only if you ask.** Both Show calls default to `pauseGameActiveState: false` and time keeps running. With `true`, `HandleQueryCreated` does **two** things, both undone by `CloseQuery`: `GameStateManager.Current.RegisterActiveStateDisableRequest(this)` and `MBCommon.PauseGameEngine()`.
 - Active-state half: `GameStateManager.OnTick` calls `ActiveState.OnIdleTick(dt)` instead of `OnTick(dt)` while any request is registered (`ActiveStateDisabledByUser`; requests are `WeakReference`s of the requesting instance, cleaned only when dead, and they are not cleared by state push/pop or by save-load). On the map that means `MapState.OnIdleTick` runs and `OnMapModeTick` is skipped, so `Campaign.RealTick`/`Tick` never advance (see Q7/Q27): hourly/daily ticks, movement and schedules all stop.
 - Engine half: `MBCommon.PauseGameEngine()` → `MBAPI.IMBWorld.PauseGame()`; `MissionState.OnTick` zeroes its dt when `MBCommon.IsPaused`, and while the disable request stands, `MissionState.OnIdleTick` only calls `CurrentMission.IdleTick(dt)` (mission flow, no simulation). So a pop-up over a battle with the flag freezes the battle too.
 - Vanilla map pop-ups usually *also* write `Campaign.Current.TimeControlMode = CampaignTimeControlMode.Stop;` on the line before `ShowInquiry(…, pauseGameActiveState: true)` — that stops the player's own time control (Q7/Q27) while the flag is the hard freeze. Mission UIs instead pass `false, false` (the escape menu's "abandon mission?" confirmation does not freeze the fight).
 - The pop-up's own tick is independent of all of that: `EngineScreenManager.Tick(dt)` (engine callback) → `ScreenManager.Tick` → global-layer `LateTick` → `GauntletQueryManager.OnLateTick` → `_activeDataSource.OnTick(dt)`, i.e. the `expireTime` bar keeps draining on frame time even while campaign time and the mission are frozen.

**6. One at a time, with a FIFO queue and a silent dedupe.** `CreateQuery`: when a pop-up is already active the new request is either enqueued (`_inquiryQueue`, FIFO, popped by `CloseQuery`) or, with `prioritize: true`, pushed to the front by `QueueAndShowNewData`, which re-queues the current pop-up (with `prioritize: false`) and closes it — so what you cut in front of comes back afterwards. Before enqueuing, the request is compared against the active **and** every queued item by `HasSameContentWith`, which compares all fields including the delegate references: two pop-ups built from the same method group or the same lambda variable are "equal", two with identical strings but distinct lambdas are not. A duplicate is dropped with nothing but a `Debug.FailedAssert("Trying to create query but it is already present! Title: …")`, and the shipping `Debug.DebugManager` is `MBDebugManager`, whose `Assert` body is empty — **in retail a duplicate inquiry simply vanishes, no exception**. When nothing is active no dedupe check happens at all.

**7. Where the callbacks run.** Affirmative/negative/timeout actions are invoked from the pop-up view-model during the QueryManager's tick (UI frame), *not* inside `Campaign.Tick()`; `ExecuteAffirmativeAction` calls the action and then `CloseQuery()`. Vanilla mutates campaign state directly from those callbacks (accepting a ransom, leaving a kingdom), which is the shape R6 should copy, subject to the tick-context rules of Q7/Q25.

**8. Vanilla usage examples.** (a) Two-option, campaign map, hard-paused: `RansomOfferCampaignBehavior.OnRansomOffered` (listener on `CampaignEvents.OnRansomOfferedToPlayerEvent`) writes `Campaign.Current.TimeControlMode = CampaignTimeControlMode.Stop;` then calls `ShowInquiry(new InquiryData(…, true, true, …Yes…, …No…, () => AcceptRansomOffer(ransomPrice), DeclineRansomOffer, "", 0f, null, () => IsAffirmativeOptionEnabled(ransomPayer, ransomPrice)), pauseGameActiveState: true)` — note the enable-callback that greys out *Yes* with a reason. (b) One-option tick pop-up: `AgingCampaignBehavior.IsItTimeOfDeath` (from `DailyTickHero`) shows a "Close"-only inquiry with sound `event:/ui/notification/quest_fail` and default pause flags. (c) N-option radio in campaign code: `AlleyHelper.CreateMultiSelectionInquiryForSelectingClanMemberToAlley` builds one `InquiryElement` per clan member (portrait, availability gate, disabled reason as `hint`) and shows it with `isExitShown: true, 1, 1` and `pauseGameActiveState: true`, handing the picked row to the caller's callback; `KingdomManagementVM` uses `"keep"`/`"dontkeep"` string identifiers switched on inside `OnConfirmLeaveKingdomWithOption`; `PrisonBreakCampaignBehavior` lists prisoners with `(1, 1)` and `false, false`; `EncounterGameMenuBehavior`'s "abandon the siege?" confirm runs in menu mode with the default flags, and `Module.cs` shows pop-ups before any campaign exists at all.

**For R6:** `InformationManager.ShowInquiry` for confirm/decline, `MBInformationManager.ShowMultiSelectionInquiry` with `(min, max) = (1, 1)` and `Identifier` dispatch for anything with more than two outcomes; pass `pauseGameActiveState: true` (plus `TimeControlMode.Stop`) for map-time decisions; build a fresh `InquiryData`/`MultiSelectionInquiryData` per request so the dedupe never swallows one; and do not use `IsAnyInquiryActive()` to detect a pop-up you only queued.

## Q27 — Campaign time

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer

**1. "Now" — `CampaignTime.Now`, and nothing else.** `public struct CampaignTime` is one private `long _numTicks`: an *absolute* position on a single campaign-wide tick timeline, not a wall clock and not a per-entity clock. The live clock lives in `internal class MapTimeTracker` behind `internal Campaign.MapTimeTracker`, and `CampaignTime.NumTicks`, the `CampaignTime(long)` constructor and the whole `TimeTicksPer*` scale are `internal` — a mod cannot read the tick count and should not try. `public static CampaignTime Now { get; }` is the current instant; `public static CampaignTime DeltaTime { get; }` is how much *game* time the last map frame advanced (zero while paused). Epoch: `CampaignTime.Zero` = tick 0, and a new campaign's clock starts at `CampaignTimeModel.CampaignStartTime` — `DefaultCampaignTimeModel` = `CampaignTime.Years(1084f) + CampaignTime.Weeks(CampaignTime.WeeksInSeason) + CampaignTime.Hours(9f)`, ≈91,000 days with the default calendar (a Bannerlord year = `WeeksInSeason × DaysInWeek × SeasonsInYear` = 3×7×4 = 84 days). `Campaign.OnInitialize` builds a fresh tracker only for a new campaign; a loaded campaign restores the serialized one, and the tracker is part of the save (registered as class 24, `[SaveableField(0)] _numTicks`) — ticks are never re-based, so a stamp written today is still comparable 50 game years later. Everything that touches the clock (`Now`, `IsPast`, `Elapsed*UntilNow`, …) dereferences `Campaign.Current`, so it throws outside a running campaign — guard it exactly as in Q26/Q16.

Calendar constants are `public static int` *fields* on `CampaignTime` (`SunRise`, `SunSet`, `MillisecondInSecond`, `SecondsInMinute`, `MinutesInHour`, `HoursInDay`, `DaysInWeek`, `WeeksInSeason`, `SeasonsInYear`) plus the computed `DaysInSeason`/`DaysInYear`. `CampaignTime.Initialize()` copies them out of `Campaign.Current.Models.CampaignTimeModel` (model override: see Q16/Q18) once inside `Campaign.OnInitialize`, before any behavior runs — a mod must never call it itself.

Public instance surface a behavior system needs:

| group | members (all public) |
|---|---|
| ordering | `== != < > <= >=`, `Equals(CampaignTime)`, `CompareTo`, `GetHashCode` |
| relation to the live clock | `IsPast`, `IsFuture`, `IsNow` (compared afresh on every read) |
| elapsed / remaining (float) | `Elapsed{Milliseconds,Seconds,Hours,Days,Weeks,Seasons,Years}UntilNow`, `Remaining…FromNow` — e.g. `ElapsedDaysUntilNow => (float)(CurrentTicks - _numTicks) / (float)TimeTicksPerDay`, so precision depends on the *elapsed* span, not on the huge absolute value; negative when the instant is the other side of now |
| absolute conversion (double) | `To{Milliseconds,Seconds,Minutes,Hours,Days,Weeks,Seasons,Years}` |
| calendar / day part | `GetHourOfDay`, `CurrentHourInDay`, `IsDayTime`/`IsNightTime` (against `SunRise`/`SunSet`), `GetDayOfWeek`, `GetWeekOfSeason`, `GetDayOfSeason`, `GetDayOfYear`, `GetSeasonOfYear` (nested `public enum Seasons`), `GetYear`, `ToString()` (localised `str_date_format` with SEASON/YEAR/DAY — usable straight in a notification, Q17) |
| same calendar day | `bool StringSameAs(CampaignTime otherTime)` |
| arithmetic / sentinels | `instant + duration`, `instant - instant` → duration, `CampaignTime.Zero`, `CampaignTime.Never` (`long.MaxValue` ticks) |
| static factories | `Milliseconds(long)`, `Seconds(long)`, `Minutes(long)`, `Hours(float)`, `Days(float)`, `Weeks(float)`, `Years(float)` and a `…FromNow(value)` twin of each |

Unit caveat: the second→day scale is fixed (`TimeTicksPerMillisecond = 10`, then ×1000 ×60 ×60 ×24 ⇒ `TimeTicksPerDay = 864,000,000`), but `DefaultCampaignTimeModel.DaysInWeek` returns 7 or **3** and `WeeksInSeason` 3 or **2** depending on `Campaign.Current.Options.AccelerationMode == GameAccelerationMode.Fast`, and `CampaignStartTime` is itself built from `Weeks(WeeksInSeason)`. Absolute stamps and day/hour arithmetic stay correct either way; week/season/year arithmetic (`GetYear`, `GetDayOfWeek`, `GetWeekOfSeason`, `ToYears`, `ElapsedYearsUntilNow`) is mode-dependent, so gate behavior on days/hours/seconds, never on calendar-year fields.

**2. Hourly / daily ticks — subscribe to the static `CampaignEvents` tick events.** Every periodic campaign tick is exposed as a `public static` property returning `IMbEvent` / `IMbEvent<T>`, hooked in `RegisterEvents()` (Q8) the usual way: `CampaignEvents.HourlyTickEvent.AddNonSerializedListener(this, (Action)OnHourlyTick);`.

| event (`CampaignEvents.`…) | payload | period | where it comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `QuarterHourlyTickEvent` | none | 15 game minutes | `CreatePeriodicEvent(CampaignTime.Hours(0.25f), …)` |
| `HourlyTickEvent` | none | whole game hour | `CreatePeriodicEvent(CampaignTime.Hours(1f), …)` |
| `DailyTickEvent` | none | whole game day | `CreatePeriodicEvent(CampaignTime.Days(1f), …)` (mechanism already covered in Q8 §3) |
| `WeeklyTickEvent` | none | every `DaysInWeek` days since campaign start | no periodic event: emitted from inside `Campaign.DailyTick` when `(int)CampaignStartTime.ElapsedDaysUntilNow % CampaignTime.DaysInWeek == 0` |
| `DailyTickPartyEvent`, `DailyTickTownEvent`, `DailyTickSettlementEvent`, `DailyTickHeroEvent`, `DailyTickClanEvent` | `MobileParty`, `Town`, `Settlement`, `Hero`, `Clan` | once per day per object | debt-based `PeriodicTicker`s created in `CampaignPeriodicEventManager.InitializeTickers()` |
| `HourlyTickPartyEvent`, `HourlyTickSettlementEvent`, `HourlyTickClanEvent` | `MobileParty`, `Settlement`, `Clan` | once per hour per object | same tickers |
| `AiHourlyTickEvent` | `MobileParty, PartyThinkParams` | per party, batched | `Campaign.Tick` → `TickPartialHourlyAi` |
| `TickEvent` | `float dt` | every map frame while time flows | `Campaign.Tick` → `CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance.Tick(_dt)` |

Two consequences for the behavior foundation. (a) Only the four *global* events are boundary-aligned: `Campaign.CreateCampaignEvents()` runs on every session (new game **and** load, from `Campaign.OnDataLoadFinished`) and derives a partial `initialWait` from `numTicks % TimeTicksPerDay`, `% TimeTicksPerHour` and `% (TimeTicksPerHour / 4)` so the next tick lands exactly on a whole day/hour/quarter-hour mark. The *per-entity* ticks are deliberately spread through the period by tickers driven by `CampaignTime.DeltaTime`, so "once a day for each of my companions" should iterate the mod's own roster from `DailyTickEvent` rather than trust `DailyTickHeroEvent`'s timing. (b) Nothing fires unless game time is flowing: `Campaign.TickMapTime(realDt)` maps `TimeControlMode` to `_dt` (`num2 = 0.25f * realDt`, ×`SpeedUpMultiplier` = 4 for the fast-forward modes, forced to 0 for `Stop`/`FastForwardStop` and for `StoppablePlay` while the main party waits) and then calls `MapTimeTracker.Tick(4320f * _dt)` — 1080 game seconds per real second at 1×, i.e. one game day ≈ 80 real seconds (≈20 s fast-forward) — and `Campaign.Tick()` runs the periodic pass only when `_dt > 0` (the `MapState.OnMapModeTick` driver and the waiting/menu zeroing are in Q25/Q26).

A mod can schedule its own periodic callback: `public static MBCampaignEvent CampaignPeriodicEventManager.CreatePeriodicEvent(CampaignTime triggerPeriod, CampaignTime initialWait)` (public, static; it appends to `Campaign.Current.CustomPeriodicCampaignEvents`, which is internal, so the factory is the only way in), then `public void AddHandler(MBCampaignEvent.CampaignEventDelegate)` with `public delegate void CampaignEventDelegate(MBCampaignEvent campaignEvent, params object[] delegateParams)` — vanilla hands every handler `CampaignTime.Now` as the single argument. `Unregister(object instance)` and `DeletePeriodicEvent()` clean up; custom events are re-checked at most once per `MinimumPeriodicEventInterval = CampaignTime.Hours(0.05f)` of game time, and `MBCampaignEvent.CheckUpdate()` loops `while (NextTriggerTime.IsPast)` — one handler call per missed period, possibly several in the same frame during fast-forward. None of it is saved: `NextTriggerTime` is `[CachedData]` and `CustomPeriodicCampaignEvents` carries no save attribute, so a mod periodic event must be re-created every session (in `RegisterEvents`) and will *not* replay time that passed while the game was closed. Recommendation for R7: keep absolute timestamps/deadlines and test them from the existing daily/hourly events instead of creating extra periodic events — they survive saves for free and cannot leak duplicate handlers.

**3. "N days since X" — store the instant, ask it later.** Never store a duration.

```csharp
private CampaignTime _lastVisit;                         // default == CampaignTime.Zero
_lastVisit = CampaignTime.Now;                           // stamp it
bool aDayPassed = _lastVisit.ElapsedDaysUntilNow >= 1f;
double days = (CampaignTime.Now - _lastVisit).ToDays;    // exact ticks, double division
```

The float `Elapsed…UntilNow` getters are the vanilla idiom: `PlayerTownVisitCampaignBehavior` gates on `_lastTimeRelationGivenPathfinder.ElapsedDaysUntilNow >= 1f`, and a plain *dialog condition* (`conversation_lord_greets_under_24_hours_on_condition`) gates on `Hero.OneToOneConversationHero.LastMeetingTimeWithPlayer.ElapsedHoursUntilNow < 24f` — exactly the "condition reads a persisted timestamp" shape the behavior system wants. Use `(CampaignTime.Now - stamp).ToDays` (double) when accumulating or comparing against a duration; `Remaining…FromNow` is the mirror. Due-date style: `CampaignTime due = CampaignTime.DaysFromNow(3f)` (also `HoursFromNow`, `WeeksFromNow`, …) then test `due.IsPast` or `CampaignTime.Now >= due`. Same-calendar-day test: `stamp.StringSameAs(CampaignTime.Now)`. Bucketing: vanilla does `(int)CampaignTime.Now.ToDays % 3 == 0` (Q24). Unset vs long-ago matters: the default struct is `Zero` = tick 0, whose `ElapsedDaysUntilNow` is ≈91,000 game days (≈26,000 in Fast acceleration mode) — it reads as "very long ago", never "recent", which is usually what a cooldown wants; when *unset* must be distinguishable, vanilla checks `stamp.Equals(CampaignTime.Zero)` first (`PlayerTownVisitCampaignBehavior`). For "no deadline", compare against `CampaignTime.Never` (`long.MaxValue` ticks): comparisons are safe, arithmetic is not (it overflows).

**4. Storing a timestamp in a `CampaignBehaviorBase.SyncData` save — yes, `CampaignTime` works directly.** It is already a registered saveable *struct*: the shipped game's `SaveableCampaignTypeDefiner.DefineStructTypes` calls `AddStructDefinition(typeof(CampaignTime), 1001)`, the payload is its single `[SaveableField(2)] private readonly long _numTicks`, and `AutoGeneratedSaveManager` wires the generated accessor (`CampaignTime.AutoGeneratedGetMemberValue_numTicks`) plus an object collector that collects nothing (no references). So the Q8 registration rule is already satisfied by the game — a mod needs no `SaveableTypeDefiner` for a `CampaignTime` field, and the same is true inside mod classes that *are* registered (vanilla precedents: `IssueCoolDownData.ExpireTime` = `[SaveableField(0)] public readonly CampaignTime` with `IsValid() => !ExpireTime.IsPast`; `Hero._birthDay`/`_deathDay`; `[SaveableProperty(620)] public CampaignTime LastMeetingTimeWithPlayer`, written by `Hero.SetHasMet()` as `LastMeetingTimeWithPlayer = CampaignTime.Now`).

```csharp
private CampaignTime _lastVisit;                      // field, not property (ref T)
public override void SyncData(IDataStore data)
{
    data.SyncData("_lastVisit", ref _lastVisit);      // exactly once per key
}
```

Mechanics and traps (contract in Q8, load semantics in Q9): the behavior record map is a registered `Dictionary<string, object>`, so the struct is stored **boxed** and it is the boxed runtime type (id 1001) that makes it saveable. `BehaviorSaveData.SyncData` does `_records.Add(key, data)` while saving — a repeated key throws, so each key must be synced exactly once per `SyncData` call, and the records are namespaced by the behavior's `StringId` (Q8/Q9 naming caveat). On load it does `TryGetValue` + `(T)value`, so a missing key returns `false` and leaves the field at its **default** — for `CampaignTime` that is `Zero` (≈91k days ago), *not* "now"; and a key whose type changed between versions breaks that cast.

CampaignTime *containers* are pre-registered by the game as well, so these cost a mod nothing: `List<CampaignTime>`, `CampaignTime[]`, `Dictionary<string, CampaignTime>`, `Dictionary<Hero, CampaignTime>`, `Dictionary<MobileParty, CampaignTime>`, `Dictionary<Settlement, CampaignTime>`, `Dictionary<Clan, CampaignTime>`, `Dictionary<Town, CampaignTime>`, `Dictionary<Village, CampaignTime>`, `Dictionary<Kingdom, CampaignTime>`, `Dictionary<Incident, CampaignTime>`, `Dictionary<Hero, List<CampaignTime>>`, `Dictionary<MobileParty, Dictionary<Settlement, CampaignTime>>`, `Dictionary<MobileParty, Dictionary<MobileParty, CampaignTime>>`, `Tuple<Kingdom, CampaignTime>`.

**Alternative: keep it as a number.** That also needs no registration, because numeric primitives are *basic types*: `SaveableBasicTypeDefiner.DefineBasicTypes` registers `int, uint, short, ushort, byte, sbyte, float, double, long, ulong, bool, string` (plus Vec/Mat/Quaternion/Color) globally, so `data.SyncData("_lastVisitSeconds", ref _lastVisitSeconds)` on a `long` field just works. Two cautions. (a) The raw tick value is unreachable (`NumTicks` and the constructor are internal), so a round trip must go through the public conversions. Recommended pair: `(long)stamp.ToSeconds` ⇄ `CampaignTime.Seconds(seconds)` — `TimeTicksPerSecond = 1000 × 10 = 10,000`, so the only loss is the sub-second remainder of the original stamp (< 1 game second), and ≈7.9×10⁹ fits a `long` with enormous room; both directions are mode-independent. Do **not** round-trip through days/hours: `Days(float)` and `Hours(float)` take a `float`, and at ≈91,000 days a float's spacing is ≈0.0078 day ≈ 11 game minutes, so the value can drift by more than the quarter-hour event period. (b) Container asymmetry: `Dictionary<string, int>`, `Dictionary<string, float>`, `Dictionary<long, int>`, `List<long>`, `List<double>`, `long[]` … are registered, but `Dictionary<string, long>` and `Dictionary<string, double>` are registered by no shipped definer, so a mod wanting them must register them itself (Q8). Anything the mod serializes in its own JSON has to be a number anyway — store seconds and rebuild with `CampaignTime.Seconds`.

Shipped 1.4.8 behaviors (e.g. `PlayerTownVisitCampaignBehavior`) already sync `CampaignTime` through `SyncData`, which is strong practical evidence, but a live save→load round trip of one mod behavior field is what would settle it for mod assemblies.
- **UNCERTAIN**: how large the per-frame `dt` passed to `MapState.OnMapModeTick(float dt)` can become — `MapState` itself does not clamp it, so the cap (engine-side) decides how far `MBCampaignEvent.CheckUpdate`'s catch-up loop can run in one frame, i.e. whether a single frame can ever deliver two `DailyTickEvent` calls after an alt-tab stall. Resolve by tracing where the frame `dt` is produced, or by counting tick-event calls against `CampaignTime.Now` in a test save.

## Q28 — Location and surroundings

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer
**Current settlement of the player party.** The player party is `MobileParty.MainParty` (`public static MobileParty MainParty => Campaign.Current.MainParty`). For it, `MobileParty.CurrentSettlement` (`public Settlement CurrentSettlement { get; set; }`) is non-null **only while the party is physically inside a settlement**; on the campaign map it is null. The public setter is the definition of "inside": it registers the party in the settlement's `Parties`, moves `Position` to the settlement's `GatePosition` (or `PortPosition` when `IsCurrentlyAtSea`), records `LastVisitedSettlement`, and propagates the same value to every attached party (companion parties follow automatically). `MobileParty.LastVisitedSettlement` (`public Settlement LastVisitedSettlement { get; private set; }` — private set) holds the last settlement the party *entered* and is **not** cleared on leaving. The static `Settlement.CurrentSettlement` (public, get-only) answers "where is the player right now": the captor party's settlement when the player is a prisoner (`PlayerCaptivity.CaptorParty.Settlement`) → `PlayerEncounter.EncounterSettlement` (player fighting inside a settlement) → `MobileParty.MainParty.CurrentSettlement` → null. For a specific person use `Hero.CurrentSettlement` (follows `PartyBelongedTo` / the prisoner holder). Enter/leave notifications (`CampaignEvents.BeforeSettlementEnteredEvent`, `SettlementEntered`, `AfterSettlementEntered`, `OnSettlementLeftEvent`) are already documented in Q32 — do not re-derive them.

**"Just nearby" is geometry, not state.** `CurrentSettlement == null` alone only means "in the field". Vanilla's proximity idiom is `LastVisitedSettlement` plus a straight-line squared distance: the public helper `MobilePartyHelper.GetCurrentSettlementOfMobilePartyForAICalculation(MobileParty mobileParty)` returns `CurrentSettlement`, else `LastVisitedSettlement` **only if** `LastVisitedSettlement.Position.DistanceSquared(party.Position) < 1f`, else null; `DefaultPartyHealingModel` uses `< 2f` for "camped at a village". So *near but not inside* ⇔ `party.CurrentSettlement == null && party.LastVisitedSettlement != null && party.LastVisitedSettlement.Position.DistanceSquared(party.Position) < ~2f`.

**Besieging ≠ inside ≠ nearby.** Besieging ⇔ `MobileParty.BesiegerCamp != null` (`public BesiegerCamp BesiegerCamp { get; set; }`, setter propagates to attached parties; vanilla check idiom `MobileParty.MainParty.BesiegerCamp != null`). A besieging party has `CurrentSettlement == null` — the `SiegeEvent` constructor only does `besiegerParty.BesiegerCamp = BesiegerCamp`, never touches `CurrentSettlement`, and vanilla itself resolves the player's siege target as `Settlement.CurrentSettlement ?? PlayerSiege.PlayerSiegeEvent.BesiegedSettlement`. The besieged target from the party: `MobileParty.BesiegedSettlement` (`public Settlement BesiegedSettlement => BesiegerCamp?.SiegeEvent.BesiegedSettlement`; null-safe because `BesiegerCamp.SiegeEvent` is private-set and assigned only in the camp's constructor). From the target side: `Settlement.IsUnderSiege` (`public bool IsUnderSiege => SiegeEvent != null`; covers land sieges **and** naval blockades — `SiegeEvent.IsBlockadeActive` distinguishes them). Parties physically *in* a settlement are enumerated by `Settlement.Parties` (`public MBReadOnlyList<MobileParty> Parties`); a fortification's garrison is *inside* (`GarrisonPartyComponent` sets `mobileParty.CurrentSettlement = settlement`) and keeps it during a siege, and carries `MobileParty.IsGarrison` (`public bool IsGarrison { get; private set; }`). In a battle at a settlement use `MapEvent.MapEventSettlement` (engagement events: see Q23/Q32). `Settlement.SiegeState`/`CurrentSiegeState` is the assault progression (walls vs lord's hall), not a party location — do not use it here.

**Type.** Public get-only flags on `Settlement`: `IsTown` and `IsCastle` delegate to the town component (`Town.IsTown => !_isCastle`, `Town.IsCastle => _isCastle`, with `_is_castle` parsed from `<Town is_castle="true">` in settlements.xml) — so a **castle also has `Settlement.Town != null`**; test `IsTown`/`IsCastle`, never `Town != null`, to tell town from castle. `IsFortification` = `IsTown || IsCastle`; `IsVillage => Village != null`; `IsHideout => Hideout != null`. Villages are first-class `Settlement` objects (own `StringId`, `Position`, `Culture`) that carry a `<Village …>` component; the town/castle a village belongs to is `Village.Bound` (public `Settlement Bound { get; set; }`), the reverse link is `Settlement.BoundVillages` (`public MBReadOnlyList<Village> BoundVillages`), and the town whose market the village feeds is `Village.TradeBound`.

**Culture.** `Settlement.Culture` is a public **field**: `public CultureObject Culture;`. `CultureObject` is sealed and derives from `BasicCultureObject : MBObjectBase`, so its string identity is `StringId` (`public string StringId { get; set; }` on `MBObjectBase`, filled from the XML `id` attribute — vanilla compares `culture.StringId == "empire"`); `Name` is a `TextObject`; `BasicCultureObject` adds `IsMainCulture`, `IsBandit`, `CanHaveSettlement`, `Banner`, colors. Cultures are `<Culture id="empire" …>` objects from `SandBoxCore/ModuleData/spcultures.xml` (registered as `RegisterType<CultureObject>("Culture", "SPCultures", 17u)`); each settlement element carries `culture="Culture.empire"` (XML `Type.stringId` reference form). For behavior conditions: `settlement.Culture.StringId` for string match, or object identity `settlement.Culture == clan.Culture` as vanilla's `DefaultSettlementValueModel` does.

**Distance from party to settlement.** The distance AI and behaviors actually use is path-aware, `float` in campaign-map units: `Campaign.Current.Models.MapDistanceModel.GetDistance(MobileParty fromMobileParty, Settlement toSettlement, bool isTargetingPort, MobileParty.NavigationType customCapability, out float estimatedLandRatio)` (`public abstract float`; pass `mobileParty.NavigationCapability` or `MobileParty.NavigationType.Default` — nested `public enum NavigationType { None = 0, Default = 1, Naval = 2, All = Default | Naval }`). The default model returns a straight `Position.Distance(GatePosition)` when the party's navigation face equals the settlement gate's face, otherwise nearest-entrance distance over a cached settlement graph; unreachable returns `MapDistanceModel.PossibleMaximumMapBoundary = 100000000f` (`public const float`) — test `distance >= 100000000f`, never `==`. The public wrapper that picks gate vs port and handles "party currently inside another settlement" (measures settlement→settlement then) is `DistanceHelper.FindClosestDistanceFromMobilePartyToSettlement(MobileParty fromMobileParty, Settlement toSettlement, MobileParty.NavigationType navCapabilities)` (public static float; `out bool isTargetingPort, out float landRatio` overloads report which). For pure straight-line distance: `party.Position` is a `CampaignVec2` public property with `public float DistanceSquared(CampaignVec2 v)` / `public float DistanceSquared(Vec2 v)` (and `.Distance` twins); measure to `Settlement.GatePosition` (`public CampaignVec2 GatePosition { get; private set; }`) — deserialize sets it equal to `Position` unless `gate_posX/Y` exist, so for villages `GatePosition == Position`. Vanilla thresholds to calibrate: `< 1f`–`< 2f` squared distance = "at/adjacent to the settlement"; 150 path units = the neighborhood radius vanilla scans for "settlements around this caravan".

**Nearest settlements — yes, vanilla helpers exist.** `SettlementHelper` is a `public static class` with `public static Settlement FindNearestSettlementToMobileParty(MobileParty mobileParty, MobileParty.NavigationType navCapabilities, Func<Settlement, bool> condition = null)` plus typed variants that differ in return type: `FindNearestTownToMobileParty` → **`Town`** (null when none!), `FindNearestVillageToMobileParty` → **`Village`**, `FindNearestCastleToMobileParty`/`FindNearestFortificationToMobileParty` → `Settlement`, `FindNearestHideoutToMobileParty` → `Hideout`, and point-based `FindNearestSettlementToPoint(in CampaignVec2 point, Func<Settlement, bool> condition = null)`. They scan all `Settlement.All` using the `DistanceHelper` path distance with the best-distance seed `Campaign.MapDiagonal * 2f`, so "no match" returns null. For *all* settlements within a radius rather than one: `public static int FindNextSettlementAroundMobileParty(MobileParty mobileParty, MobileParty.NavigationType navCapabilities, float maxDistance, int lastIndex, Func<Settlement, bool> condition = null)` returns the next index into `Settlement.All` or `-1` — vanilla loop: seed an `int num = -1`, keep assigning `num = SettlementHelper.FindNextSettlementAroundMobileParty(party, party.NavigationCapability, maxDistance, num, …)` until it returns -1, and use `Settlement.All[num]`.

**A village's produced goods, by item id.** `settlement.IsVillage` → `settlement.Village` (public field) → `Village.VillageType` (public field of type `VillageType : MBObjectBase`; the type's identity is its `StringId`, e.g. `"vineyard"`, `"wheat_farm"`, `"olive_trees"`). The production table is `VillageType.Productions` (`public MBReadOnlyList<(ItemObject, float)> Productions` = item + units per day); `VillageType.PrimaryProduction` (`public ItemObject PrimaryProduction { get; }`) picks the highest `amount × item.Value` entry; `public float GetProductionPerDay(ItemObject item)` (on `VillageType`; returns 0 when the item is not a produce, `ItemCategory` overload also exists); and `public bool IsProducing(ItemObject item)` on `Village`. The items are real `ItemObject`s, so to go *from an item id* combine with Q29's registry lookup: `ItemObject grape = MBObjectManager.Instance.GetObject<ItemObject>("grape"); village.IsProducing(grape); village.VillageType.GetProductionPerDay(grape);`. Concretely, vanilla's `DefaultVillageTypes` creates the `"vineyard"` type and gives it baseline `DefaultItems.Grain` (id `"grain"`, 3/day — the food baseline nearly all village types carry) plus `("grape", 11f)` resolved through `Game.Current.ObjectManager.GetObject<ItemObject>("grape")`, so vineyards produce item **`grape`** 11 units/day and its `PrimaryProduction` is grape (11 × value 20 beats grain). The item `id="grape"` ships in `SandBoxCore/ModuleData/items/horses_and_others.xml` (Goods, `IsFood="true"`, value 20). The settlement→type wiring is the XML reference `<Village village_type="VillageType.silk_plant" bound="Settlement.castle_EN1" …>`, read by `Village.Deserialize`.
