## Q29 — Items, inventory and gold

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer
**Item lookup by string id.** `MBObjectManager.Instance.GetObject<ItemObject>(stringId)` is a plain registry lookup and returns
**null** for an unknown id — no exception, no placeholder object, and null also when no type record for `ItemObject` exists.
`ItemObject` is `sealed`, so the fast sealed branch of the lookup is used. Item ids are the `<Item id="…">` ids of the module
item XML (`xmlschemas/Items.xsd`, `SandBoxCore/ModuleData/items/*.xml`); the type is registered as
`RegisterType<ItemObject>("Item", "Items", 4u)`. A null result must be checked by the caller: `ItemRoster.AddToCounts` wraps
the item in an `EquipmentElement`, which accepts `Item == null`, and the very next cached-stat update reads `item.Value` and
throws a `NullReferenceException` (plus a `Debug.FailedAssert` dialog in a debug build). Vanilla code does not check, e.g.
StoryMode `party.ItemRoster.AddToCounts(MBObjectManager.Instance.GetObject<ItemObject>("fish"), 20)`, which is safe only
because that id ships in the module.

An unknown id becomes a real object only through the **XML/save reference** path: `ReadObjectReferenceFromXml` reads an
attribute of the form `Type.stringId` (`Item.ragged_robes`; `MBInvalidReferenceException` if the dot is missing, null if the
attribute is absent) and calls `GetPresumedObject`, which for `AutoCreate` types (the `RegisterType` default) registers a
placeholder `ItemObject` with `IsReady == false`. When such an id disappears from the XML, load-time repair replaces it:
`ItemRoster.CalculateCachedStatsOnLoad` → `ReplaceInvalidItemsWithTrash` converts each slot holding a not-ready item (or a
not-ready `ItemModifier`) into `DefaultItems.Trash`, and `Hero.CheckInvalidEquipmentsAndReplaceIfNeeded` does the same for the
twelve equipment slots and compensates the party with `PartyBelongedTo?.ItemRoster.AddToCounts(DefaultItems.Trash, 1)`.
A C# `GetObject<ItemObject>` of the same id still returns null — only XML references auto-create.

**The party inventory is the party's, not the hero's.** Items live in an `ItemRoster`, which belongs to a `PartyBase`
(`PartyBase.ItemRoster`, one per party, saved with the game); `MobileParty.ItemRoster => Party.ItemRoster`. For the player that
is `PartyBase.MainParty.ItemRoster` == `MobileParty.MainParty.ItemRoster`. A settlement has its own party roster plus a
separate warehouse `Settlement.Stash` (opened by `OpenScreenAsStash`). A hero owns no `ItemRoster` at all.

**Add / remove.** `public int AddToCounts(ItemObject item, int number)` (public) forwards to
`public int AddToCounts(EquipmentElement rosterElement, int number)`; the return value is the roster slot index, or −1 when
`number == 0` (nothing happens). Negative `number` removes; the element is swap-erased once `Amount <= 0`; subtracting from an
element that is not present raises `Debug.FailedAssert("Trying to delete an element from Item Roster that does not exist!")`
and returns −1 with the roster unchanged. Other mutators: `Add(ItemRosterElement)` / `Add(IEnumerable<ItemRosterElement>)`
(both go through `AddToCounts`), `Remove(ItemRosterElement)` (`AddToCounts(element, -Amount)`),
`RemoveIf(Func<ItemRosterElement, int> match)`, `Clear()`. The roster enforces **no** capacity limit:
`MobileParty.InventoryCapacity` (`InventoryCapacityModel`) and `TotalWeightCarried` are read by the UI and by trade/logic code,
and `AddToCounts` will happily exceed them.

**Count / find.** `public int GetItemNumber(ItemObject item)` returns the amount or 0 (it is `FindIndexOfItem` + amount);
`FindIndexOfItem(ItemObject)` → −1 when absent; `FindIndexOfElement(EquipmentElement)` matches element equality; iteration is
`Count` + indexer + `GetItemAtIndex` / `GetElementNumber` / `GetElementCopyAtIndex`, and cached `TotalValue`, `TotalFood`,
`TradeGoodsTotalValue` are maintained for free. Matching is inconsistent and is a real trap: `GetItemNumber` / `FindIndexOfItem`
match the `ItemObject` only and look at the *first* matching slot, while `AddToCounts` / `FindIndexOfElement` match item **and**
`ItemModifier`. The same weapon with two modifiers occupies two slots and `GetItemNumber` reports only the first.

**Item events.** Editing a roster directly fires nothing on the campaign event bus; the only hook is the per-roster C# event
`ItemRoster.RosterUpdatedEvent` (`delegate void RosterUpdatedEventDelegate(ItemRosterElement item, int count)`). The
event-bus path is `GiveItemAction.ApplyForHeroes(Hero giver, Hero receiver, in ItemRosterElement)` /
`ApplyForParties(PartyBase giverParty, PartyBase receiverParty, in ItemRosterElement)`, which dispatch
`CampaignEventDispatcher.OnHeroOrPartyGaveItem((Hero, PartyBase) giver, (Hero, PartyBase) receiver, ItemRosterElement, bool
showNotification)`, listened to by `DefaultNotificationsCampaignBehavior.OnHeroOrPartyGaveItem` (plain text, and only when
`showNotification` and `Amount > 0`). `GiveItemAction` cannot create or destroy items — both sides must exist — and its
hero↔hero branch subtracts the amount from *both* heroes' party rosters (see Uncertain). The idiomatic vanilla move for
party↔party is plain `AddToCounts(±n)` (`ItemBarterable.Apply` does exactly that).

**Gold is not an item.** There is no gold `ItemObject` (`DefaultItems` exposes Grain, Planks, …, `public static ItemObject Trash`,
and no `id="gold"` exists in any module item XML). Gold is three independent integer stores: `Hero._gold`
(`[SaveableField(650)]`, `public int Gold` whose setter floors at 0, `public void ChangeHeroGold(int)` clamping to
`int.MaxValue`); `MobileParty._partyTradeGold` (`[SaveableField(1956)]`, `public int PartyTradeGold` whose setter floors at 0,
but for a lord party with a leader hero the property **proxies** `LeaderHero.Gold`; `IsLordParty` is
`_partyComponent is LordPartyComponent`); and `SettlementComponent.Gold` (`public int Gold`, `public void ChangeGold(int)`).
`Clan.Gold => Leader?.Gold ?? 0` is only a read-through to the clan leader. The player's main party is itself a lord party led
by the player (`Campaign.OnPlayerCharacterChanged`: `MainParty = MobileParty.CreateParty("player_party_" + …, null)` then
`LordPartyComponent.ConvertPartyToLordParty(MainParty, Hero.MainHero, Hero.MainHero)`), so `PartyBase.MainParty.PartyTradeGold`
and `Hero.MainHero.Gold` are the same number.

**Gold transfer API** (`GiveGoldAction`, all `public static`): `ApplyBetweenCharacters(Hero giverHero, Hero recipientHero,
int amount, bool disableNotification = false)`, `ApplyForCharacterToParty(Hero, PartyBase, int, bool)`,
`ApplyForPartyToCharacter(PartyBase, Hero, int, bool)`, `ApplyForPartyToParty(PartyBase, PartyBase, int, bool)`,
`ApplyForCharacterToSettlement(Hero, Settlement, int, bool)`, `ApplyForSettlementToCharacter(Settlement, Hero, int, bool)`,
`ApplyForSettlementToParty(Settlement, PartyBase, int, bool)`, `ApplyForPartyToSettlement(PartyBase, Settlement, int, bool)`.
All funnel into `private static void ApplyInternal(Hero giverHero, PartyBase giverParty, Hero recipientHero,
PartyBase recipientParty, int goldAmount, bool showQuickInformation, string transactionStringId = "")`, whose semantics:
(1) the amount is **capped at the giver** — a hero giver at `MathF.Min(giverHero.Gold, goldAmount)`, a mobile-party giver at
its `PartyTradeGold`, a settlement giver at its `SettlementComponent.Gold` — and only the clamped amount moves; (2) a **null
giver side creates gold** (no cap, nothing is subtracted) and a **null recipient side destroys it**, which is how vanilla
cheats (`CampaignCheats.AddGoldToHero` → `ApplyBetweenCharacters(null, hero, amount, disableNotification: true)`) and trade
payouts (`InventoryLogic` pays a caravan master) add money out of nothing; (3) there is no recipient ceiling except
`int.MaxValue` in `ChangeHeroGold`, and the 0 floors of the two setters; (4) **every** call dispatches
`CampaignEventDispatcher.OnHeroOrPartyTradedGold((Hero, PartyBase) giver, (Hero, PartyBase) recipient,
(int, string) goldAmount, bool showNotification)`, so the event is unconditional; the visible map notification comes from
`DefaultNotificationsCampaignBehavior.OnHeroOrPartyTradedGold`, which needs `showQuickInformation` — set by the action only
when the main hero or `PartyBase.MainParty` is one of the two sides and `disableNotification` was not passed — and then shows
the coin icon/sound for the giving or the receiving side. Setting `hero.Gold` / `ChangeHeroGold` or
`party.PartyTradeGold` directly bypasses the action, the cap and the event.

**Companion inventory.** A companion in the player's party has no inventory of its own: the only roster a `Hero` ever touches
in its own code is `hero.PartyBelongedTo.ItemRoster`, so everything except worn gear is ordinary party property and is shared
with the whole party. What is per-companion is equipment — `[SaveableProperty(210/220/881)] private Equipment
_battleEquipment/_civilianEquipment/_stealthEquipment`, exposed as `public Equipment BattleEquipment => _battleEquipment ??
Campaign.Current.DeadBattleEquipment;` (and `CivilianEquipment`, `StealthEquipment`; twelve slots each) — filled from the
character template by `public void ResetEquipments()`, plus `public MBList<ItemObject> SpecialItems` for mission/quest gear.
Equipment items are *not* mirrored into the party roster unless code pushes them (`CampaignCheats`, `CharacterData`,
StoryMode quests call `hero.PartyBelongedTo.ItemRoster.AddToCounts(hero.BattleEquipment[i], 1)`). The inventory screen models
this as sides `InventorySide.CivilianEquipment/BattleEquipment/StealthEquipment` against `party.ItemRoster`
(`InventoryScreenHelper.OpenScreenAsInventoryOf(MobileParty party, CharacterObject character)`). When a wanderer companion is
fired, `RemoveCompanionAction` calls `ResetEquipments()`, so gear you handed them is gone; anything still in the party roster
stays with the party, and no gold or item is transferred. A companion who leads their own party gets a brand-new lord party —
`MobilePartyHelper.CreateNewClanMobileParty(Hero hero, Clan clan)` → `SpawnLordParty` — whose `ItemRoster` starts empty;
nothing is moved out of the player's party, so such a companion only takes their equipment with them.

**Companion gold.** A companion owns a normal `Hero._gold`, which starts at 0 (constructor `_gold = 0`) and in vanilla is
funded exactly once: `conversation_companion_hire_on_consequence` pays the wanderer with
`GiveGoldAction.ApplyBetweenCharacters(Hero.MainHero, Hero.OneToOneConversationHero, hiringPrice)` (Q6), so a hired companion
arrives owning the hiring fee, and it is never taken back. While they sit in the player's party nothing spends that purse: party
purchasing power and wages read `MobileParty.PartyTradeGold` (for the player's party that is the player's own gold) or
`Clan.PlayerClan.Gold` (the clan leader, i.e. the player). The companion's own gold becomes meaningful when they are not an
inert party member: they lead a party (their `PartyTradeGold` proxies it, and `CalculatePlunderedGoldAmountFromDefeatedParty`
plunders `DefaultBattleRewardModel.CalculateGoldLossAfterDefeat(hero)` = min(5% of their gold, 10000)); they are ransomed
(`DefaultRansomValueCalculationModel.PrisonerRansomValue` = `sqrt(max(0, hero.Gold)) * 6`); you ask them to lead a party or to
be granted a fief (`CompanionRolesCampaignBehavior` tops their purse up from the main hero and gates fiefs on
`NeededGoldToGrantFief = 20000`); they offer gold in a barter (`GoldBarterBehavior` uses `OffererHero.Gold`, or the party's
`PartyTradeGold` when the offerer has no hero); or they ever lead a clan (`Clan.Gold` reads the clan leader's purse). To fund
one deliberately: `GiveGoldAction.ApplyBetweenCharacters(Hero.MainHero, companionHero, amount)`.

| actor | gold — meaningful? API | item — meaningful? API |
| --- | --- | --- |
| player | yes; one store, `Hero.MainHero.Gold` == `PartyBase.MainParty.PartyTradeGold`; `GiveGoldAction.Apply…` (capped, notified), direct `Hero.Gold`/`ChangeHeroGold` (uncapped, silent) | yes; `PartyBase.MainParty.ItemRoster.AddToCounts(item, ±n)`, `GetItemNumber(item)`; `InventoryCapacity` is advisory |
| companion in the player's party | purse exists but is inert: `companion.Gold` is only read by ransom/plunder/barter/party-leader models, never spent by party expenses | no store of their own: shared `companion.PartyBelongedTo.Party.ItemRoster`; personal gear = `BattleEquipment`/`CivilianEquipment`/`StealthEquipment` + `SpecialItems` |
| companion not in the player's party (wanderer, or leading their own lord party) | yes: their own `Hero.Gold`, and for their own party `party.PartyTradeGold` **is** that number | own party roster `MobileParty.MainParty`→`theirParty.ItemRoster` (fresh, empty at `CreateNewClanMobileParty`); a partyless wanderer has only equipment slots |
| world (create / destroy) | yes: `ApplyBetweenCharacters(null, hero, n)` creates, `ApplyBetweenCharacters(hero, null, n)` destroys; always capped on the giving side | no create/destroy API: vanilla creates and deletes items by `ItemRoster.AddToCounts(item, ±n)` on a party roster (StoryMode quests, `CampaignCheats`); `GiveItemAction` only moves between two existing sides |
| settlement | `SettlementComponent.Gold` via `ApplyForCharacterToSettlement` / `ApplyForSettlementToCharacter` / `ChangeGold(int)` | `Settlement.Stash` warehouse roster plus the settlement's own `Settlement.Party.ItemRoster` |

### Uncertain
- **UNCERTAIN**: `GiveItemAction.ApplyInternal` subtracts `itemRosterElement.Amount` from the giver's **and** the receiver's party roster in the two-hero branch, which reads as a vanilla bug (a hero→hero gift removes the item from both parties). Resolve by finding a vanilla caller that passes two heroes with different parties (`ItemBarterable.Apply` does when the other side has no party) and testing one gift in game, or by reading the unreleased source.
- **UNCERTAIN**: which object the party inventory screen actually writes when gear is moved — `InventoryLogic.PartyEquipment` keeps `Dictionary<CharacterObject, Equipment[3]>` copies and `ResetEquipment()` writes them back with `character.First*Equipment.FillFrom(equipment)`, while the saved per-hero store is `Hero._battleEquipment`. Resolve by tracing the apply path in the Native/SandBox inventory screen logic (or by giving a mod companion gear, saving, and dumping `hero.BattleEquipment`).
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether `Debug.FailedAssert("Trying to delete an element from Item Roster that does not exist!")` is visible/abortive in the shipping build or a no-op log line, which decides how defensive the mod must be before removing an item. Resolve by testing one bad removal in game, or by checking the `Debug` build configuration of TaleWorlds.Core.
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether any DLC or module behavior outside the locally decompiled DLLs spends a companion's own gold while they are in the player's party (`GoldBarterBehavior`, ransom, plunder, `CompanionRolesCampaignBehavior` and clan finance are the only uses found). Resolve by grepping every shipped module DLL for `.Gold` and `ChangeHeroGold`.
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether `MBObjectManager.GetObject<ItemObject>` of an id that exists only as a presumed (XML-created, `IsReady == false`) object ever returns that placeholder in a live campaign, or whether presumed items are always registered by the time a C# lookup could see them. Resolve by dumping `GetObjectTypeList<ItemObject>()` for not-ready entries at runtime.

## Q30 — Debug console commands

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer
**Registration is one attribute on one static method.** A command is a method carrying
`TaleWorlds.Library.CommandLineFunctionality.CommandLineArgumentFunction` — a public class nested in the static class
`CommandLineFunctionality`, derived from `Attribute`, with public fields `Name` and `GroupName` and the constructor
`CommandLineArgumentFunction(string name, string groupname)`. With `using TaleWorlds.Library;` the vanilla spelling is
`[CommandLineFunctionality.CommandLineArgumentFunction("add_gold_to_hero", "campaign")]`. There is no XML, no
`SubModule.xml` entry and no registration call a mod has to make:

```csharp
[CommandLineFunctionality.CommandLineArgumentFunction("behavior_dump", "albocarius")]
public static string BehaviorDump(List<string> strings)
{
    return "...";   // the returned string is what the console prints
}
```

**Method signature.** Required: `static`, return type exactly `string`, and a parameter list bindable to
`Func<List<string>, string>` — in practice exactly one `List<string>`. All 135 attributed methods in the locally decompiled
sources have the identical shape `public static string Name(List<string> strings)`. The scan is
`GetMethods(BindingFlags.Static | BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.NonPublic)`, so `public` is convention, not a rule:
`internal` and `private` static commands register just as well. The parameter list itself is never validated (see Uncertain).

**The declaring class need be neither static nor public.** The scan walks every type of the assembly
(`assembly.GetTypesSafe()`) and binds the method statically, so it can live anywhere: `Mission` is
`public sealed class Mission` and hosts `mission.flee_enemies` → `public static string MakeEnemiesFleeCheat(…)`;
`GauntletUISubModule` is a `public class … : MBSubModuleBase` and hosts `chatlog.clear` →
`public static string ClearChatLog(List<string> strings)`. A mod may therefore put commands straight on its
`MBSubModuleBase` subclass or on a plain static helper class. Instance methods and open generic types are not usable — the
delegate is created with no target instance.

**Discovery: every loaded assembly that references TaleWorlds.Library.**
`CommandLineFunctionality.CollectCommandLineFunctions()` iterates `AppDomain.CurrentDomain.GetAssemblies()` — vanilla,
module and mod assemblies alike, anything already loaded — and keeps an assembly when `CheckAssemblyReferencesThis` says
yes: the assembly *is* TaleWorlds.Library, or one of its `GetReferencedAssemblies()` entries (direct references only, not
transitive) is named `TaleWorlds.Library`. Using the attribute creates that reference, so a normal mod assembly qualifies by
itself; an assembly that never references TaleWorlds.Library (the netstandard2.0 Core project, PROJECT rule 4) can never
host commands. Inside a qualifying assembly every static method with the attribute (`inherit: false`, and only the *first*
attribute instance is examined) whose `ReturnType == typeof(string)` is registered. Module assemblies are the same kind of
assembly a mod ships: `SandBox.View` provides `campaign.kill_hero` → `public static string KillHero(List<string> strings)`
and StoryMode provides `storymode.add_family_members` → `public static string AddFamilyMembers(List<string> strings)`. The
consequence of `GetAssemblies()` is load order — an assembly loaded after the scan is invisible to it. Module and submodule
assemblies are loaded at start-up (`ModuleHelper.InitializeModules(Utilities.GetModulesNames(), …)`, then
`Module.LoadSubModules`), but the scan is triggered from native code, so its exact moment is not visible in the managed
sources (see Uncertain).

**From the managed table to the console window.** The discovered keys are pushed into the engine by the internal callback
`ManagedExtensions.CollectCommandLineFunctions()`, marked `[EngineCallback(null, false)]`, which calls
`TaleWorlds.Engine.Utilities.AddCommandLineFunction(string concatName)` per name; that forwards to
`IUtil.AddCommandLineFunction` (`[EngineMethod("add_command_line_function", false, null, false)]`). Completion reads the same
native registry (`IUtil.GetPossibleCommandLineStartingWith(string command, int index)`,
`[EngineMethod("get_possible_command_line_starting_with", …)]`, wrapped by `Utilities.GetPossibleCommandLineStartingWith`),
and any code can run a command line with `Utilities.ExecuteCommandLineCommand(string command)` →
`IUtil.ExecuteCommandLineCommand` (`[EngineMethod("execute_command_line_command", …)]`). Both
`CommandLineFunctionality.CollectCommandLineFunctions()` and `Utilities.AddCommandLineFunction` are public, so a mod can
re-scan and push names itself; re-scanning is cheap and safe because `AllFunctions` is a static dictionary and only names not
already in it are returned and added.

**Naming: `group.command`.** The key is literally `GroupName + "." + Name`, and that full key is what the player types —
group, dot, command. The group is free-form and is the only namespacing mechanism. Sixteen groups and 134 distinct commands
appear in the local sources:

| group | count | example |
|---|---|---|
| `campaign` | 89 | `campaign.add_gold_to_hero` |
| `naval` | 14 | `naval.add_ship_to_player` (NavalDLC — DLC, not an API to copy) |
| `mission` | 12 | `mission.flee_enemies` |
| `console` | 3 | `console.clear` |
| `localization` | 3 | `localization.change_language` |
| `chatlog` | 2 | `chatlog.clear` |
| `facegen` | 2 | `facegen.show_debug` |
| `mp_host` | 2 | `mp_host.end_warmup` |
| `mp_perks` | 2 | `mp_perks.raise_event` |
| `ai`, `game`, `module`, `scoreboard`, `storymode`, `ui` | 1 each | `ui.toggle_ui`, `module.get_item_mesh_names` |

Registration is first-wins (`if (!AllFunctions.ContainsKey(text))`): a mod cannot override `campaign.add_gold_to_hero`, and
two mods choosing the same `group.command` silently lose the race. So the group must be unique to the mod
(`albocarius.…`), lower-case snake_case like every vanilla name.

**Argument parsing: what the method receives.** Dispatch goes through
`CommandLineFunctionality.CallFunction(string concatName, string concatArguments, out bool found)` (plus a `List<string>`
overload). `concatName` is the full `group.command` key; `concatArguments` is the remainder of the typed line, split by
`concatArguments.Split(new char[1] { ' ' })` — one space, no quote handling, so `a  b` yields an empty entry, and an empty
argument string yields an **empty** list rather than one empty string. Every token is a raw string: the command parses
numbers itself (`int.TryParse`) and multi-word names use the pipe separator (`CampaignCheats.CheatNameSeparator = "|"`, read
back by `CampaignCheats.GetSeparatedNames` / `ConcatenateString`). The vanilla argument hygiene is
`CheckParameters(List<string> strings, int ParameterCount)`, `CheckHelp(List<string> strings)` (`help` is the reserved first
token, `CampaignCheats.Help = "help"`) and a returned usage line — none of it automatic:
`GauntletUISubModule.SetCanFocusWhileInMission` reads `strings[0]` with no guard, so a bare
`chatlog.can_focus_while_in_mission` is an `IndexOutOfRangeException`. An unregistered name returns
`"Could not find the command " + concatName` with `found = false`; the native console answers its own `Unknown command.` for
names only it knows. `CommandLineFunctionality.HasFunctionForCommand(string command)` is the public probe, and
`GameStateManager.StateActivateCommand` shows managed code invoking a command by name
(`CommandLineFunctionality.CallFunction(GameStateManager.StateActivateCommand, "", out var _)`), set to
`"state_string.benchmark_start"` by the options screen.

**Output = the return value.** The `string` a command returns is its printed result; vanilla commands return player-facing
text (`"UI is now disabled."`, `"Chatlog cleared!"`, `"Cheat mode is not enabled."`) and multi-line usage text with embedded
`\n` (`Mission.MakeTeamFleeCheat`). A command that wants to write *while* it runs calls `MBDebug.EchoCommandWindow(string
content)`, which forwards to `IDebug.EchoCommandWindow` (`[EngineMethod("echo_command_window", false, null, false)]`); the
same write is itself a command, `console.echo_command_window`, which returns `""`. `console.clear` (`MBDebug.ClearConsole`)
clears the window. The log is a separate pipe: `MBDebug.Print(string message, int logLevel = 0, …)` is unconditional, while
`MBDebug.ConsolePrint` is `[Conditional("_RGL_KEEP_ASSERTS")]` and is therefore compiled away in a normal mod build — code
calling it produces nothing in game.

**Availability in a normal, non-developer game.** Nothing on the managed side gates it: registration and dispatch never
consult cheat or development mode, and the window itself is a native feature — `TaleWorlds.Native.dll` carries the console
title string `RGL Command line console`, the widget strings `Input`, `Clear`, `- History -`, `input_popup`, and native-only
messages such as `Unknown command.`, `Invalid number of arguments. Expecting 0 or 1` and
`Development mode needs to be enabled.` for the engine's own command set. What *is* gated is the behaviour of most vanilla
commands: `Game.Current.CheatMode` → `GameManager.CheatMode` → `MBGameManager.CheatMode` → `NativeConfig.CheatMode`,
refreshed in `NativeConfig.OnConfigChanged()` from `IConfig.GetCheatMode()` / `IConfig.GetDevelopmentMode()`
(`[EngineMethod("get_cheat_mode", false, null, false)]`, `[EngineMethod("get_development_mode", …)]`), i.e. from the engine
config file whose keys `cheat_mode` and `development_mode` live only in the native DLL. Each command then enforces its own
policy — `CampaignCheats.CheckCheatUsage(ref string ErrorType)` yields `Cheat mode is disabled!` when
`Game.Current.CheatMode` is false, and `Mission.MakeEnemiesFleeCheat` returns `Cheat mode is not enabled.`. **How a normal
player opens the window — key, config entry or launcher option — could not be established from the local data** (see
Uncertain): `DebugHotKeyCategory` declares the ids `EngineInterfaceHotkeyToggleConsole` and
`EngineInterfaceHotkeyShowConsoleManager` but never calls `RegisterDebugHotkey` for them, no console binding exists in any
module XML, and `Module.ProcessApplicationArguments` understands only the `/dedicated…` server switches — other launch
arguments are read ad hoc (`MBDebug.TestModeEnabled = Utilities.CommandLineArgumentExists("/runTest")`), and no shipped
launcher DLL mentions a cheat or dev flag. For this mod: treat the console as a developer/QA surface, never as a player
feature, and gate any state-mutating command yourself. The in-game *cheat menu* is a different thing and is gamepad-only:
`ActionCampaignOptionData("EnableCheats", …)` is yielded only under `if (TaleWorlds.InputSystem.Input.IsGamepadActive)` and
runs `DefaultCampaignOptionsProvider.ExecuteEnableCheats` → `mapState.Handler.OnGameplayCheatsEnabled()` →
`MapScreen.HandleCheatMenuInput` / `OpenGameplayCheats` (the `Native/ModuleData/consoles.xml` text documents the
L1 + R2 + Down combo). The PC keyboard path is the console, not that menu.

**Commands on the campaign map, and what they see.** Yes: the 89-command `campaign` group exists to be typed on the map, and
a command body runs inside the game's own managed context with the same live objects the running game uses —
`campaign.add_gold_to_hero` ends in `GiveGoldAction.ApplyBetweenCharacters(null, obj, result, disableNotification: true)`, an
ordinary campaign mutation that the game and the save both see. What is live depends on the game state, and the command must
guard it: `Campaign.Current` is `public static Campaign Current { get; private set; }`, assigned in
`Campaign.SetLoadingParameters(GameLoadingType)` and set back to null in `Campaign.OnDestroy()`, so in the main menu, a
custom battle or a multiplayer game it is null and vanilla answers `Campaign was not started.`
(`CampaignCheats.CheckCheatUsage`, whose other failure is `Cheat mode is disabled!`). In a loaded single-player campaign it
is the live campaign object whether the map or a mission is on screen; `Mission.Current` is the other state handle, and
`Mission.MakeEnemiesFleeCheat` additionally refuses when `GameNetwork.IsClientOrReplay`. Whether campaign simulation keeps
ticking while the window is open is native-side and unverified (Uncertain).

**Use in this mod (SPEC Track R, R10).** Put the commands in `src/AlbocariusCompanions.Game` — the only project allowed to
reference TaleWorlds — as `public static string X(List<string> strings)` methods under a mod-unique group (`albocarius`, so
`albocarius.behavior_dump`), validate the arguments, guard on `Campaign.Current` / `Game.Current.CheatMode`, return one
summary line and echo progress with `MBDebug.EchoCommandWindow`.

The managed layer declares but never binds `EngineInterfaceHotkeyToggleConsole` / `EngineInterfaceHotkeyShowConsoleManager`, and no shipped XML contains a console binding. Resolve on the Windows test machine (`ssh aliboron@100.94.114.51`): start the game and try `` ` ``, Ctrl+``, F12 and Ctrl+Shift+C; then inspect `%USERPROFILE%\Documents\Mount and Blade II Bannerlord\config\engine_config.txt` for `cheat_mode` / `development_mode`, and try `campaign.add_gold_to_hero 1000`.
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether the window opens at all in a plain retail game with `cheat_mode` and `development_mode` both false, or whether the native side refuses it — the native strings prove the config keys and a `Development mode needs to be enabled.` message but not whether that gate covers the window, the native commands only, or specific managed commands. Same test run resolves it.
- **UNCERTAIN**: when the native engine calls the `[EngineCallback]` `ManagedExtensions.CollectCommandLineFunctions` relative to `Module.LoadSubModules`, i.e. whether a mod's commands are found in the first scan. Resolve with one attributed command in the mod build: type `albocarius.behavior_dump`; if it is missing, call `CommandLineFunctionality.CollectCommandLineFunctions()` and `TaleWorlds.Engine.Utilities.AddCommandLineFunction(name)` from `OnSubModuleLoad` and retest.
- **UNCERTAIN**: what happens to an attributed method whose parameter list is not `List<string>` — only the return type is checked, and the `Delegate.CreateDelegate` cast sits outside any try/catch, so either the exception escapes the whole scan (losing later commands) or the engine tolerates it. Resolve by shipping one deliberately bad method in the mod and checking whether the game still starts and whether the other commands of the same assembly work.
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether the native console prints the returned string verbatim (including embedded `\n`) and whether mod names appear in its completion list (`IUtil.GetPossibleCommandLineStartingWith`). Resolve in the same session: `mission.flee_team help` returns multi-line usage text, then press Tab after typing `albocarius.`.
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether campaign simulation keeps ticking while the console window is open, and on which thread the command body actually runs (all vanilla bodies touch `Campaign.Current` / `Mission.Current` objects directly, which implies the game thread but does not prove it). Resolve by watching a party's position or a tick counter with the window open, or by timing `Campaign.Current.GameTick` before and after a command.

## Q31 — Misc conditions

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer

Three independent state reads on `Campaign.Current` objects. None of them needs a game-model patch or an action call on the read path, and one of them (the clan tier) has **no** public write path at all.

#### 1. Clan tier of the player's clan

The API is `Clan.PlayerClan.Tier` — `Clan.PlayerClan` is `Campaign.Current.PlayerDefaultFaction` (`public static Clan PlayerClan`), the clan whose string id is `player_faction`, and it is assigned exactly once during campaign setup, so the object identity is stable for the whole campaign (the clan stays the same object even after the player joins a kingdom — only `MapFaction` changes, see §2):

```csharp
Clan.PlayerClan.Tier                              // public get, private set
Clan.PlayerClan.Renown                            // public float get/set
Campaign.Current.Models.ClanTierModel.MinClanTier // vanilla 0
Campaign.Current.Models.ClanTierModel.MaxClanTier // vanilla 6
```

| read | signature | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tier | `Clan.PlayerClan.Tier` | `public int Tier { get; private set; }` — **no public setter**: read-only for mods |
| range | `ClanTierModel.MinClanTier` / `MaxClanTier` (`public abstract int { get; }`) | the private setter clamps every assignment into that window, so the real range is model-defined; `DefaultClanTierModel` = **0 … 6** |
| renown | `Clan.PlayerClan.Renown` (`public float Renown { get; set; }`) | progress inside the tier; writing it does **not** move the tier |
| next tier | `Clan.PlayerClan.RenownRequirementForNextTier` (`public int`) | = `ClanTierModel.GetRequiredRenownForTier(Tier + 1)`; vanilla thresholds `0 / 50 / 150 / 350 / 900 / 2350 / 6150` indexed by tier |
| tier perks | `Clan.PlayerClan.CompanionLimit` (Q6: `tier + 3` + perks), `Clan.PlayerClan.WarPartyLimit` | both `public int`, recomputed from `ClanTierModel` on every read |

Starting value and range in vanilla: the player clan is declared `tier="0"` in `spclans.xml`, `Clan.Deserialize` reads that attribute (a **missing** attribute would default to `1`) and then seeds `Renown` with `ClanTierModel.CalculateInitialRenown(this)`, which for tier 0 draws in `[0, 30)` — below the tier-1 threshold of 50, so a new game really is tier 0. Tier moves only through `Clan.AddRenown(float value, bool shouldNotify = true)`: it ignores `value <= 0`, adds renown, recomputes `ClanTierModel.CalculateTier(this)` and assigns `Tier` **only when the new tier is higher**, then fires `CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance.OnClanTierChanged` → `CampaignEvents.ClanTierIncrease` (`public static IMbEvent<Clan, bool>`; subscription mechanics in Q32). Besides save/`Deserialize` load, the only other writes to the private setter are the two clan factories `Clan.CreateSettlementRebelClan` (tier = `RebelClanStartingTier`, vanilla 3) and `Clan.CreateCompanionToLordClan` (tier = `CompanionToLordClanStartingTier`, vanilla 2). `Clan.ResetClanRenown()` is the one code path that can lower a tier, and it has no call site anywhere in the decompiled assemblies — in practice the tier only ever rises. Consequence for our condition system: **read `Clan.PlayerClan.Tier`, never try to set it.** Vanilla reads the same value as `Clan.PlayerClan.Tier <= Campaign.Current.Models.ClanTierModel.MinClanTier`. One quirk: the player clan is `is_minor_faction="true"`, which changes only the vanilla *party*-limit branch (`MathF.Clamp(tier, 1, 4)` instead of the 1/2/3 ladder used for ordinary clans), not the companion limit.

#### 2. Is the player at war — with anyone, and with one given faction

**A clan without a kingdom counts as a full faction.** `Clan.MapFaction` is `Kingdom ?? this` and `Clan.IsMapFaction => _kingdom == null`, so while the player has no kingdom the clan itself is the map faction that carries stance links, appears in other factions' `FactionsAtWarWith`, and can be a war party — no fallback, no special case. Vanilla proves it with its own war declarations: both `BeHostileAction` and `ChangeCrimeRatingAction` pass `Hero.MainHero.MapFaction` straight into `DeclareWarAction`, and that is a bare clan object in a kingdom-less game.

| question | call |
| --- | --- |
| at war with a given faction? | `Hero.MainHero.MapFaction.IsAtWarWith(other)` — interface member `bool IFaction.IsAtWarWith(IFaction other)`; `Clan.IsAtWarWith` and `Kingdom.IsAtWarWith` both just forward to `FactionManager.IsAtWarAgainstFaction(IFaction faction1, IFaction faction2)` (`public static bool`, argument order irrelevant, null-safe) |
| at war with anybody? | `Hero.MainHero.MapFaction.FactionsAtWarWith` (`public MBReadOnlyList<IFaction>`, and `MBReadOnlyList<T> : List<T>` so LINQ works); it is rebuilt by `IFaction.UpdateFactionsAtWarWith()`. Kingdom-only view: `Helpers.FactionHelper.GetEnemyKingdoms(IFaction faction)`; vanilla also simply loops `Kingdom.All` and tests `Clan.PlayerClan.MapFaction.IsAtWarWith(kingdom)` (`FactionHelper.CanPlayerOfferMercenaryService`) |
| declared war, or "always at war"? | `FactionManager.IsAtConstantWarAgainstFaction(IFaction, IFaction)` (`public static bool`) or `DiplomacyModel.GetShallowDiplomaticStance(IFaction, IFaction)` |
| stance detail | `IFaction.GetStanceWith(IFaction other)` → `StanceLink.IsAtWar` / `StanceLink.IsNeutral` (`public bool`); the backing `StanceType` property is `internal`, so do not depend on it |

Four things a condition system must not get wrong:

- **`FactionsAtWarWith` is not a "wars I declared" list.** `Clan.UpdateFactionsAtWarWith()` walks `Kingdom.All` **and** `Clan.All` and adds every non-eliminated faction for which `IsAtWarWith` is true — bandit clans included. It is refreshed for every kingdom and clan on new game, game load, clan creation and kingdom change (`CampaignFactionManagerBehaviour.RefreshFactionsAtWarWith`), so a fresh neutral player already has a long list. Vanilla always filters it: `x.IsKingdomFaction` (`FactionHelper.GetEnemyKingdoms`), `!GetShallowDiplomaticStance(...).HasValue` (`KingdomManager` when a clan founds a kingdom and inherits its wars), `!IsBanditFaction` (encyclopedia "Enemy" filter).
- **Bandit pairs are constant war, not wars.** `DefaultDiplomacyModel.GetShallowDiplomaticStance` returns War whenever exactly one side `IsBanditFaction`; `IsAtConstantWar` adds outlaw minor factions against a same-culture kingdom (the player clan is `is_minor_faction="true"` but *not* `is_outlaw`, so only the bandit branch applies to the player). `FactionManager.IsAtWarAgainstFaction` short-circuits to `true` for those pairs and never consults a stance link — "at war with looters" is permanently true. The same call returns `false` for a null, identical or `IsEliminated` counterpart.
- **The read has a side effect.** For a pair that has no stored stance, `IsAtWarAgainstFaction` falls through to `FactionManager.GetStanceLinkInternal(IFaction, IFaction)`, which *creates and stores* a `StanceLink` (skipped for eliminated and shallow-stance pairs); the backing `_stances` field is `[SaveableField(20)]`, so a query writes a record that lands in the save. Harmless, but the query is not pure.
- **Writing is a different pair of doors** (relevant to Q32's event work): `FactionManager.DeclareWar(IFaction, IFaction)` / `FactionManager.SetNeutral(IFaction, IFaction)` change the stance silently and no-op for identical or shallow-stance pairs, whereas the `DeclareWarAction.ApplyBy…(IFaction faction1, IFaction faction2)` family routes through `FactionManager.DeclareWar` **and** fires `OnWarDeclared` → `CampaignEvents.WarDeclared` (`IMbEvent<IFaction, IFaction, DeclareWarAction.DeclareWarDetail>`); the reverse is `MakePeaceAction` → `CampaignEvents.MakePeace`. Player-scale triggers: `BeHostileAction` (main party attacks a neutral party → `DeclareWarAction.ApplyByPlayerHostility(attackerParty.MapFaction, defenderParty.MapFaction)`) and `ChangeCrimeRatingAction.Apply(IFaction faction, float deltaCrimeRating, bool showNotification = true)`, which past `CrimeModel.DeclareWarCrimeRatingThreshold` declares war on the offending faction but only while `Hero.MainHero.MapFaction.Leader == Hero.MainHero`.

#### 3. Is a specific hero in the player's party — and how that differs from clan membership

Party membership is **roster** state; clan membership is a **field on the hero**. They are separate axes and neither implies the other.

| test | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `hero.PartyBelongedTo == MobileParty.MainParty` | the hero is a member of the player's party. `public MobileParty PartyBelongedTo { get; private set; }`; null when the hero leads no party |
| `MobileParty.MainParty.MemberRoster.Contains(hero.CharacterObject)` | the same fact read from the other side: `public bool TroopRoster.Contains(CharacterObject character)`. Rosters are keyed on `CharacterObject`, never on `Hero`, so always convert with `hero.CharacterObject` |
| `Helpers.HeroHelper.IsCompanionInPlayerParty(Hero hero)` | `public static bool` vanilla helper: false unless `hero.IsPlayerCompanion`, then `hero.PartyBelongedTo == MobileParty.MainParty` — companion-only, so it misses family/lord members of the party |
| `hero.PartyBelongedToAsPrisoner == PartyBase.MainParty` | the hero is the party's **prisoner**: `PartyBelongedTo` is null and the hero is in `MainParty.PrisonRoster`, not `MemberRoster`; `Hero.IsPrisoner` reflects `HeroState` |
| `hero.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan`, `hero.IsPlayerCompanion`, `Clan.PlayerClan.Companions` / `.Heroes` / `.AliveLords` | clan membership (`Hero.Clan` getter returns `CompanionOf ?? _clan`, so hired companions count). Says nothing about where the hero physically is |

Why the two party tests agree: the roster is the single source of truth. `TroopRoster.AddToCounts(CharacterObject character, int count, bool insertAtFront = false, int woundedCount = 0, int xpChange = 0, bool removeDepleted = true, int index = -1)` delegates to `TroopRoster.AddToCountsAtIndex`, which — for a hero element whose roster has an `OwnerParty` — calls `PartyBase.OnHeroAdded(Hero, TroopRoster)` / `OnHeroRemoved(Hero, TroopRoster)`; member rosters route through `MobileParty.OnHeroAdded/OnHeroRemoved(Hero)` to `Hero.OnAddedToParty(MobileParty)` / `Hero.OnRemovedFromParty(MobileParty)`, the only writers of `PartyBelongedTo` (they also clear `Hero.StayingInSettlement`, Q3/Q19); prison rosters instead call `Hero.OnAddedToPartyAsPrisoner(PartyBase)`. So `hero.PartyBelongedTo == MobileParty.MainParty` ⟺ the hero occupies a slot in `MainParty.MemberRoster` with count > 0, and the sanctioned way to move a hero is `AddHeroToPartyAction.Apply(Hero hero, MobileParty party, bool showNotification = true)` (Q6) or a plain `MemberRoster.AddToCounts(hero.CharacterObject, ±1)` — never the private setter. Wounded heroes still count as present: the roster stores a wounded count per element and `Hero.IsWounded` is a separate flag (health reads in Q19/Q20).

Where the axes differ, straight out of vanilla:

- **in the player's clan but not in the party**: the companion-rejoin dialog condition is `(IsPlayerCompanion || Clan == Clan.PlayerClan) && PartyBelongedTo != MobileParty.MainParty && (PartyBelongedTo == null || !PartyBelongedTo.IsCaravan)` plus a `Hero.GovernorOf` case for a companion governing a town; dismissed companions sit with `PartyBelongedTo == null` and a non-null `StayingInSettlement` (Q3/Q19). Its consequence calls `AddHeroToPartyAction.Apply(Hero.OneToOneConversationHero, MobileParty.MainParty)`.
- **in the party but not in the clan**: `AddHeroToPartyAction.Apply` never touches `Clan` or `CompanionOf`, and vanilla uses it for foreign heroes — a freed lord joining the player party (`PrisonBreakCampaignBehavior`), a FamilyFeud culprit handed over (`FamilyFeudIssueBehavior`), a captured bandit held for bounty (`BanditInteractionsCampaignBehavior`). The reverse transition is just as visible: turning a companion into a lord does `RemoveCompanionAction.ApplyByByTurningToLord(Hero.MainHero.Clan, hero)` followed by `MobileParty.MainParty.MemberRoster.AddToCounts(hero.CharacterObject, -1)`. Only `Hero.IsPlayerCompanion` (`CompanionOf == Clan.PlayerClan`) marks the companion subset, and `Clan.PlayerClan.Companions` is the roster Q2's `too_many_companions()` counts.

Recipe for our conditions: "mine" = `hero.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan || hero.IsPlayerCompanion`; "here right now" = `hero.PartyBelongedTo == MobileParty.MainParty` (or the `MemberRoster.Contains` twin); add `hero.PartyBelongedToAsPrisoner == PartyBase.MainParty` when prisoners should count — that exact pair is what vanilla `IssueManager` tests to decide whether an issue owner is travelling with the player.

### Uncertain

- **UNCERTAIN**: whether the player clan's tier is really 0 for *every* campaign start — `spclans.xml` says `tier="0"` and `CalculateInitialRenown` draws renown 0…29 (below the tier-1 threshold 50), but a scenario/mod `spclans` override, or a `tier` attribute in another loaded clan file, could raise it, and `Clan.Deserialize` defaults to **1** when the attribute is absent. Resolve by logging `Clan.PlayerClan.Tier` and `Clan.PlayerClan.Renown` from an `OnNewGameCreatedEvent` listener plus dumping the loaded `Clan.All` tiers.
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether `FactionsAtWarWith` can go stale between refreshes — `SetStance` and `AddStance` refresh both sides, and `CampaignFactionManagerBehaviour` refreshes all factions on the listed events, but a link created lazily by a *read* (`GetStanceLinkInternal`) with a Neutral default is not pushed into anyone's list. Resolve at runtime by comparing `Clan.PlayerClan.MapFaction.FactionsAtWarWith` against a full `Kingdom.All`/`Clan.All` scan with `IsAtWarWith`, over several in-game days and after a rebel clan spawns.
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether a lazily created `StanceLink` (from a pure query) can later be read as a "real" war by diplomacy or UI that walks stance links instead of the model — e.g. alliance/peace-value or war-score code and the encyclopedia diplomacy tab. Resolve by dumping `Helpers.FactionHelper.GetStances(Clan.PlayerClan.MapFaction)` before and after a single `IsAtWarWith` call and comparing the encyclopedia "Diplomacy" filters.
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether `hero.PartyBelongedTo` can ever disagree with `MainParty.MemberRoster.Contains(hero.CharacterObject)` — the hero hooks are skipped when the roster has no `OwnerParty` (`TroopRoster.CreateDummyTroopRoster`, used by party-screen view models), so adding a hero to a detached roster moves nothing, and copy-in/copy-out between a dummy and a real roster is untested. Resolve by asserting the two views against each other for every hero in `Hero.All` during a long modded session.
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether a companion who is attached to a caravan or garrison party still counts against the companion limit and should count as "in the player's party" for our conditions — Q2's `too_many_companions()` is clan-side (`Clan.PlayerClan.Companions.Count >= Clan.PlayerClan.CompanionLimit`), while the rejoin condition above explicitly excludes `PartyBelongedTo.IsCaravan`. Resolve by assigning a companion a caravan role, then reading `hero.Clan`, `hero.PartyBelongedTo`, `Clan.PlayerClan.Companions.Count` and `MainParty.MemberRoster.Contains(hero.CharacterObject)` together in-game.

## Q32 — Game events (part 2)

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer

All members below are `public static IMbEvent<…>` properties on `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignEvents` unless noted; subscribe them in `CampaignBehaviorBase.RegisterEvents()` with `CampaignEvents.X.AddNonSerializedListener(this, handler)` exactly as in Q8/Q23. `CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance.Fire…` call sites are internal fan-out, not a public API. Two of the nine events (unpaid wages, morale change) have **no** event at all — only state + tick hooks.

| event | member (or other hook) | args | player / clan check | timing vs state change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| wages unpaid | **no event**; poll `DailyTickClanEvent` (or `DailyTickPartyEvent`) and read `MobileParty.HasUnpaidWages` | `(Clan clan)` / `(MobileParty party)` | `clan == Clan.PlayerClan` (then `MobileParty.MainParty.HasUnpaidWages > 0f`); party variant also needs `party.IsMainParty` | inside the daily clan tick, after `DefaultClanFinanceModel.ApplyMoraleEffect` writes `HasUnpaidWages` (unpaid fraction 0…1) and pushes the no-wage morale hit; order vs other `DailyTickClanEvent` listeners unspecified |
| food ran out / starvation | `OnMainPartyStarvingEvent`; general daily hook `OnPartyConsumedFoodEvent` | none / `(MobileParty party)` | starving event needs none (fired only when `mobileParty.IsMainParty`); state is `PartyBase.IsStarving` (`RemainingFoodPercentage < 0`) | after `RemainingFoodPercentage` is updated in `FoodConsumptionBehavior.DailyTickParty` (`DailyTickPartyEvent`); the starving event additionally requires the party to have been starving *before* that day's consumption too, i.e. it first fires on the 2nd starving day, once per day while starving |
| party morale changed | **no event** — see Q22 (poll `DailyTickPartyEvent` / `HourlyTickPartyEvent`, or patch the `MobileParty.RecentEventsMorale` setter) | n/a | `party.IsMainParty` when polling | n/a — no hook fires on morale change; all sources are `+=` writes into `RecentEventsMorale` |
| settlement entered | `BeforeSettlementEnteredEvent`, `SettlementEntered`, `AfterSettlementEntered` | `(MobileParty, Settlement, Hero)` | `mobileParty.IsMainParty`; on hero-only entry `EnterSettlementAction.ApplyForCharacterOnly` passes a null party, so also accept `hero == Hero.MainHero` | all three fire back-to-back from `EnterSettlementAction.ApplyInternal`, *after* `mobileParty.CurrentSettlement` is set and `SettlementComponent.OnPartyEntered` ran |
| settlement left | `OnSettlementLeftEvent` | `(MobileParty, Settlement)` — settlement = the one being left | `mobileParty.IsMainParty` | after `CurrentSettlement = null` and `SettlementComponent.OnPartyLeft` in `LeaveSettlementAction.ApplyForParty`; `ApplyForCharacterOnly` fires **no** event |
| siege started | `OnSiegeEventStartedEvent` | `(SiegeEvent)` | attacking: `siegeEvent.BesiegerCamp.LeaderParty.IsMainParty`; defending: `siegeEvent.BesiegedSettlement.OwnerClan == Clan.PlayerClan` | last statement of the `SiegeEvent(Settlement, MobileParty)` constructor — camps and sides fully set up, before any siege battle; battle-level events per assault are in Q23 |
| siege ended | `OnSiegeEventEndedEvent`; player entering the siege fight: `OnPlayerSiegeStartedEvent` | `(SiegeEvent)` / none | same as above; the player-siege event is player-only by construction | first statement of `SiegeEvent.FinalizeSiegeEvent()`, before `BesiegerCamp.FinalizeSiegeEvent()` and `Settlement.FinalizeSiegeEvent()` (the latter only clears siege state); each battle, incl. the capture battle, ended earlier via `MapEventEnded` / siege-completed events (Q23); end is triggered when the last besieger party leaves the camp, after blockade battles, by AI lift decisions or faction destruction |
| player joined / left a kingdom | `OnClanChangedKingdomEvent`; mercenary service additionally `OnMercenaryServiceStartedEvent` / `OnMercenaryServiceEndedEvent` | `(Clan, Kingdom oldKingdom, Kingdom newKingdom, ChangeKingdomAction.ChangeKingdomActionDetail, bool)` / `(Clan, StartMercenaryServiceAction.StartMercenaryServiceActionDetails)` | `clan == Clan.PlayerClan`; direction from `detail` (`JoinKingdom`, `JoinAsMercenary`, `CreateKingdom` vs `LeaveKingdom`, `LeaveAsMercenary`, …) | last statement of `ChangeKingdomAction.ApplyInternal` — after `clan.Kingdom` is assigned and all side effects (stance/peace changes, fief hand-back on leave); the mercenary-service events fire *inside* the action, before this one |
| hero joined the clan | companions/wanderers: `NewCompanionAdded`; lord-type heroes: `OnHeroChangedClanEvent` | `(Hero)` / `(Hero, Clan oldClan)` | companion: `hero.IsPlayerCompanion` (already true at fire time); lord: `hero.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan` | companion: after `companion.CompanionOf = clan` inside `AddCompanionAction.Apply`; lord: after the `_clan` swap inside the `Hero.Clan` property setter — companions never pass through that setter, so only one of the two events fires |
| hero left the clan | companions: `CompanionRemoved`; lord-type: `OnHeroChangedClanEvent` | `(Hero, RemoveCompanionAction.RemoveCompanionDetail)` / `(Hero, Clan oldClan)` | companion: `detail` + your own roster tracking (the event has no Clan arg and `IsPlayerCompanion` is already false); lord: 2nd arg `== Clan.PlayerClan` | companion: last step of `RemoveCompanionAction.ApplyInternal` (after `CompanionOf = null`, roster removal, prisoner/fugitive handling); lord: after the clan swap, 2nd arg is the clan left |
| hero died | clan heroes: `BeforeHeroKilledEvent` then `HeroKilledEvent`; the player character: only `OnBeforeMainCharacterDiedEvent` (then `OnGameOverEvent` later) | all three: `(Hero victim, Hero killer, KillCharacterAction.KillCharacterActionDetail, bool)` | `victim.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan` (the `Clan` getter covers companions via `CompanionOf`); player themselves: `victim.IsHumanPlayerCharacter` | Before: before death mark / obituary / clan bookkeeping, but **deferred** when the victim is in an active battle — `KillCharacterAction.ApplyInternal` early-returns via `AddDeathMark` and the events fire only after the map event finalizes (Q23); HeroKilled: after `MakeDead` and clan-leader / kingdom handling; for `Hero.MainHero` the action returns at the main-character branch, so Before/HeroKilled never fire for the player unless a caller passes `isForced` |

### Uncertain

- **UNCERTAIN**: the order of `DailyTickClanEvent` listeners — `MbEvent` fan-out follows behavior registration order, so it is not documented whether a mod's own daily-clan handler sees `HasUnpaidWages` before or after `ClanVariablesCampaignBehavior.DailyTickClan` runs the finance pass — resolve by reading the daily-tick wiring in `CampaignEventDispatcher` / behavior registration list (Q8's lifecycle chain) and by logging both listeners in-game for one day.
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether any vanilla code path kills the player with `isForced: true` (which would make `BeforeHeroKilledEvent`/`HeroKilledEvent` fire for `Hero.MainHero` too) — resolve with `grep -rn "KillCharacterAction.Apply" decomp/` checking every call site's `isForced` argument.

## Q33 — Vanilla companion grievances

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer

**One behavior owns the whole feature: `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignBehaviors.CompanionGrievanceBehavior` (public, `: CampaignBehaviorBase`)**, added to the sandbox roster by `SandBoxManager.Initialize` one line before `CompanionRolesCampaignBehavior` (Q8). There is no DLC subclass, no model class and no UI: `grep -rln "Grievance" decomp/` returns exactly six files — the behavior, `SandBoxManager.cs`, `AutoGeneratedSaveManager.cs`, and three unrelated Charm-perk uses (`ForgivableGrievances` in `DefaultPerks.cs`, `CharacterRelationCampaignBehavior.cs`, `Persuasion.cs`). Nothing else in the game reads grievance state, so a grievance has **no** direct effect on morale (Q22), wages (Q31), party AI, or any screen; its only output is a relation change (Q21). The dialog table in Q18 Table 6 is the same system; this section is the full lifecycle map.

**1. Types.** `CompanionGrievanceBehavior.GrievanceType` is an `internal enum` nested in the behavior, and its ordinals matter because they index an array (§3): `Invalid = 0` (sentinel: "this companion would not complain about this"), `NoWage = 1`, `Starvation = 2`, `VillageRaided = 3`, `DesertedBattle = 4`.

**Table 1 — what triggers each type.** `RegisterEvents` binds exactly five listeners: `CampaignEvents.HourlyTickEvent` → `OnHourlyTick`, `CampaignEvents.VillageLooted` → `OnVillageRaided`, `CampaignEvents.PlayerDesertedBattleEvent` → `OnPlayerDesertedBattle`, `CampaignEvents.OnSessionLaunchedEvent` → `OnSessionLaunched` (which calls `AddDialogs`, Q7/Q8) and `CampaignEvents.DailyTickEvent` → `OnDailyTick` (Q8/Q23/Q27). There is no conversation-end, relation or party-change listener.

| Type | Source | Exact trigger test | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Starvation` | `OnDailyTick`, first check | `PartyBase.MainParty.IsStarving` (i.e. `_remainingFoodPercentage < 0`) | polled, no event needed (Q31) |
| `NoWage` | `OnDailyTick`, second check (same tick) | `MobileParty.MainParty.HasUnpaidWages > 0f` — the 0…1 wage fraction written by the clan finance pass (Q22/Q31) | a starving party behind on wages can raise **two** different types in one tick, because the cooldown array is per type |
| `VillageRaided` | event `CampaignEvents.VillageLooted` (`IMbEvent<Village>`, Q23) → `OnVillageRaided(Village village)` | `village.Settlement.Party?.MapEvent` must be non-null **and** `mapEvent.InvolvedParties` must contain `PartyBase.MainParty` | the event fires from the `Village.VillageState` setter on a change to `Looted` (chain: `ChangeVillageStateAction.ApplyBySettingToLooted` → Q23); an AI raid, or a village already looted after the battle ended, never matches |
| `DesertedBattle` | event `CampaignEvents.PlayerDesertedBattleEvent` (`IMbEvent<int>`, Q23) → `OnPlayerDesertedBattle(int sacrificedMenCount)` | none — the argument is ignored | raised only by the encounter game menu option `leave_soldiers_behind` ("Try to get away.") confirmed by `try_to_get_away_accept` ("Go ahead with that."), whose consequence fires `CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance.OnPlayerDesertedBattle(...)`; plain retreat/surrender does not fire it |

**2. Which companion — two gates inside `DecideCompanionGrievances`.** (a) Pool: `foreach (Hero item in Hero.MainHero.CompanionsInParty)` — `Clan.Companions` whose `PartyBelongedTo == Hero.MainHero.PartyBelongedTo`, i.e. companions physically in the main party. There is **no** occupation, "is the mentor", clan or behavior filter in this file, so mod companions hired into `Clan.PlayerClan` are treated exactly like vanilla ones. (b) Trait gate `private GrievanceType GetGrievanceTypeForCompanion(Hero companionHero, GrievanceType type)` returns `type` only when the hero's trait **level is > 0** — `DesertedBattle` → `DefaultTraits.Valor`, `Starvation` → `DefaultTraits.Generosity`, `NoWage` → `DefaultTraits.Generosity`, `VillageRaided` → `DefaultTraits.Mercy` — otherwise `GrievanceType.Invalid`.

**3. Creation, re-arm and cadence** — `private void DecideCompanionGrievances(GrievanceType eventType)`, called by all four triggers:

- Global gate: return when `_nextGrievableTimeForComplaintType[(int)eventType].IsFuture` (per-type cooldown, Q27) or `MobileParty.MainParty.IsCurrentlyAtSea` (Q13).
- The scan stops at the **first** hit (`break`), so a trigger creates or re-arms at most one row.
- No row for that hero: `GetGrievanceTypeForCompanion`; if not `Invalid` → `_heroGrievances[hero] = new Grievance(hero, CampaignTime.Now, type)` (row starts `HasBeenSettled = false`, `Count = 1`, `HaveGrievance = true`) and the type's cooldown becomes `CampaignTime.DaysFromNow(4f)`.
- Row exists: re-arm only when `value.TypeOfGrievance == eventType && !value.HaveGrievance && value.NextGrievanceTime.IsPast` → `value.HaveGrievance = true`, `value.Count++`, same `DaysFromNow(4f)` cooldown. This path does **not** re-check the trait gate and `HasBeenSettled` does not block it. The row's type is frozen at creation, so a companion whose row is `Starvation` can only ever complain about food — a later raid or desertion is never attached to an existing row (`Invalid` ≠ match), and the type slot stays blocked for him.
- Obsolescence, in `OnDailyTick` over **every** row (including heroes who left the party): `if (value.NextGrievanceTime.ElapsedDaysUntilNow >= 56f) { value.HasBeenSettled = false; value.Count = 0; }`. With `Count = 0` the hero is back in the "first complaint" branch (`Count <= 1`).
- Declared constants: `BaseGrievanceFrequencyInDays = 4` (the 4-day writes are literals), `GrievanceObsolescenceDurationInDays = 56` (also literal at the use site), `GrievanceCooldownForSameTypeInDays = 1` (unused).

**4. How the conversation is opened** — `private void OnHourlyTick()`, the mechanism described in Q25:

- Bail-outs, in this order: `MobileParty.MainParty.IsCurrentlyAtSea`, `!(GameStateManager.Current.ActiveState is MapState)`, `MobileParty.MainParty.MapEvent != null`, `PlayerEncounter.Current != null`.
- First row with `value.GrievingHero.PartyBelongedTo == MobileParty.MainParty && value.HaveGrievance`: `_currentGrievance = value`; `new ConversationCharacterData(Hero.MainHero.CharacterObject, MobileParty.MainParty.Party)` and `new ConversationCharacterData(value.GrievingHero.CharacterObject)`; then `CampaignMapConversation.OpenConversation(playerCharacterData, conversationPartnerData)` (Q25 mechanism A). The `IsCurrentlyAtSea` sub-branch that would use `CampaignMission.OpenConversationMission` (mechanism B) is dead code here: the guard above already returned for the same party (`PartyBase.MainParty.MobileParty` is `MobileParty.MainParty`).
- Immediately after opening, **unconditionally**: `value.HaveGrievance = false; value.NextGrievanceTime = CampaignTime.DaysFromNow(4 + MBRandom.RandomInt(4));` — the row is consumed at open time, not when the player answers, and the earliest re-arm is 4–7 game days later.
- `_currentGrievance` is cleared **only** by the three consequence methods. A grievance conversation that ends any other way (interrupted by an encounter, or every matching line suppressed by a mod) leaves `_currentGrievance` set, and since the two `start` lines are ordinary global registrations at priority 120 (Q7/Q20), the grievance opener can resurface in any later conversation with that same hero.

**5. Registered dialog lines.** 14 registrations in `AddDialogs`, all through the Q7 API (`AddDialogLine`, `AddPlayerLine`, `AddDialogLineWithVariation`, whose chained `ConversationSentence.Variation(params object[] list)` forwards to `GameText.AddVariation(string text, params object[] propertiesAndWeights)` → pairs of `(tagName, weight)` become `GameTextManager.ChoiceTag` values with `IsTagReversed = weight < 0`, Q14). Token graph: `start` → `grievance_received` → `grievance_noticed` → `grievance_listened` → `close_window`, plus the repeat branch `start` → `grievance_repeated` → `close_window`. Priorities: the two `start` lines pass `120`; everything else keeps the `int priority = 100` default, so a grievance opener outranks normal conversation openings (Q20).

**6. Every consequence.** The grievance system mutates exactly two things: the row (`HasBeenSettled`, `_currentGrievance = null`) and hero relation. It never calls a leave, dismiss, fire or kill action itself.

| Path | Consequence method | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Player picks `grievance_1` | `companion_grievance_accepted_consequence()` | locates the row via `_heroGrievances.FirstOrDefault(t => t.Value == _currentGrievance && t.Key == _currentGrievance.GrievingHero).Value`; sets `HasBeenSettled = true`; **relation +10 only when `Count <= 1`** (a repeat that is accepted again yields neither bonus nor penalty); `_currentGrievance = null` |
| Player picks `grievance_2` | `companion_grievance_consequence()` | **nothing on a first complaint** — the whole body is inside `if (_currentGrievance.Count > 1)`; on a repeat: `int relationChange = (_currentGrievance.HasBeenSettled ? (-5) : (-2));` applied |
| Player picks `grievance_3` | `companion_grievance_rejected_consequence()` | relation **−15**, unconditional; `HasBeenSettled` is *not* written, so the row stays "unsettled" and the next repeat still costs −2; `_currentGrievance = null` |
| Repeat branch (`Count > 1`) | `companion_grievance_consequence()` from the four `companion_grievance_repetition_*` lines | same −2 / −5, applied automatically — the player gets no option |

All relation writes go through the single public action `public static void ChangeRelationAction.ApplyRelationChangeBetweenHeroes(Hero hero, Hero gainedRelationWith, int relationChange, bool showQuickNotification = true)` (Q21). Removal is therefore only indirect: `CompanionRolesCampaignBehavior.OnHeroRelationChanged` runs `KillCharacterAction.ApplyByRemove` when a **negative** change leaves the main-hero relation *strictly* below −10 (`relationChange < 0 && effectiveHero.GetRelation(effectiveHeroGainedRelationWith) < -10`; the class also declares `private const int CompanionRelationLimit = -10` but the listener compares against the literal — Q18 Table 5, Q19, Q21). A −15 rejection therefore dismisses a companion whose relation was **+4 or lower**, while repeated −2 hits (at most one per ~4 days) erode any relation slowly. Cross-check the trait side: the same two events give the *player* −30 `Mercy`/`Valor` (Q24), and the same conditions drive morale (Q22), which is a separate system.

**7. Saved state.** `public override void SyncData(IDataStore dataStore)` syncs three members: `_heroGrievances` (`Dictionary<Hero, Grievance>`), `_currentGrievance` and `_nextGrievableTimeForComplaintType` (`CampaignTime[]`) — rows, the in-flight grievance and the per-type cooldowns all survive save/load (Q9). Row fields: `[SaveableField(1)] Hero GrievingHero`, `[SaveableField(2)] CampaignTime NextGrievanceTime`, `[SaveableField(3)] GrievanceType TypeOfGrievance`, `[SaveableProperty(4)] bool HaveGrievance`, `[SaveableField(5)] bool HasBeenSettled`, `[SaveableField(6)] int Count`; the constructor sets `HasBeenSettled = false`, `Count = 1`, `HaveGrievance = true`, so a freshly created row is immediately pickable by `OnHourlyTick`. Non-saved state: `_currentGrievance` (pointer, but synced), the two constants, and nothing else. The nested `public class CompanionGrievanceBehaviorTypeDefiner : SaveableTypeDefiner` (base type id `80000`) declares the enum (id 1), the row class (id 10) and the `Dictionary<Hero, Grievance>` container; the generated getters/collectors live in `AutoGeneratedSaveManager`.

**8. Narrowest Harmony hook points** (V2 "exclude specific heroes").

(a) *Getting a grievance.* Narrowest per-hero gate: `private GrievanceType GetGrievanceTypeForCompanion(Hero companionHero, GrievanceType type)` — called once per candidate hero, only from `DecideCompanionGrievances`. A prefix `static bool Prefix(Hero companionHero) => !IsExcluded(companionHero);` skips the original and Harmony leaves the value-type `__result` at `default`, i.e. ordinal **0 = `GrievanceType.Invalid`**, which is exactly "no grievance for this companion" — and because `GrievanceType` is `internal`, that default is also the only way a mod can produce `Invalid` without reflection. Caveats: it gates **creation only** — an existing row (loaded save, or a hero excluded later) re-arms through the `value.TypeOfGrievance == eventType && !value.HaveGrievance && value.NextGrievanceTime.IsPast` branch without consulting it, and purging existing rows needs the private `_heroGrievances` (via `AccessTools.Field` / `SyncData`) reached through `public T Campaign.GetCampaignBehavior<T>()`. One hook for a whole grievance type or for all heroes: `private void DecideCompanionGrievances(GrievanceType eventType)` (prefix returning `false`) — coarser, not per-hero. Dialog-only suppression, which does **not** stop `OnHourlyTick` from opening the conversation and consuming the row: `private bool companion_start_grievance_condition()` and `private bool companion_repeat_grievance_condition()`, both parameterless — identify the hero from `public static Hero Hero.OneToOneConversationHero` (or `__instance` + the private `_currentGrievance.GrievingHero`).

(b) *Any grievance consequence.* The three consequence methods, all `private void` and parameterless (the hero is `Hero.OneToOneConversationHero` at dialog time, or `_currentGrievance.GrievingHero` read from `__instance`): `companion_grievance_accepted_consequence()`, `companion_grievance_consequence()`, `companion_grievance_rejected_consequence()`. Skipping them suppresses the relation write **and** the `_currentGrievance = null` reset, so a prefix must restore that field itself (`AccessTools.Field(typeof(CompanionGrievanceBehavior), "_currentGrievance")`) or the stale pointer keeps re-arming the priority-120 opener (§4). Alternative single choke point for all deltas: patch the public action `public static void ChangeRelationAction.ApplyRelationChangeBetweenHeroes(Hero hero, Hero gainedRelationWith, int relationChange, bool showQuickNotification = true)` with a prefix gated on the target hero — one hook, but it fires for every relation change in the game, so gate it narrowly. The grievance behavior itself never removes or fires a companion; the removal hook, if needed, is `private void CompanionRolesCampaignBehavior.OnHeroRelationChanged(Hero effectiveHero, Hero effectiveHeroGainedRelationWith, int relationChange, bool showNotification, ChangeRelationAction.ChangeRelationDetail detail, Hero originalHero, Hero originalGainedRelationWith)` (Q18/Q21, task V1).

**Mod guard (SPEC_VANILLA_GUARDS V2).** Mod companions are excluded with three prefixes: `GetGrievanceTypeForCompanion`
returns its default (`Invalid`) for a mod hero, so no row is created; `OnHourlyTick` first removes mod-hero rows from
`_heroGrievances` and clears `_currentGrievance` when it belongs to a mod hero (rows from saves made before the guard, and
the re-arm path that skips the per-hero gate, §3/§8); `companion_start_grievance_condition` and
`companion_repeat_grievance_condition` return false while a mod hero is the conversation partner, so no grievance line and
therefore no consequence can run. Side effect accepted: a re-armed old row can still win `DecideCompanionGrievances`' first
hit for one tick (its `break`), which then only delays a vanilla companion's complaint; the row is gone at the next hour.

## Q34 — Vanilla behaviors acting on companions (audit)

Status: VERIFIED

### Answer

Scope: non-DLC code only — `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem`, `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.ViewModelCollection`, `SandBox`, `StoryMode` (NavalDLC never searched). A site counts when it selects or mutates a `Hero` **because** that hero is a companion or wanderer: `Hero.IsWanderer`, `Hero.IsPlayerCompanion`, `Hero.CompanionOf`, `Clan.Companions` / `Clan.PlayerClan.Companions`, `Hero.CompanionsInParty`, `Clan.CompanionLimit`, `Occupation.Wanderer`, or a `CompanionRemoved` / `NewCompanionAdded` / `HeroRelationChanged`-style listener. Names that only look like companion logic are excluded from the tables: `AddCompanionBehaviors` / `AddWandererBehaviors` agent-behavior wiring and the `AlleyHelper`-style AI helpers (checked in `GuardsCampaignBehavior`, `CommonTownsfolkCampaignBehavior`, `BarberCampaignBehavior`, `BoardGameCampaignBehavior`, `RecruitmentAgentSpawnBehavior`, `AlleyCampaignBehavior`, `RetirementCampaignBehavior`, `StealthCharactersCampaignBehavior` — none of them touch a hero as a companion).

**Which vanilla sites can see a mod companion.** The factory builds the hero from a template whose XML `occupation` is `Special` (`src/AlbocariusCompanions.Core/Templates/NpcCharacterXml.cs`, GAME_MAP Q11), then calls `SetNewOccupation(Occupation.Wanderer)`, and the mod hires with `AddCompanionAction.Apply(Clan.PlayerClan, hero)`, which only sets `CompanionOf`. Therefore:

- **Visible to vanilla:** `Hero.IsWanderer` (the occupation is switched at run time), `Hero.IsPlayerCompanion`, `Clan.PlayerClan.Companions` (the `CompanionOf` back-link), `Hero.CompanionsInParty`, and everything derived from `Clan.CompanionLimit`.
- **Invisible to vanilla:** the wanderer template pool (`InitializeCompanionTemplateList` keeps only `IsTemplate && Occupation.Wanderer`), and every gate that tests `hero.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan` — neither `AddCompanionAction` nor the mod ever sets `Hero.Clan`, so a mod companion has `Clan == null` (`DefaultNotificationsCampaignBehavior.OnTournamentFinished`, `ClanMemberRolesCampaignBehavior.clan_members_gather_on_condition()` and the mission-agent loop behind it are inert for them).
- **Two cross-cutting side effects.** (1) Every mod companion raises `Clan.PlayerClan.Companions.Count`, which is the trigger for `PerkResetCampaignBehavior` (kill), `LordConversationsCampaignBehavior.too_many_companions` (vanilla hiring blocked) and the `PreconditionFlags.CompanionLimitReached` / `CheckCompanionLimit()` cancel paths in `LordsNeedsTutorIssueBehavior` and `FamilyFeudIssueBehavior`. (2) The `Special` templates keep vanilla from spawning or cloning mod characters, but the sites that key on `IsWanderer` alone — `SwapCompanions`, `TrySpawnNewCompanion`, `TavernEmployeesCampaignBehavior.FindCompanionWithType`, `FightTournamentGame.CanNpcJoinTournament` — still act on an **unhired** mod wanderer. The one registration path that ignores the template rule is `CompanionsCampaignBehavior.OnHeroCreated(Hero, bool)`, which calls `AddToAliveCompanions(hero, isTemplateControlled: true)` and skips `IsTemplateKnown` — already covered by the existing `AddToAliveCompanions` prefix (`src/AlbocariusCompanions.Game/HarmonyPatches.cs`, Q10).

Classification key: **keep** = mechanical and neutral (movement, combat, party roles, equipment, placement, the hire flow the mod already owns). **exclude** = removes/kills/disables the hero on vanilla logic, or makes it speak / gets it announced with vanilla text. **decide** = a role change or gameplay choice for the user. Q18 (dialog points), Q19 (dismissal), Q21 (relation removal) and Q33 (grievances) are already mapped and are referenced, not re-researched.

**Table 1 — removal, dismissal, death, disablement.**

| class.member | what it does | trigger | consequence for the hero | class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CompanionsCampaignBehavior.TryKillCompanion()` | 10% daily roll, random template from `_aliveCompanionTemplates`, then the first alive wanderer with that template and `CompanionOf == null` away from the player | `DailyTickEvent` → `DailyTick` | deleted from the world by `KillCharacterAction.ApplyByRemove` | exclude |
| `CompanionsCampaignBehavior.OnHeroKilled(Hero, Hero, KillCharacterAction.KillCharacterActionDetail, bool)` | listener; drops the template and calls `UnregisterDeadHero` when `victim.IsWanderer && !victim.HasMet` | `HeroKilledEvent` | a killed mod hero the player never met leaves the save object registry | exclude |
| `CompanionsCampaignBehavior.WeeklyTick()` | `Hero.DeadOrDisabledHeroes` with `IsWanderer` and `DeathDay` ≥ 40 days → `CampaignObjectManager.UnregisterDeadHero(Hero)` | weekly tick | only already dead or disabled heroes are unregistered | keep |
| `CompanionsCampaignBehavior.OnHeroCreated(Hero, bool)` and `.OnHeroOccupationChanged(Hero, Occupation)` | register the hero's `Template` in `_aliveCompanionTemplates` (`HeroCreated` bypasses `IsTemplateKnown`) | `HeroCreated`, `HeroOccupationChangedEvent` | hero becomes a target of the daily cull and of `TrySpawnNewCompanion` | exclude — already patched (`AddToAliveCompanions` prefix) |
| `PerkResetCampaignBehavior.DailyTick()` | `Clan.PlayerClan.Companions.Count > Clan.PlayerClan.CompanionLimit` → warn, and past a 6-day window remove one | `DailyTickEvent` | a hired mod companion is removed | exclude |
| `PerkResetCampaignBehavior.RemoveACompanionFromPlayerParty()` | random start index over `Clan.PlayerClan.Companions`, first hero not in a `MapEvent` and not in `IssueManager.IssueSolvingCompanionList` | from `DailyTick` | `KillCharacterAction.ApplyByRemove` — permanent, no dialog, no quest | exclude |
| `PerkResetCampaignBehavior.WarnPlayerAboutCompanionLimit()` | quick info "Your party is above your companion limits. … some of the companions might leave soon." | 6-day cooldown | vanilla warning naming the situation, not the hero | exclude |

**Narrowest Harmony targets for the exclude rows.** All prefixes must be scoped to mod companions by registry id and log once per occurrence (`orchestra/SPEC_VANILLA_GUARDS.md` §0); this table is reporting only, the patches themselves are a later V4 step.

- `CompanionsCampaignBehavior.TryKillCompanion()` — `private void TryKillCompanion()`, no parameters; the narrowest kill point for wanderer culling.
- `CompanionsCampaignBehavior.OnHeroKilled(Hero victim, Hero killer, KillCharacterAction.KillCharacterActionDetail detail, bool showNotification = true)` — private listener; suppress only the `UnregisterDeadHero` step (`internal void UnregisterDeadHero(Hero hero)` is patchable but far too broad).
- `CompanionsCampaignBehavior.OnHeroCreated(Hero hero, bool showNotification = true)` — private; the existing `AddToAliveCompanions(Hero, bool)` prefix (Q10) already covers `OnHeroOccupationChanged`, so this is the remaining registration path.
- `PerkResetCampaignBehavior.RemoveACompanionFromPlayerParty()` — `private void RemoveACompanionFromPlayerParty()`, no parameters, the narrowest removal point; `private void DailyTick()` to stop the whole limit pass and `private void WarnPlayerAboutCompanionLimit()` for the toast. The model-level alternative is `DefaultClanTierModel.GetCompanionLimit(Clan clan)` (public override), which also fixes the `too_many_companions`, `CompanionLimitReached` and `CheckCompanionLimit` rows.
- `PlayerTrackCompanionBehavior.AddHeroToScatteredCompanions(Hero hero)` — `private void`, one `Hero` parameter: the only gate that both tests `hero.IsPlayerCompanion` and feeds every later popup, so the `private void SettlementEntered(MobileParty party, Settlement settlement, Hero hero)` "Tracking" inquiry is never reached.
- `DefaultNotificationsCampaignBehavior.OnCompanionRemoved(Hero hero, RemoveCompanionAction.RemoveCompanionDetail detail)` — `private void`, both parameters available in a prefix signature.
- `IssueBase.StartIssueWithAlternativeSolution()` — public, no parameters; returning `false` keeps a mod companion out of `DisableHeroAction.Apply(Hero)`. Narrower per-issue points are the private `CheckCompanionLimit()` members, but the disable itself has no companion-identity gate to hook because the hero is picked in the issue selection UI.
- `IssueManager.CheckIfTroopsCanReturnToMainParty()` — private, no parameters; the inquiry is its only output, so suppressing it is safe.
- `TavernEmployeesCampaignBehavior.FindCompanionWithType(TavernInquiryCompanionType companionType)` — private, one parameter of the behavior's internal enum; the public overload `public void FindCompanionWithType(PartyRole role)` delegates to it, so the private one covers both entries.
- `LordConversationsCampaignBehavior.conversation_hero_hire_on_condition()` and `.conversation_companion_hire_on_consequence()` — both private, no parameters (already patched, Q6/Q7).
- `LordConversationsCampaignBehavior.conversation_wanderer_player_owned_on_condition()` — `private bool`, no parameters.
- The grievance, dismissal and relation rows are already covered by Q33, Q19 and Q18/Q21 respectively — no additional target is needed here.

**Mod guard (SPEC_VANILLA_GUARDS V3).** `RemoveACompanionFromPlayerParty` gets a prefix that opens a window (thread-static
flag, closed by a finalizer) and `KillCharacterAction.ApplyByRemove` a prefix that skips a mod companion only while the
window is open. Vanilla's loop then `break`s without removing anyone; the daily check retries and can pick a vanilla
companion another day. With only mod companions above the limit nobody is removed (logged each day).

### Evidence

- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/Hero.cs` — `IsPlayerCompanion` — `Hero.IsPlayerCompanion => CompanionOf == Clan.PlayerClan`, the identity test most rows key on; in the same file `IsWanderer` is `Occupation == Occupation.Wanderer`.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/Hero.cs` — `CompanionsInParty` — the hero list the grievance, location, cutscene and log rows iterate.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/Hero.cs` — `CanBecomePrisoner` — captivity allowed for `IsLord || IsPlayerCompanion || IsSpecial`, so a hired mod companion is capturable outside a settlement takeover.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/Hero.cs` — `CanBeGovernorOrHavePartyRole` — `public bool CanBeGovernorOrHavePartyRole()` (no parameters), the eligibility gate reused by the governor and party-leader candidate lists.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/Clan.cs` — `CompanionLimit` — the clan property that forwards to `ClanTierModel.GetCompanionLimit`, the number every limit check compares against.
- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/Clan.cs` — `GetHeirApparents` — skips `IsWanderer` and notable heroes, so a companion can never become the clan heir.
