### Uncertain

- **UNCERTAIN**: which vanilla member chooses the hero that becomes an issue's alternative solution — `IssueBase.AlternativeSolutionHero` is a get-only enumeration of `AlternativeSolutionSentTroops` and `IssueManager` only *reports* the result, so there is no companion-identity gate to prefix. Resolve by tracing the issue option-selection UI in the `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.ViewModelCollection` issue-menu VMs (the candidate list that fills `AlternativeSolutionSentTroops`), or by dumping that roster at run time (Q16/Q29).
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether `Hero.Clan` is null for vanilla-hired companions as well as mod-hired ones — the mod never sets it and `AddCompanionAction` does not either — which decides whether the rows gated on `hero.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan` (`OnTournamentFinished`, `clan_members_gather_on_condition`, parts of `ExpelClanDecisionItemVM`) are inert or live for a mod companion. Resolve in-game by printing `.Clan` for every `Hero.MainHero.CompanionsInParty` entry after hiring through the mod's dialog (Q16).
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether `CompanionsCampaignBehavior.OnHeroKilled` really unregisters a mod hero, which additionally requires `!victim.HasMet` — unresolved for heroes built by `HeroCreator.CreateSpecialHero` that were never talked to. Resolve by killing an unhired, never-approached mod companion in a test run and checking whether it still resolves as an encyclopedia page (Q16/Q32).
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether the "ApplicapleCompanion" overlay highlight (misspelling included) is reachable at all, since it depends on a caller passing that exact condition string; `SettlementMenuOverlayVM` sets `IsHighlightEnabled` and no other file was confirmed to supply the string. Resolve by grepping the VM collection and the `SandBox.GauntletUI` layer for it (Q15/Q17).
- **UNCERTAIN**: whether the prisoner-release pass also reaches a mod companion that owns no caravan — `ReleasePrisonersForClan` iterates `clan.Companions` but only acts through `companion.OwnedCaravans`, and it is unproven whether vanilla ever gives a mod companion a caravan (the `companion_is_caravan_leader_on_condition` path in Q34 Table 1 suggests it can). Resolve in-game by making a mod companion a caravan leader, starting a war and signing peace, then checking the caravan's prisoner list (Q23/Q30).

## Triggers & roles (SPEC_SELECTION_AND_EVENTS Track R)

Q35–Q46 answer the research questions R1–R5 (R1 = Q35–Q42). Nothing here is used in mod code until it has an API index row.

## Q35 — Campaign events catalog 1 (battle, siege, crime, prisoners)

Status: DRAFT

### Answer

All 30 members are `public static` `IMbEvent<...>` properties on `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignEvents` (declarations in `CampaignEvents.cs`, lines 597–929). Every one is raised through a `CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance.OnX(...)` fan-out; rows marked "see Q23" / "see Q32" keep their full timing analysis in those verified sections (only the raise-site name and a one-line timing are repeated here). Raise sites below were verified in non-DLC sources (`TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem*`); NavalDLC was searched only to prove absence and is never a raiser of any row here.

## Q36 — Campaign events catalog 2 (prisoners, raids, sieges, loot)

Status: DRAFT

### Answer

All 29 members are `public static IMbEvent<…>` on `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignEvents` (CampaignEvents.cs lines 931–1141; see Evidence bullet for the per-member line list). Subscription and fan-out work exactly as in **Q8**/**Q9** (`CampaignBehaviorBase.RegisterEvents()` + `AddNonSerializedListener`; listener order caveat in Q23's Notes). A grep of `CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance.<Name>(` over the whole of `decomp` (TaleWorlds.\*, SandBox\*, StoryMode\*, including NavalDLC) found a raising call site inside `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem` for **every one** of the 29 and **no NavalDLC-only raiser** — even the port/blockade machinery is vanilla 1.4.8 — so no member here is "DLC only". Timing anchors repeated below: `MapEventEnded` fires once results are committed; siege/raid/force components finalize afterwards inside `MapEvent.FinalizeEventAux` (see **Q23**); `SiegeEvent.FinalizeSiegeEvent` ends the whole siege after its last battle (see **Q32**).

### Uncertain

- `OnPrisonerDonatedToSettlementEvent`'s first argument is *not* consistently the donor (party-screen donate passes the **receiving** `rightParty.MobileParty`, sell passes the seller, disband passes the disbanding party), and I did not trace whether `rightParty` in the donate screen can be a non-mobile settlement party (`MobileParty` would then be `null`) — gate on the flow, not on arg1.
- `SiegeCompletedEvent`'s leader argument flips sides between battle types (besieger leader for siege battles, garrison leader for sally-outs), and `AfterSiegeCompletedEvent` always uses the attacker-side leader — read straight out of `MapEvent.FinalizeEventAux` (:2097–2138 vs :2185) but not runtime-tested; double-check with a live-log probe before keying dialogue on the leader arg.
- `OnPlayerPartyKnockedOrKilledTroopEvent`: the exact scope of `MapEvent.IsPlayerSimulation` (which parts of the player's battle are simulated vs live-mission) was not fully traced; the per-hit chat volume estimate is qualitative.
- `OnHideoutDeactivatedEvent` — whether the hideout had ever been spotted is not checked by the raiser, so the event can fire for hideouts the player never knew about; the row's pairing advice (gate with a player-won `MapEventEnded` at that settlement) is the mitigation but is not something vanilla enforces.
- `OnMapEventContinuityNeedsUpdateEvent` — I read the two raiser families and the consuming behavior, but did not trace whether other stance mutations (e.g. war-end mediation paths) also flip `StanceLink.StanceType`; "any war↔peace flip" describes the two sites verified.

## Q37 — Campaign events catalog 3 (party, army, settlement, tournaments)

Status: DRAFT

### Answer

All 37 members are `public static` `IMbEvent<...>` properties on `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignEvents` (declarations in `CampaignEvents.cs`, lines 631–841). Every one is raised through a `CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance.OnX(...)` fan-out; the four SandBox mission/alley/tournament sites use the cast form `((CampaignEventReceiver)CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance).OnX(...)` — same dispatcher, same listeners, so the normal Q8 subscription pattern (`RegisterEvents` + `AddNonSerializedListener`) covers them. A whole-decomp sweep found at least one non-DLC raiser for every member, so no row here is "DLC only"; NavalDLC was touched only in that sweep to prove non-DLC raisers exist. Rows marked "see Q23" / "see Q32" keep their full timing analysis in those verified sections; only the raise-site and a one-line timing are repeated. Three ordering quirks worth knowing before wiring reactions: `ArmyGathered` fires *before* `ArmyCreated` for the same host (both come out of `Kingdom.CreateArmy`); the destroy pair fires in order `MobilePartyDestroyed` (data intact) → `MapInteractableDestroyed` → `OnPartyRemovedEvent` (data already wiped); and the settlement-entered trio are three back-to-back slots fired *after* the enter is already applied (Q32).

#### War & armies

| Member | Arguments (types, in order) | When it fires — raising call site (BEFORE/AFTER the outcome) | Player party/clan test | Usefulness → trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ArmyCreated | `(Army army)` | `Kingdom.CreateArmy` (Kingdom.cs:687) — AFTER `new Army(...)` and `army.Gather(target, calledParties)` have run, so the army already exists with its member list assigned. AI callers: `AiPartyThinkBehavior` (:141) via `ArmyManagementCalculationModel.CanLordCreateArmy` (:522); the player's "create army" menu uses the same entry point. - `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.Incidents/IncidentEffect.cs` — `IncidentEffect` — the building-level effect's apply path (:165–184) raises one bulk OnBuildingLevelChanged with delta ±n (debug cheats also raise it, CampaignCheats.cs:1569)

### Uncertain

- `AlleyOccupiedByPlayer` — the 2nd argument is the party screen's `leftMemberRoster` (MissionAlleyHandler.cs:258); the method's decompiler output is garbled (IL comments), so whether that roster represents the player's losses or the troops left behind as alley garrison was not pinned down. The trigger recommendation only relies on the timing.
- `PlayerStartedTournamentMatch` — verified it fires unconditionally at every match start inside an attended tournament mission (TournamentBehavior.cs:168); whether the player is fighting in that particular match is only readable from the SandBox behavior's `CurrentMatch.IsPlayerParticipating()`, which the event arguments do not expose.
- `MobilePartyCreated` / `OnPartyRemovedEvent` for the MainParty — whether campaign init/teardown routes the main party through `CreateParty`/`RemoveParty` was not verified, so don't assume those two events fire (or don't fire) for the MainParty.
- `HeroOrPartyGaveItem` — in the hero-pair branch GiveItemAction.cs:20 shows `AddToCounts(..., -Amount)` for the receiver (decompiler artifact or real game bug); the event arguments are trustworthy but the roster side-effect of that branch should not be relied on.
- `BeforeMissionOpenedEvent` — the game-layer caller of `OnMissionIsStarting` lives in TaleWorlds.Engine, which is not decompiled; only the Campaign.cs body (already gated on `PlayingInCampaignMode`) was verified.
- Tick rows — "once per party/settlement/town per hour or day, staggered" is read from the `PeriodicTicker` usage; the exact distribution phase inside the day (which fraction of the day each item gets its slot) was not traced.

## Q38 — Campaign events catalog 4 (party, troops, missions, ships)

Status: DRAFT

### Answer

All 36 members are `public static` `IMbEvent<...>` properties on `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignEvents` (declarations in `CampaignEvents.cs`, lines 843–1111), raised through `CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance.OnX(...)` fan-out, so the normal Q8 subscription pattern covers every one. A whole-decomp sweep (NavalDLC opened only to prove absence/presence) found non-DLC raising code for 34 of the 36; the literal DLC-only exceptions are `OnShipCreatedEvent` (sole raiser is NavalDLC `ShipProductionCampaignBehavior`) and — practically — the `OnMapMarkerCreated/Removed` pair, because no base-game or SandBox code ever calls `MapMarkerManager.CreateMapMarker` (only NavalDLC storyline quests do, and vanilla quest cleanup at `QuestBase` then merely removes those DLC markers). The whole naval block (`RaftStateChanged`, `NavigationStateChanged`, `ShipDestroyed/OwnerChanged/Created/Repaired`, `FigureheadUnlocked`) *does* live in the base `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem` assembly (actions in `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.Actions`, `Ship`/`Figurehead` types in base) and several raisers are base-game files (`PlayerEncounter`, `MapEvent`, `MobileParty.RemoveParty`), but ships only exist in campaigns with naval content, so treat those rows as content-gated flavor hooks, not core triggers (see Uncertain). Three useful discovery pairs worth knowing: an army removal has *two* slots (`PartyRemovedFromArmy` from inside `Army`, always; `OnPartyLeftArmy` only when the `MobileParty.Army` setter is nulled) — use `PartyRemovedFromArmy` as the canonical counterpart of `OnPartyJoinedArmy`; disbanding has a *start → end* pair ~days apart (`OnPartyDisbandStarted` when the party is told to melt away, `OnPartyDisbanded` when it reaches a settlement and is about to be removed, rosters still intact in the handler); and recruitment has two granularities (`OnUnitRecruited` = player-only per unit, `OnTroopRecruited` = every party in the world incl. AI). Tick and starvation rows overlap earlier verified sections: the `CampaignPeriodicEventManager` ticker mechanism is Q27's, the food/starving timing analysis is Q32's, tournament lifecycle events are Q37's — only the join-instant row is new here.

### Uncertain

- Naval events in a non-DLC campaign — the ship actions, `Ship`/`Figurehead` types and most raisers are in base `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem` (verified), but no base/SandBox content spawns ships; whether a mod-enabled non-DLC campaign would see `Ship.All` populated was not proven. Treat every naval row as "fires only when naval content is active".
- Whether `Army.DisperseInternal` (Q37) detaches member parties through the `MobileParty.Army` setter — if it does, army disbanding ALSO raises `OnPartyLeftArmy`; verified only that `PartyRemovedFromArmy` fires from `OnRemovePartyInternal` for the removal paths traced.
- `OnPartyDisbandStarted/OnPartyDisbanded` for the MainParty itself — no raiser was found that passes the MainParty (the clan screen excludes it; player "disband" acts on clan war parties); cannot state absolutely that the player's own party never fires the pair.
- Player and `OnTroopGivenToSettlement` — verified the player CAN fire it, but only in the army-leader auto-top-up role (chain :255→:271→:317→:542); the player's manual garrison transfers in the settlement/garrison screen showed no raiser in the single-raise-point grep, but that UI path was not traced to its own code, so "manual donations never fire it" is inferred from grep, not from reading the garrison-screen code.
- `PlayerStartRecruitmentEvent` — the GauntletTutorialSystem call (SandBox.GauntletUI) was seen in the grep but its exact tutorial trigger context was not opened; immaterial to the "not useful" verdict.
- Whether `OnMissionEndedEvent` fires for conversation/arena fake missions — only real campaign missions were traced (`CampaignMissionComponent`); `MapConversationMission` is a different `ICampaignMission` shim without that component, presumed silent but not proven.
- `OnQuarterDailyPartyTick` — "≈4× per in-game day, staggered" follows the PeriodicTicker interval pattern (same caveat as Q27/Q37 tick rows: exact intra-day phase not traced).

## Q39 — Campaign events catalog 5 (heroes, clan, kingdom)

Status: DRAFT

### Answer

All 34 members are `public static` `IMbEvent<...>` properties on `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignEvents` (declarations in `CampaignEvents.cs` lines 591–755; the instance overrides that `Invoke` the statics are at 1423–1833 in the same file). Every member has at least one **non-DLC raiser** — none in this catalog is NavalDLC-only. The fan-out mechanics (`CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance.OnX(...)` → `CampaignEventReceiver` → the `CampaignEvents` override → static event; subscription via `CampaignEvents.X.AddNonSerializedListener(this, handler)` in `RegisterEvents`) are exactly as in Q8/Q23 and are not repeated per row. Rows marked "see QX" keep their full analysis in the verified section Q21/Q23/Q24/Q31/Q32/Q6 and only repeat the raise site and timing here. Raise sites were grepped in `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem*`, `SandBox*`, `StoryMode*` (never NavalDLC). Note two name traps: `ClanTierIncrease` is raised by the dispatcher method named `OnClanTierChanged`, and `ChildEducationCompletedEvent` fires **per education stage**, not only at final completion.

#### Hero lifecycle (creation, state, leveling, parties)

| Member | Arguments (types, in order) | When it fires — raising call site, BEFORE/AFTER the outcome | Player party/clan test | Usefulness → trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HeroCreated | `(Hero hero, bool isBornNaturally)` | `HeroCreator.InitializeHeroFromSettings` (HeroCreator.cs:297, dispatch at :345) — LAST statement, after skills/equipment/relatives/appearance are fully set up; 2nd arg = `initializationArgs.IsOffspring` (true only for newborns; **false for every factory path incl. `CreateSpecialHero`**, so mod-spawned heroes fire it too — Q4 spawn, Q1: vanilla `CompanionsCampaignBehavior.OnHeroCreated` already listens) | `hero.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan`, `hero.IsPlayerCompanion`, wanderer test per Q2; expect **self-fires** from our own spawn flow (Q4) and filter them | useful → `heroCreated` — but only react to foreign creations, not our own |
| OnHeroActivatedEvent | `(Hero hero, Hero.CharacterStates previousState)` | `Hero.ChangeState` (Hero.cs:1769–1784) — AFTER `_heroState = newState` is written, fires only when `newState == Active`, payload carries the PREVIOUS state; fires on every into-Active transition: fugitive reactivation (Q19/Q35 fugitive rows), mod activation during our spawn flow (Q4), age-related activation (Q34 aging rows). Vanilla `CompanionsCampaignBehavior.OnHeroActivated` is a listener (Q1) | `hero == Hero.MainHero` (player's own activation), `hero.IsPlayerCompanion`, `hero.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan` | useful → `heroActivated` — "companion wakes up"; `previousState == Fugitive` distinguishes tavern respawns (Q19) |
| HeroOccupationChangedEvent | `(Hero hero, Occupation oldOccupation)` | `Hero.SetNewOccupation` (Hero.cs:1283–1288) — AFTER `Occupation = occupation`, payload is the OLD value; every occupation conversion fires it (Q34: turn-companion-to-lord calls `SetNewOccupation(Lord)`); also fires from our own wanderer setup (Q2/Q4) | no party/clan arg: test `hero.IsPlayerCompanion` / `hero.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan`; guard self-fires from Q2/Q4 setup | useful → `heroOccupationChanged` — companion becomes lord (see Q31 grant-fief chain) |

## Q40 — Campaign events catalog 6 (diplomacy, family, clan)

Status: DRAFT

### Answer

All 34 members are `public static` `IMbEvent<...>` properties on `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignEvents` (declaration range lines 759–1119 of `CampaignEvents.cs`; the instance overrides that `Invoke` the statics sit beside them). The fan-out mechanics (`CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance.OnX(...)` → `CampaignEventReceiver` → the `CampaignEvents` override → static event; subscription via `CampaignEvents.X.AddNonSerializedListener(this, handler)` in `RegisterEvents`) are exactly as in Q8/Q23 and are not repeated per row. Raise sites were grepped in `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem*`, `SandBox*`, `StoryMode*` (never NavalDLC); **no member in this catalog is DLC-only**. Four traps: (1) the peace/marriage/vassal-mercenary "OfferedToPlayer" trio does **not** fire when the offer is created — it fires from the `_onInspect` lambda of a map-notification VM, i.e. when the player inspects the banner (the auto-execute timing lives in the non-decompiled GauntletUI layer); (2) `OnPeaceOfferResolvedEvent` is a **dead event** in 1.4.8 — two vanilla listeners subscribe, but no code in any decompiled assembly (DLCs included) ever calls the dispatcher method; (3) two raisers are written as `((CampaignEventReceiver)CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance).OnX(...)` casts (heir-selection request, alley-leader busy) — grepping `\.OnX(` catches both forms; (4) dispatcher method names lack the `Event` suffix (`OnClanDestroyed(...)` raises `OnClanDestroyedEvent`). Rows marked "see QX" keep their full analysis in the verified section Q23/Q32/Q27/Q17 and only repeat the raise site and timing here.

| OnMercenaryServiceEndedEvent | `(Clan clan, EndMercenaryServiceAction.EndMercenaryServiceActionDetails details)` | see **Q32** — dispatch at `EndMercenaryServiceAction.cs:15`; `details` names the reason (`ApplyByBecomingVassal`, `ByLeavingKingdom`, …) | `clan == Clan.PlayerClan` | useful → `mercenaryLeft` — see Q32 |

#### Marriage, children and succession

| Member | Arguments (types, in order) | When it fires — raising call site, BEFORE/AFTER the outcome | Player party/clan test | Usefulness → trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OnMarriageOfferedToPlayerEvent | `(Hero suitor, Hero maiden)` | `_onInspect` lambda of `MarriageOfferNotificationItemVM` (:21) — fires on banner inspect, then stops game time (`TimeControlMode.Stop`, :23) and removes the notification, **BEFORE** the accept/decline inquiry; arg order fixed by the `MarriageOfferMapNotification` ctor — suitor = male, maiden = female (:47–48) | either hero in `Clan.PlayerClan` or `== Hero.MainHero` (offer concerning player kin) | useful → `marriageOfferReceived` — wedding-talk beat; acceptance fires **no** dedicated event (`MarryHeroesViaOffer` → `MarriageAction.Apply`, :127–137); the marriage itself is `HeroMarriedEvent` (Q39) |
| OnMarriageOfferCanceledEvent | `(Hero suitor, Hero maiden)` | raised by `MarriageOfferCampaignBehavior` on: popup decline (:159), 2-day expiry (:183), partner taken prisoner (:211), war between the clans (:219/:262), hero died (:227/:270), relation breaking the inter-clan permission (:294); also `MarriageOfferMapNotification.IsValid()` raises it during banner validity checks (:60), and `MarriageOfferNotificationItemVM.OnFinalize` raises it if the banner dies **uninspected** (:41–43); never raised on acceptance | either hero in `Clan.PlayerClan` / `== Hero.MainHero` | useful → `marriageOfferCanceled` — offer withdrawn; reason readable from live state (war/capture/death) |
| OnChildConceivedEvent | `(Hero mother)` | `MakePregnantAction.Apply` — sets `mother.IsPregnant = true` (:7) then raises (:8) → **AFTER** the flag; only non-cheat raiser is `PregnancyCampaignBehavior` (:122, model-driven daily spouse-proximity roll) | `mother.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan` (companion or player's wife) | useful → `childConceived` — pregnancy announcement; fires for every AI couple → gate on player clan / companions |
| OnGivenBirthEvent | `(Hero mother, List<Hero> aliveChildren, int stillbornCount)` | `PregnancyCampaignBehavior.CheckOffspringToDeliver` — dispatch at :183, **AFTER** `HeroCreator.DeliverOffSpring` created the living newborns (:172–173) and **BEFORE** `mother.IsPregnant = false` (:184) and the maternal-death roll (:186–189, `KillCharacterAction.ApplyInLabor` → Q32 death events follow) | `mother.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan`; `aliveChildren` = the newborn heroes | useful → `childBorn` — birth beat; beware mother can die *after* this event |
| OnHeirSelectionRequestedEvent | `(Dictionary<Hero, int> candidateHeirs)` | SandBox `HeirSelectionCampaignBehavior` (:127, written as an `((CampaignEventReceiver)CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance)` cast) inside its `OnBeforeMainCharacterDied` handler — **BEFORE** any heir is chosen; dict = candidate heir heroes → heir points; the death path then continues (MainParty cleared, `DestroyKingdomAction.ApplyByKingdomLeaderDeath` :173) | player-only by construction (candidates are player-clan heroes) | useful → `heirSelectionRequested` — the player just died, heir not yet picked: grief/farewell barks |
| OnHeirSelectionOverEvent | `(Hero selectedHeir)` | only raiser is UI: `HeirSelectionPopupVM.ExecuteFinalizeHeirSelection` (:265, …Map.HeirSelectionPopup/) once the player confirms — **BEFORE** anything is applied: the behavior listener (:135–137) then runs `ApplyHeirSelectionAction.ApplyByDeath` (→ `ChangeClanLeaderAction` :27 → this catalog's `OnClanLeaderChangedEvent`; → `ChangePlayerCharacterAction` :68) | player-only by construction; `selectedHeir.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan` | useful → `heirSelected` — new main character known before the switch runs; farewell barks for the old one |
| OnBeforePlayerCharacterChangedEvent | `(Hero oldPlayer, Hero newPlayer)` | `ChangePlayerCharacterAction.Apply` (:21) — **BEFORE** any MainHero/party state is transferred | player-only by construction | useful → `playerCharacterChanging` — rare (heir succession / "play as this character"); pre-switch cleanup + farewells |
| OnPlayerCharacterChangedEvent | `(Hero oldPlayer, Hero newPlayer, MobileParty newPlayerParty, bool isMainPartyChanged)` | same action (:59) — **AFTER** the MainHero swap, party-owner transfer (:43–53) and ship/captivity handling; `newPlayerParty` = party led by the new character; `isMainPartyChanged` = whether the MainParty itself changed owner | player-only by construction | useful → `playerCharacterChanged` — greeting beats for the new character; vanilla housekeeping listens too (`VassalAndMercenaryOfferCampaignBehavior` :212ff) |
| OnClanLeaderChangedEvent | `(Hero oldLeader, Hero newLeader)` | `ChangeClanLeaderAction.ApplyInternal` — `clan.SetLeader(newLeader)` (:50) then dispatch (:51) → **AFTER** the leader is written; raisers: `ApplyHeirSelectionAction` (:27 player succession), `KillCharacterAction` (:65 auto-succession when the clan leader dies), `KingSelectionKingdomDecision` (:222), save-compat passes (`ClanVariablesCampaignBehavior`) | no clan arg: `newLeader.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan` / `oldLeader.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan` | useful → `clanLeaderChanged` — "new leader" barks, esp. player-clan succession (leader-role recognition) |

#### Clan lifecycle and state

| Member | Arguments (types, in order) | When it fires — raising call site, BEFORE/AFTER the outcome | Player party/clan test | Usefulness → trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DailyTickClanEvent | `(Clan clan)` | `CampaignPeriodicEventManager.InitializeTickers` — `_dailyTickClanTicker` over `Clan.All` (:246–249) spreading one clan per slice; dispatcher fan-out at :1323 → every clan **exactly once per in-game day** (mechanics in **Q27**); vanilla consumers: Q32 unpaid-wages finance pass, `AllianceCampaignBehavior.DailyTickClan` expiry sweep (:137) | `clan == Clan.PlayerClan` | useful → `dailyClanTick` — once-a-day poll host (unpaid wages Q32, grievance feed Q33) |
| HourlyTickClanEvent | `(Clan clan)` | same wiring: `_hourlyTickClanTicker` over `Clan.All` (:230–233), dispatcher fan-out at :1269 → every clan once per in-game hour | `clan == Clan.PlayerClan` | useful (polling host only) → `hourlyClanTick` — cheap hourly clan-scoped polling; vanilla listeners are AI housekeeping (`KingdomManager`, `PartyHealCampaignBehavior`, `BanditSpawnCampaignBehavior`) |
| OnClanDestroyedEvent | `(Clan clan)` | `DestroyClanAction.ApplyInternal` — dispatch at :22 is the **FIRST statement**, before `DeactivateClan()` (:23), war-party destruction, per-hero `KillCharacterAction.ApplyByRemove` and fief redistribution (:50–61) → the clan object is still fully readable at fire time (opposite of Q39 `KingdomDestroyedEvent`) | `clan == Clan.PlayerClan` (player-clan annihilation — game effectively over) or a lord clan (drama case; args safe here) | useful → `clanDestroyed` — house-ends beat; args intact pre-teardown |
| OnHeroChangedClanEvent | `(Hero hero, Clan oldClan)` | see **Q32** — raised in the `Hero.Clan` setter (Hero.cs:523) after the clan write; second arg = the clan being left | joined: `hero.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan`; left: `oldClan == Clan.PlayerClan` | useful → `heroChangedClan` — see Q32 |
| OnClanInfluenceChangedEvent | `(Clan clan, float amount)` | `ChangeClanInfluenceAction.ApplyInternal` — `clan.Influence += amount` (:7) then raise (:8) → **AFTER** the delta; fires for every clan on **every** influence delta (battles, decisions, policies, daily passes) — very high volume | `clan == Clan.PlayerClan` (player influence = decision power) | useful → `clanInfluenceChanged` — gate on player clan and a magnitude threshold, else too noisy |
| CompanionRemoved | `(Hero companion, RemoveCompanionAction.RemoveCompanionDetail detail)` | see **Q32/Q17** — sole dispatcher raise is the LAST statement of `RemoveCompanionAction.ApplyInternal` (:56); do not confuse with the `CompanionOf` setter's `_companionOf.OnCompanionRemoved(this)` (Hero.cs:266) — that is internal `Clan` bookkeeping (Clan.cs:1220) with no event fan-out | no clan argument — capture companion state before removal; `detail` separates dismissal/death/turning-lord (Q32 rows) | useful → `companionRemoved` — see Q32/Q34 ("left your clan" beats) |

#### Hero roles, movement and bookkeeping

| Member | Arguments (types, in order) | When it fires — raising call site, BEFORE/AFTER the outcome | Player party/clan test | Usefulness → trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OnHeroGetsBusyEvent | `(Hero hero, HeroGetsBusyReasons reason)` | six raisers, all **AFTER** the role/state change is applied; payload enum `HeroGetsBusyReasons` = `BecomeGovernor=0, BecomeEmissary=1, BecomeCaravanLeader=2, BecomeAlleyLeader=3, SolvesIssue=4, Traveling=5`: governor — `ChangeGovernorAction:31`; emissary — `EnterSettlementAction:58` (player-clan hero with no party entering a settlement alone, `GovernorOf == null`); caravan leader — `CaravanPartyComponent.CreateCaravanParty:260` / `ConvertPartyToCaravanParty:215` after the caravan party exists; alley leader — SandBox `AlleyCampaignBehavior:666` (cast form `(HeroGetsBusyReasons)3`); issue solver — `IssuesCampaignBehavior:646` (hero handed over to solve an issue); traveling — `Hero.ChangeState:1778` after `_heroState` is written (:1772) | `hero.IsPlayerCompanion` / `hero.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan`, filter on `reason` | useful → `heroGotBusy` — the role hook (governor / caravan leader / emissary appointments, R1); ignore the noisy `Traveling` reason |
| OnHeroSharedFoodWithAnotherHeroEvent | `(Hero supporter, Hero supported, float influence)` | `FoodConsumptionBehavior.PartyConsumeFood` — dispatch at :191 inside the army food-share loop (a starving army party is fed by the best-supplied party of the same army); fires per donor **AFTER** the item transfer and `GainKingdomInfluenceAction.ApplyForGivingFood` (:177); runs from the daily party tick; `influence` = influence gained by the donor (≈0.2 per food item) | fed: `supported == MobileParty.MainParty.LeaderHero`; feeding: `supporter == MobileParty.MainParty.LeaderHero` | useful → `sharedFood` — gratitude/provider flavor when the player's party feeds (or is fed by) army allies |
| OnHeroTeleportationRequestedEvent | `(Hero hero, Settlement targetSettlement, MobileParty targetParty, TeleportHeroAction.TeleportationDetail detail)` | `TeleportHeroAction.ApplyInternal` — dispatch at :22 is the **FIRST statement, BEFORE** the switch that performs the teleport (:23–111); branches early-return when the target party is inactive/engaging, so the teleport may **not** happen; `TeleportationDetail` enum (:9–18) = Immediate/Delayed × Settlement/Party variants | `hero.IsPlayerCompanion` (companion being re-placed — Q1/Q17 spawn flow), `hero.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan`, `hero == Hero.MainHero` | useful → `heroTeleportRequested` — with the BEFORE-may-not-happen caveat; for a reliable "companion moved" combine with polling `hero.PartyBelongedTo`/`CurrentSettlement` |
| OnHeroUnregisteredEvent | `(Hero hero)` | `CampaignObjectManager.UnregisterDeadHero` (CampaignObjectManager.cs:477–482) — after the hero is removed from `DeadOrDisabledHeroes`, dispatch at :481; callers: 40-day cleanup of never-met wanderers (`CompanionsCampaignBehavior.WeeklyTick` :158), killed unmet wanderers (:191), notable/rebellion cleanup, and an old-save migration pass in `Hero.OnLoad` (:1725) | `hero.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan` is technically testable, but the hero is already dead and removed from all live lists | not useful — post-death registry bookkeeping; the reaction beats belong on `HeroKilledEvent` (Q32) |

- `decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/CampaignObjectManager.cs` — `UnregisterDeadHero` — remove from `DeadOrDisabledHeroes` then `OnHeroUnregistered` (:477–482); callers: `CompanionsCampaignBehavior` (:158 weekly 40-day cleanup, :191 killed-unmet-wanderer), `Hero.OnLoad` migration pass (:1725), notable/rebellion cleanup.

### Uncertain

- The exact UI timing of notification `_onInspect` execution (`MapNotificationItemBaseVM.ExecuteAction`): whether the offered-to-player trio fires only on player click or also when a banner auto-expands/auto-executes lives in the non-decompiled GauntletUI layer — resolve by logging a listener for each of the three events in-game.
- `OnPeaceOfferResolvedEvent` being fully dead is based on grep over all decompiled game code (DLCs included); only genuinely non-decompiled engine code could fire it unseen — confirm with a logging listener before assuming a "peace resolved" hook exists.
- Listener order inside the `DailyTickClanEvent` / `HourlyTickClanEvent` fan-out is behavior-registration order (same caveat as Q32) — unresolved whether a mod's daily-clan handler runs before `ClanVariablesCampaignBehavior`'s finance pass or `AllianceCampaignBehavior`'s expiry sweep.

## Q42 — Campaign events catalog 8 (economy, crafting, save) + polling-only signals

Status: DRAFT

### Answer

All 31 members below are `public static IMbEvent<...>` (or `IMbEvent<TArgs>` / no-arg `IMbEvent`) properties of
`TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignEvents` (`decomp/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem/CampaignEvents.cs`),
fanned out by `CampaignEventDispatcher` `OnX` methods and subscribed with the Q8 pattern
(`CampaignBehaviorBase.RegisterEvents()` + `CampaignEvents.XEvent.AddNonSerializedListener(this, handler)`).
Raise sites were verified in non-DLC sources only (`TaleWorlds.*`, `SandBox*`, `StoryMode*`); no event in this batch depends on NavalDLC.
Daily/hourly tick plumbing and battle/war/death context is already covered in Q23 and Q32 — reused below with "see Q23" / "see Q32".
Gold/asset income at :584 was independently verified in Q40. Timings are stated as BEFORE/AFTER the game outcome the event names.

#### Trade, inventory and caravan transactions

| Member | Arguments (types, in order) | When it fires — raising call site, BEFORE/AFTER the outcome | Player party/clan test | Usefulness → trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OnItemSoldEvent` | `PartyBase, PartyBase, ItemRosterElement, int, Settlement` | **Never fires.** No dispatcher call site exists anywhere in 1.4.8 managed code (all decompiled dirs incl. NavalDLC); the only consumers are listeners in `SettlementNameplateNotificationsVM` (dead UI path left over from a refactor). | n/a | **not useful** — dead event in managed 1.4.8; player sell feedback must come from `PlayerInventoryExchangeEvent` (below) instead. |
| `PlayerInventoryExchangeEvent` | `List<(ItemRosterElement,int)> purchased, List<(ItemRosterElement,int)> sold, bool isTrading` | `InventoryLogic.DoneLogic()` — when the player closes an inventory screen (trade/loot/gift): AFTER every item transfer is applied to the rosters, but BEFORE the counterparty gold is settled (`SetGold`/`GiveGoldAction` run a few lines later). | Fires only for the player's inventory session — always player, no test needed. | Useful → `tradeSessionClosed`: merchant companion quips about volume; filter `isTrading` for trade-only lines (false = loot/gift/donate). |

Vanilla handler (`DiscardItemsCampaignBehavior`) just grants discard XP. | Always player (main-party inventory). | Useful → `itemsDiscarded`: comment on wasted loot; arg carries only the post-close roster, so snapshot before/after if the mod needs the discarded delta. |

Same point in the frame: after items moved, before gold settled. | Always player (Trade skill XP pass over `PartyBase.MainParty`). | Useful → `tradeProfit`: reuse vanilla's own profit number for merchant/caravan-master barks instead of recomputing. |
| `OnCaravanTransactionCompletedEvent` | `MobileParty caravanParty, Town town, List<(EquipmentElement,int)> tradedItems` | End of the caravan's daily trade pass: `CaravansCampaignBehavior.SellGoods` :1222 and `BuyGoods` :1265 (behavior driven from `DailyTickEvent`, see Q27), and `SellGoodsForTradeAction` :66 when a caravan sells to a town. In all sites AFTER all `SellItemsAction`/roster/gold moves, and only if `mobileParty.IsCaravan` and the item list is non-empty. | `caravanParty.Clan == Clan.PlayerClan` (player-owned caravan, Q38 caravan ownership). | Useful → `caravanTradeCompleted`: caravan-master companion reports a player caravan's buy/sell round; full item list is in the third arg. |

All AFTER the income is booked. | Already player-guarded at every site (`clan == Clan.PlayerClan` / `hero == Hero.MainHero`) — no filter needed. | Useful → `assetIncome`: daily income flavour keyed by `AssetIncomeType` (Taxes/TributesEarned/Caravan/Workshop) + amount. |

#### Polling-only signals

No campaign event exists for these states — the mod must read the member on a tick. Tick choice reuses Q23/Q27 (hourly
`HourlyTickPartyEvent`/`DailyTickPartyEvent` or the boundary-aligned global `HourlyTickEvent`/`DailyTickEvent`, see Q27);
gold/item APIs are per Q29, morale per Q22, location primitives per Q28, clock per Q27.

| Signal | Exact member to read (public?) | Suggested tick | Suggested trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| Party food low | `PartyBase.RemainingFoodPercentage` (public int; counts below 0 = no food) / summary `MobileParty.Food` (public float); `PartyBase.IsStarving` (public bool) only true once already starving — approaching starvation has no event (the starving events, see Q23/Q32, first fire on the 2nd starving day, once per day) | hourly (gate on `MobileParty.MainParty`) | `foodLow` / `foodCritical` |
| Wage debt | `MobileParty.HasUnpaidWages` (public float, unpaid fraction 0…1 — Q22/Q23) | daily in `DailyTickPartyEvent`, after the clan-finance pass (see Q32) | `wageDebt` |
| Morale low | `MobileParty.MainParty.Morale` (public float 0…100, recomputed per read; recent-events component `RecentEventsMorale`) — no morale-changed event, see Q22; desertion band is ≤ 10 | hourly | `moraleLow` |
| Player gold below X | `Hero.MainHero.Gold` (public int; writes via `ChangeHeroGold`, see Q29) | daily, and/or immediately after `OnPlayerEarnedGoldFromAssetEvent` / big `PlayerInventoryExchangeEvent` | `goldLow` |
| Companion wounded | `Hero.IsWounded` (public bool, `HitPoints <= WoundedHealthLimit`) over `Clan.PlayerClan.Companions` (public `MBReadOnlyList<Hero>`, `Clan.cs` :186); wounding happens at battle settlement and there is no unwound event — see Q23 (`HeroWounded`) | daily | `companionWounded` |
| Near settlement | `MobileParty.MainParty.CurrentSettlement` (public; non-null = physically inside) or `MobileParty.MainParty.Position` vs `Settlement.GatePosition`/`Settlement.Position.DistanceToSquared` over `Settlement.All` — full location primitives in Q28 | hourly | `nearSettlement` |
| Time of day / season | `CampaignTime.Now.GetHourOfDay`, `CampaignTime.Now.IsNightTime`, `CampaignTime.Now.GetSeasonOfYear` (all public, full clock API in Q27; `HourlyTickEvent` is boundary-aligned to whole hours) | hourly | `nightfall` / `seasonChanged` |

### Uncertain

- `OnItemsDiscardedByPlayerEvent`: the arg is the post-close roster; how `ItemDiscardModel.GetXpBonusForDiscardingItems` derives "discarded value" from it (it may diff against a cached roster) was not read — a mod wanting the discarded delta should keep its own roster snapshot.
- Caravan timing granularity: `BuyGoods`/`SellGoods` sit inside the caravan AI daily pass driven from `DailyTickEvent` (:283), but the exact enclosing method between `DailyTick()` :564 and the calls at :386-:394 was not named — if per-party spread matters, confirm which ticker drives :386-:394.
- Finance sites :448/:491: dispatch is at the town/village `TradeTaxAccumulated -= num` withdrawal with the `clan == Clan.PlayerClan` guard; the exact line that credits the clan gold sits in the enclosing pass and was not separately verified (Q40's :584 pattern shows the AFTER-credit convention).
- Whether the player themselves can ever own an issue: generation skips player-clan nobles and targets notables; `issue.IssueOwner == Hero.MainHero` paths in `IssueBase` (`IsTriedToSolveBefore`) suggest player-owned issues exist via dialogs, but a raise path for creating a player-owned issue was not found — gate on clan, not on MainHero.
- Crafting-order completer: `WeaponDesignVM._getCurrentCraftingHero().Hero` is passed as `completerHero`; whether the UI hero selector allows companions (not just `Hero.MainHero`) was not confirmed from the VM code — treat `completerHero` as "player-side hero".
- Persuasion partner identity: no explicit argument names the conversation partner; using `ConversationManager.OneToOneConversationHero` as the persuasion target is inferred from the sole caller chain, not asserted by the event args.

## Q43 — Proximity trigger

Status: DRAFT

### Answer

There is no proximity event (Q42 already lists this as the polling-only signal `nearSettlement`). Detection is **a distance poll on a game-time tick + a two-threshold latch** (Schmitt trigger) whose state lives in the behavior's saved data. Every primitive needed is public and already mapped in Q28: `MobileParty.MainParty` (`MobileParty.cs:276`, = `Campaign.Current.MainParty`), `MobileParty.Position` (`:1061`, a `CampaignVec2`), `Settlement.Position` / `Settlement.GatePosition` (`Settlement.cs:277` / `:271`), `Settlement.Find(string)` (`:1145`).

**1. Which tick.** Time-unit conversions and the tick table are in Q27 (`MapTimeTracker.Tick(4320f * _dt)`, `Campaign.cs:874`): 1 campaign dt unit = 4320 game seconds = 1.2 game hours, 1 game day = 80 real seconds at 1× speed (≈20 s fast-forward), so **1 game hour ≈ 3.3 real s at 1×, ≈0.8 s at 4×**.

| Tick (public?) | Mechanism | How often, in campaign time | Cost for this poll | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CampaignEvents.HourlyTickEvent` (`IMbEvent`, no args, `CampaignEvents.cs:837`) | periodic event made by `Campaign.CreateCampaignEvents` with `CampaignTime.Hours(1f)` (`Campaign.cs:1017`), handler `Campaign.HourlyTick` (`:771`) → `CampaignEventDispatcher.HourlyTick()` (`:1233`) | exactly 1×/game hour, aligned to the whole-hour boundary (Q27) | one distance per configured target per hour — O(1) each | **default choice** |
| `CampaignEvents.HourlyTickPartyEvent` (`IMbEvent<MobileParty>`, `:841`) | `_hourlyTickMobilePartyTicker` over `MobileParty.All` (`CampaignPeriodicEventManager.cs:218`), `PeriodicTickSome(DeltaHours)` (`:392`) — one entity per map frame, amortised | each party 1×/game hour, *not* hour-aligned | same, plus a `party == MobileParty.MainParty` filter (MainParty is in `MobileParty.All`, see Q37) | fine alternative; use when the trigger is per-party-shaped |
| `CampaignEvents.QuarterHourlyTickEvent` (`IMbEvent`, `:839`) | `Campaign.cs:1024` with `CampaignTime.Hours(0.25f)`, handler `Campaign.QuarterHourlyTick` (`:777`) → dispatcher `:1242` | 4×/game hour, hour-aligned | 4× the hourly work, still trivial | use when 1 hour is too coarse |
| mod-owned finer event: `CampaignPeriodicEventManager.CreatePeriodicEvent(CampaignTime triggerPeriod, CampaignTime initialWait)` → public `MBCampaignEvent` + `AddHandler`, handler shape `void H(MBCampaignEvent e, object[] args)` | public static (`CampaignPeriodicEventManager.cs:408`); swept by `SignalPeriodicEvents` (`:432`-`:444`), `MBCampaignEvent.CheckUpdate` drains `NextTriggerTime += TriggerPeriod` in a `while (NextTriggerTime.IsPast …)` loop (catch-up, no drift) | the whole sweep only runs every `MinimumPeriodicEventInterval = CampaignTime.Hours(0.05f)` (`:207`) → **a mod cannot poll faster than every 0.05 game hours ≈ 3 game minutes** (20×/hour) with this mechanism | this is what vanilla's own proximity behavior uses — `MapTracksCampaignBehavior.AddEventHandler` (`:215`-`:218`) creates `Hours(0.25f)` with an initial wait of `Hours(0.1f)` |
| `CampaignEvents.TickEvent` (`IMbEvent<float>`, arg = campaign `_dt`, `:847`) | dispatched once per map frame by `CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance.Tick(_dt)` inside `Campaign.Tick` (`Campaign.cs:960`) | every render frame while time flows (~60/s, ≈200 per game hour at 1×); skipped while `_dt == 0` except the first frames (`:958`) | per-frame listener overhead for work that only matters per game minute | **avoid**; only with a self-throttle that accumulates `_dt` |
| AI partial-hourly tick `CampaignEvents.TickPartialHourlyAiEvent` (`IMbEvent<MobileParty>`, `:867`) and `AiHourlyTickEvent` (`:865`) | nine category tickers `_caravan/…/_lord/_partiesWithoutPartyComponents…PartialHourlyAiEventTicker` with `PeriodicTickSome(DeltaHours * 0.99)` (`:376`-`:387`); raised by `AiPartyThinkBehavior` (`:18`) | ~1×/game hour per AI party; the actual think pass runs only every 6th such tick (`DefaultThinkingPeriodInHours = 6`, `:14`) | n/a | **wrong tick for the player party**: the think pass excludes it explicitly (`mobileParty != MobileParty.MainParty`, `:65`), so `AiHourlyTickEvent` never fires for MainParty |

Recommendation: subscribe `HourlyTickEvent` in `RegisterEvents()` (Q23/Q35 listener idiom) and gate on the player party; move to a mod-owned `CreatePeriodicEvent(CampaignTime.Hours(0.25f), CampaignTime.Hours(0.1f))` — re-created from `CampaignEvents.OnGameLoadFinishedEvent` plus new-game, exactly the `MapTracksCampaignBehavior` shape (`:133` → `GameLoadFinished` `:197` → `AddEventHandler` `:215`) — only if the design needs sub-hour reaction. Hourly is enough because at Speed 4 the party spends ≈7 game hours inside a 25-unit ring (7 polls), and the latch below makes the poll phase irrelevant. The boundary alignment of `HourlyTickEvent` is also convenient for cooldown stamps (`CampaignTime.Now.GetHourOfDay`, Q27).

**2. Computing map distance.**

| Member (public?) | What it measures | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| `CampaignVec2.Distance(CampaignVec2)` / `DistanceSquared(CampaignVec2)` + `Vec2` overloads — `CampaignVec2.cs:180`/`:170`/`:185`/`:175` | straight-line distance in **campaign map units**; no terrain, river or gate awareness | trivial vector arithmetic; in a hot loop compare `DistanceSquared` against squared radii (Q28 uses `2500f` = 50²) |
| `MobileParty.MainParty.Position` (`CampaignVec2`, `MobileParty.cs:1061`), `CampaignVec2.ToVec2()` (`:117`) | the party's map point | free |
| `Settlement.Position` (`Settlement.cs:277`), `Settlement.GatePosition` (`:271`) | target point; `GatePosition` equals the settlement position unless the settlement XML carries `gate_posX/gate_posY` (parsed `:950`-`:953`) | free |
| `DistanceHelper.FindClosestDistanceFromMobilePartyToSettlement(MobileParty, Settlement, MobileParty.NavigationType)` and its 3 overloads (`out bool isTargetingPort` / `out float landRatio` / `maxDistance` → bool) — `Helpers/DistanceHelper.cs:133`/`:163`/`:170`/`:176` | vanilla's own party→settlement distance: navigation-capability aware, port variant considered for naval parties; if the party is *inside* a settlement it switches to settlement→settlement navigation distance | moderate: face/terrain queries + navigation-cache lookups — **no A\* per call** |
| `Campaign.Current.Models.MapDistanceModel.GetDistance(MobileParty, Settlement, bool isTargetingPort, MobileParty.NavigationType, out float estimatedLandRatio)` (`Campaign.Models` public, `Campaign.cs:386`; `MapDistanceModel.cs:35`; default `DefaultMapDistanceModel.cs:60`) | same measure at model level: same navigation face → straight line to `GatePosition`, other face → nearest entrance + cached settlement-to-settlement distance with land ratio, sea-only party at a land target → the unreachable sentinel | cache lookup + one straight line |
| `MapDistanceModel.PossibleMaximumMapBoundary = 100000000f` (`const`, `MapDistanceModel.cs:23`) | "no route" marker returned by the path-aware measure — compare `>=` it and treat as unreachable, never against a radius | free |
| `Settlement.StartFindingLocatablesAroundPosition(Vec2 position, float radius)` + `Settlement.FindNextLocatable(ref LocatableSearchData<Settlement>)` (`Settlement.cs:1160`/`:1165`) | "which settlements lie within R of this point" as a grid query (wrapper over `Campaign.SettlementLocator`, `Campaign.cs:441`); the shape vanilla's proximity behavior uses (`MapTracksCampaignBehavior.cs:233`). `LocatorGrid<T>` itself is internal (`TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.Map/LocatorGrid.cs:6`) → a mod can query vanilla's settlement grid but cannot build its own; `LocatableSearchData<T>` is a public struct (`Map/LocatableSearchData.cs:5`) | grid cells, not a scan |
| `SettlementHelper.FindNearestSettlementToPoint(in CampaignVec2, Func<Settlement,bool>)` (`Helpers/SettlementHelper.cs:69`, straight-line over `Settlement.All`), `FindNearestSettlementToMobileParty` (`:50`) and `FindNextSettlementAroundMobileParty(MobileParty, NavigationType, float maxDistance, int lastIndex, Func<…>)` (`:164`, path distance, resumable index) | nearest-settlement lookup when the target is *not* named in config | straight scan of `Settlement.All` (493 settlements in the shipped SandBox XML) or path-distance with a `Campaign.MapDiagonal * 2f` cutoff |
| `Campaign.MapDiagonal` / `MapDiagonalSquared` / `MapMinimumPosition` / `MapMaximumPosition` (public static, `Campaign.cs:192`-`:198`, computed `:1097`-`:1098`) | whole-map scale for normalising a radius | free |

For a settlement named in the mod's JSON the poll is one or two calls per target per tick — no scan, no pathfinding. Reach it from the config string id, never from a stored object (see 4/5). Q28 covers the same primitives plus the "adjacent" thresholds (`150f` path units, `2500f` squared, `< 1f..2f` squared = standing next to it).

**3. Radius scale (what the units mean).**

* Map extent of the shipped SandBox settlement data ≈ 707 × 548 map units (x 76.5…782.6, y 62.2…610.6 over all 493 settlements), i.e. a map diagonal of ≈900 units — but read `Campaign.MapDiagonal` at runtime instead of hardcoding. A 25-unit radius is ≈3 % of the diagonal.
* Speed → distance: `MobileParty.Speed` (public, `MobileParty.cs:407`); vanilla base `DefaultPartySpeedCalculatingModel.BaseSpeed => 4f` (`:93`) scaled by party size as `BaseSpeed * (200 / (200 + menCount)) ^ 0.4` (`:240`) → ≈3.3 at 100 men, ≈2.7 at 300 men; modifiers of −0.3 forest, −0.3 water, −0.25 night, −0.1 snow, −0.1 desert, +0.3 cavalry, +0.15 mounted footmen (`:61`-`:73`).
* Movement is `NextMoveDistance = Speed × dt` with `dt` in campaign dt (`MobileParty.ComputeNextMoveDistance`, `:2868`; army-leader twin `:2855`), and Q27 gives 1 dt unit = 1.2 game hours ⇒ **distance per game hour = Speed × 0.833 units**; Speed 4 ⇒ ≈3.3 units/hour, ≈80 units/day (independent of the time-control mode, which changes only real seconds per game hour).
* Vanilla's own rules of thumb treat Speed as *units per game hour*: patrol search radius `= ConversationParty.Speed * CampaignTime.HoursInDay * 0.5f` (`PatrolPartiesCampaignBehavior.cs:388`); a spawn delay of `distance / Speed + 3` hours (`LandlordNeedsAccessToVillageCommonsIssueBehavior.cs:744`). So "radius ≈ Speed × desired lead time in hours" is within ~20 %.
* Vanilla distance bands in map units: `DefaultEncounterModel.GetEncounterJoiningRadius => 3f` (`:36`) — parties meet at ~3 units; `SettlementDefendingWaitingPositionRadius => 3f` and `SettlementDefendingNearbyPartyCheckRadius => 9f` (`DefaultMobilePartyAIModel.cs:32`/`:30`) — the "standing right outside the fortification" band; `FleeToNearbySettlementRadius => FleeToNearbyPartyRadius * 2f` (`:20`) ≈ 3 × 10 × 0.25 × 1.5 × 2 ≈ **22.5 units** — vanilla's notion of "a settlement a party can reach right now" (uses `AiCheckInterval => 0.25f` `:16` and `Campaign.EstimatedMaximumLordPartySpeedExceptPlayer = 10f`, `Campaign.cs:330`/`:1195`); `DefaultMapDistanceModel.MaximumSpawnDistanceForCompanionsAfterDisband => 150f` (`:16`) — the far band (Q28); `EscortMerchantCaravanIssueBehavior.cs:798` treats `DistanceSquared < 9f` (3 units) as "at the village".
* Settlement spacing, measured from the shipped `settlements.xml` (493 settlements, 120 towns+castles): nearest-fortification distance min **16.9**, p10 22.2, **median 30.9**, p90 44.4, max 54.8 units; gate-to-position offset min 0.01, median ≈2.5, max ≈98 units (the far ones are port entries — so use `Position` for "approaching the town", `GatePosition` for "at the gate").
* **Suggested scale: `R_enter` = 20-25 units, `R_exit` = 2 × `R_enter` (40-50).** For a Speed-4 party that is ≈6-7 game hours (≈20-25 real s at 1×, ≈5-6 s fast-forward) of lead time before it reaches the gate, and `R_exit − R_enter` ≈ 25 units is far more than one hourly poll step (≈3.3 units), so the latch cannot flap between polls. Caveat from the spacing data: min fortification spacing is 16.9 units, so 25-unit rings *can* overlap; if only one proximity line should ever be active, keep a single closest armed target (or suppress other targets while one is armed) — that is a mod policy decision, not engine behaviour.

**4. Hysteresis and the state that must survive save/load.**

Per target settlement, keep a latch (enter radius `R1`, exit radius `R2 > R1`). Per poll, in order:

1. `if (!MobileParty.MainParty.IsValid) return;` — same guard vanilla uses (`MapTracksCampaignBehavior.cs:223`).
2. If the party is inside a settlement, skip the approach edge (see 5).
3. `d = MobileParty.MainParty.Position.Distance(target.GatePosition)` (or `.DistanceSquared` against squared constants, Q28).
4. `if (armed && d > R2) armed = false;` — re-arm only after genuinely leaving the larger ring.
5. `if (!armed && d <= R1) { armed = true; fire the trigger; }` — so the line fires exactly once per approach, on the way in.

State to persist, using this repo's Q8/Q9 pattern (`AlbocariusCompanionsCampaignBehavior.SyncData` already does `dataStore.SyncData("_key", ref field)` with `List<string>` / `Dictionary<string, …>`):

* The latch: settlement **string id** + armed flag (or a `List<string>` of currently armed ids). Re-resolve with `Settlement.Find(id)` after load — do not keep the object obtained before a load. Old saves without the key keep the initialised (empty) field and therefore start unarmed (Q9 semantics).
* A "already said it" / cooldown marker: prefer Q20's conversation once-markers (`_conversationFlags`) keyed per (companion, settlement, approach) rather than a second counter; if a time cooldown is wanted, store a `CampaignTime` stamp (`CampaignTime.Now`, Q27) not a frame/poll counter, because poll counts vanish across save/load and speed changes.
* A mod-owned `MBCampaignEvent` does **not** survive save/load: `Campaign.CustomPeriodicCampaignEvents` (`Campaign.cs:424`) is absent from Campaign's save-collect list (`:1841`-`:1871`) and `MBCampaignEvent.NextTriggerTime` is `[CachedData]` (`MBCampaignEvent.cs:14`). Create the event from a `CampaignEvents.OnGameLoadFinishedEvent` listener (and after new game) — vanilla's proximity behavior does exactly that (`:133`/`:197`/`:215`); listeners themselves are re-registered every session (Q8).
* The built-in tickers do survive (their `PeriodicTicker<T>` state is save-registered, `[SaveableProperty] TickDebt/Index`), so subscribing to `HourlyTickEvent` needs no extra persistence at all.

**5. Finding the settlement by string id, and "already inside"; worked example (Onira).**

* `Settlement.Find(string idString)` — public static (`Settlement.cs:1145`), implemented as `MBObjectManager.Instance.GetObject<Settlement>(idString)` → **returns null for an unknown id**, so log and disable that target instead of throwing (Q15 error safety). `Settlement.FindFirst(predicate)` (`:1150`) and `Settlement.StartFindingLocatablesAroundPosition` (`:1160`) cover the unnamed-target variants.
* Ids come from `~/bannerlord/moduledata_win/SandBox/ModuleData/settlements.xml` (`<Settlement id=… posX posY gate_posX gate_posY owner culture …>`, 493 entries: 273 villages, 99 hideouts, 67 castles, 53 towns). **Onira = `id="town_ES5"`**, position (645.315, 325.385), gate (644.077, 327.4114), `owner="Faction.clan_empire_south_1"`, culture `Culture.empire`. Its nearest neighbours: `village_ES5_3` 19.9 units, `village_ES5_1` 25.1, `village_ES5_2` 27.4, nearest foreign fortification 31.1 — so `R_enter = 25` around Onira reaches its own villages but no other town or castle.
* "Player is already inside" (Q28): `MobileParty.MainParty.CurrentSettlement` (public, `MobileParty.cs:598`) is non-null only while the party is physically inside a settlement; `Settlement.CurrentSettlement` / `Settlement.Parties` give the same facts from the settlement side. A party that has just walked out of the gate is *not* inside but ~1 unit from it — vanilla expresses that state as `LastVisitedSettlement != null && LastVisitedSettlement.Position.Distance(Position) < 1f` (`AiPartyThinkBehavior.cs:61`); use that (or Q28's `1f..2f`-squared idiom) to swallow the "just left the gate" edge so the companion does not immediately re-greet.
* Wiring for the example: a JSON entry (`"settlementId": "town_ES5"`, `"enterUnits": 25`, `"exitUnits": 50`) resolved with `Settlement.Find` on new game and on load → `HourlyTickEvent` handler → skip when `CurrentSettlement != null` or the party is within 1-2 units of the gate and `armed` is already true from the previous approach → hysteresis latch → on the enter edge raise the mod's `nearSettlement` trigger (Q42) for the Onira-born companion, delivered as an authored conversation entry point (Q20/Q7, with the once-marker) or an in-game notification (Q17). Persist `town_ES5 → armed` in `SyncData`; after a load `Settlement.Find("town_ES5")` re-resolves it and the latch stays closed until the party walks out past 50 units.

### Uncertain

- Physical scale of map units: unresolved in Q28 (they are campaign-map units with no real-world equivalent), and the ≈707 × 548 extent plus the spacing/gate-offset statistics quoted above were computed by parsing the shipped `settlements.xml`, not read from the engine — at runtime normalise against `Campaign.MapDiagonal` instead.
- Membership of `MobileParty.MainParty` in the AI category lists (`MobileParty.AllLordParties` = `CampaignObjectManager.LordParties`, `Campaign.cs:489`; `AllPartiesWithoutPartyComponent` :493) was not traced. The operative, verified fact is the consumer-side exclusion at `AiPartyThinkBehavior.cs:65`, which alone rules out `AiHourlyTickEvent` for the player party.
- `TickEvent`'s real-time rate is render-frame dependent (the ≈200-per-game-hour figure assumes ~60 fps); and whether other game types pass `doParallel: true` to the periodic tickers was not checked — this build passes `false` throughout `InitializeTickers`, so handler re-entrancy is not a concern here.
- The ≤0.05 game-hour latency floor for a mod-owned periodic event is derived from `MinimumPeriodicEventInterval` + the `SignalPeriodicEvents` gate, not documented by vanilla; if the mod needs a faster reaction than that it must accumulate `TickEvent`'s `_dt` itself, which costs a per-frame listener.
- "Custom periodic events do not survive save/load" is inferred from the absence of `Campaign.CustomPeriodicCampaignEvents` from the save-collect list rather than from an explicit save attribute; either way, re-creating the event in `OnGameLoadFinishedEvent` is the safe path and is what vanilla does.
- `Settlement.GatePosition` outliers: the shipped XML shows gate offsets from ≈0.01 to ≈98 units (median ≈2.5); the far entries are presumably ports/harbours but that was not checked entry by entry — measure to `Position` for "nearing the town", to `GatePosition` for "at the gate".
- Radius exclusivity is not an engine property: with a minimum fortification spacing of 16.9 units, `R_enter` = 20-25 rings can overlap around two settlements, so "only one proximity line at a time" needs an explicit tie-break in the mod.

## Q44 — Companion becomes a lord

Status: DRAFT

### Answer

Scope: the dialog chain itself (tokens, texts, priorities, the repeatable fief list) is already mapped in **Q18 Table 5** — not repeated here; this section covers the mechanics behind it, the campaign events it fires and in what order, the relation effects, the mod hook point for the SPEC R3 "`noble`" penalty, how the mod detects a former companion who now leads a clan, and the conversation consequences for that hero. Also relevant: Q19 (dismissal vs `ByTurningToLord`), Q21 (relation storage/effective mapping/write API), Q31 (party-vs-clan membership; the raw main-party roster write), Q33 (policy table: the grant-a-fief row marks the mod registry entry and its JSON dialogs "stale — decide"), Q39/Q40 (event rows; `OnClanCreatedEvent` is already slated as the mod `clanCreated` bus hook).

**1. Every vanilla way a player companion becomes a clan leader / lord.** There is exactly **one live, player-facing path**: the "grant a fief" conversation, executed by `CompanionRolesCampaignBehavior.ClanNameSelectionIsDone(string clanName)` (:258). Gates, in conversation order:

| Gate | Code | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| option shows | `turn_companion_to_lord_on_condition` (:170) | `Hero.OneToOneConversationHero.IsPlayerCompanion` **and** `Hero.MainHero.IsKingdomLeader` (i.e. `MapFaction.IsKingdomFaction && MapFaction.Leader == MainHero`, `Hero.cs:605` — this is the "kingdom/king conversation" of the question) and the hero's party is not currently at sea |
| refusal branch | `turn_companion_to_lord_no_fief_on_condition` (:165); `companion_is_leading_caravan_condition` (:185) | PlayerClan owns no Town/Castle → "no fief" line; he leads a caravan → he refuses |
| fief list | `fief_grant_answer_consequence` (:195), `list_player_fief_clickable_condition` (:200) | repeatable over `Hero.MainHero.Clan.Settlements` where `IsTown ‖ IsCastle`; blocked while `fief.SiegeEvent != null`, `fief.Town.IsOwnerUnassigned`, or an unresolved `SettlementClaimantDecision`/`SettlementClaimantPreliminaryDecision` exists for it |
| confirm box | `turn_companion_to_lord_consequence` (:232) + `fief_selected_confirm_clickable_on_condition` (:447) | player can press Confirm only with `Hero.MainHero.Gold >= 20000` and `Hero.MainHero.Clan.Influence >= 500f` (`NeededGoldToGrantFief`); the actual charge happens later (see below) |
| clan name | `ConfirmTurningCompanionToLordConsequence` (:244) | free-text `ShowTextInquiry`, validated by `FactionHelper.IsClanNameApplicable`, callback `ClanNameSelectionIsDone` |

The execution block, in statement order (:260–288): capture `Hero.OneToOneConversationHero` → `RemoveCompanionAction.ApplyByByTurningToLord(Hero.MainHero.Clan, hero)` (the vanilla double-"By" typo is real; detail `ByTurningToLord` skips the party-roster removal and does **not** make him fugitive, Q19) → `hero.SetNewOccupation(Occupation.Lord)` → `Clan.CreateCompanionToLordClan(hero, _selectedFief, clanNameText, bannerId)` (:266, the **only** call site of this public factory in the whole decompiled tree) → main-party roster fix and party handling (:267–282, see row 5 of the event table) → `AdjustCompanionsEquipment` (:291, `EquipmentSelectionModel.GetEquipmentForCompanionWhenTurningToLord`, keeps the higher-tier item per slot) → `SpawnNewHeroesForNewCompanionClan` (:359, two founder heroes from `hero.Culture.LordTemplates` via `HeroCreator.CreateSpecialHero`, age `RandomInt(adult,50)`, Steward/Leadership/OneHanded/Medicine and OneHanded/Leadership/Tactics/Engineering skill sets, then joined to the new clan — see row 6) → `GiveGoldAction.ApplyBetweenCharacters(MainHero, hero, 20000)` (the player pays; the hero keeps the purse, it is *not* refunded) → `GainKingdomInfluenceAction.ApplyForDefault(MainHero, −500f)` → `ChangeRelationAction.ApplyPlayerRelation(hero, 50)` → `ConversationManager.ContinueConversation()` (the thanks line, Q18).

Inside `Clan.CreateCompanionToLordClan` (Clan.cs:1339–1354): `CreateClan(Hero.MainHero.MapFaction.StringId + "_companion_clan")` (uniquified by `CampaignObjectManager.FindNextUniqueStringId<Clan>`, Clan.cs:740) → `ChangeClanName` → `Culture = settlement.Culture`, banner from the settlement's faction colors → `clan.Kingdom = Hero.MainHero.Clan.Kingdom` → `clan.Tier = ClanTierModel.CompanionToLordClanStartingTier` (= 2, `DefaultClanTierModel.cs:39`) → `SetInitialHomeSettlement` → **`hero.Clan = clan`** (the `Hero.Clan` setter, `Hero.cs:498`, moves the hero into the clan's lord/hero caches and fires `OnHeroChangedClan`) → `clan.SetLeader(hero)` (`Clan.cs:948`, a bare field write — **no event**) → `clan.IsNoble = true` → `ChangeOwnerOfSettlementAction.ApplyByGift(settlement, hero)` → `CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance.OnClanCreated(clan, isCompanion: true)` as the factory's **last statement**.

Ruled out as companion→lord paths (checked; none applies to a hired player companion):

| Mechanism | Why it is not this flow |
|---|---|
| `ApplyHeirSelectionAction` → `ChangeClanLeaderAction` (SandBox `HeirSelectionCampaignBehavior:137` on player death, `RetirementCampaignBehavior:51` on retirement) | picks from `Clan.GetHeirApparents()` (`Clan.cs:1356`), which skips `IsWanderer` heroes → hired companions can never inherit PlayerClan |
| `ChangeClanLeaderAction` succession from `KillCharacterAction` when a clan leader dies | iterates clan `Heroes`, never `Companions`; player companions are not in their clan's hero caches while hired (`CompanionOf` lives on the hero, the clan keeps a separate `_companionsCache`) |
| `KingdomDecision`/`KingSelectionKingdomDecision:222`, `ClanVariablesCampaignBehavior:111/218/299` | move *existing lords* between clans or set leaders of existing clans; no occupation change, no `IsPlayerCompanion` input |
| `CampaignCheats.create_clan` (:2019) | debug; creates a brand-new special hero, not a conversion, and fires `OnClanCreated(clan, isCompanion: false)` (:2057) |

**2. Campaign events fired, in order.** Everything happens synchronously inside one dialog consequence (the modal inquiries complete before callbacks run):

| # | Event (payload) | Raised by / where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `CompanionRemoved(hero, detail: ByTurningToLord)` | last statement of `RemoveCompanionAction.ApplyInternal`; `CompanionOf = null` and the PlayerClan companion-cache removal happened first, **silently** (the `Hero.CompanionOf` setter, `Hero.cs:253`, fires no event) |
| 2 | `HeroOccupationChanged(hero, <old occupation>)` | `SetNewOccupation(Occupation.Lord)` (:262); `IMbEvent<Hero, Occupation>`, payload is the *old* occupation (Q39/Q40) |
| 3 | `OnHeroChangedClan(hero, oldClan)` — `oldClan == null` for a hired companion, because his PlayerClan link lived in `CompanionOf`, not `_clan` | `Hero.Clan` setter inside the factory (:1348) |
| 4 | `OnSettlementOwnerChanged(fief, openToClaim: false, newOwner: hero, oldOwner, null, detail: ByGift)` | `ApplyByGift` → last statement of `ChangeOwnerOfSettlementAction.ApplyInternal` (:94); no relation writes inside it |
| 5 | `OnClanCreated(clan, isCompanion: true)` | factory's last statement (Clan.cs:1352). State at this moment: leader, Kingdom, tier 2, `IsNoble`, fief ownership all set; **no lord party yet, founders not yet created, gold/influence/+50 not yet moved**. If the companion was riding in the MainParty, the roster decrement and the `partyBelongedTo.ActualClan = clan` re-point (:281, `MobileParty.cs:972`) run **after** the event, and no `MobilePartyCreated` fires; only a partyless hero gets `LordPartyComponent.CreateLordParty` (:274) + 12–15 BasicTroop + 10–15 EliteBasicTroop, which fires `MobilePartyCreated` |
| 6 | `HeroCreated ×2` (`IMbEvent<Hero, bool>`, special-spawn flag; see Q39/Q40) for the founders, each followed by `OnHeroChangedClan(founder, null)` | `CreateNewHeroForNewCompanionClan` (:421) + `item.Clan = clan` (:404); founders `EnterSettlementAction.ApplyForCharacterOnly` into the fief (:408) |
| 7 | `HeroRelationChanged` ×3+ (silent pairs included) | see 3 below: two silent (founder↔MainHero, `showQuickNotification: false`, :406), one notification-shown founder↔founder (:415), then the +50 player row (:287) |

No `OnClanLeaderChangedEvent` fires anywhere in this flow — that event exists only on `ChangeClanLeaderAction` (`IMbEvent<Hero, Hero>`, `CampaignEvents.cs:925`), which the conversion never calls.

**3. What vanilla already does to relations.** Full write sites in the flow, with magnitudes from the code:

| Pair | Change | Where |
|---|---|---|
| MainHero ↔ new lord | first `+RandomInt(5,10)` (silent, as one of the clan founders, :406), then **+50** via `ChangeRelationAction.ApplyPlayerRelation(hero, 50)` (:287), i.e. stored ≈ `Round(50 × GetRelationIncreaseFactor)` on top (Q21 scaling/clamp rules) | `SpawnNewHeroesForNewCompanionClan`, then :287 |
| founder ↔ founder (the two new heroes) | `+RandomInt(5,10)`, notification shown | :415 |
| founder ↔ founder ↔ MainHero other combinations | the second founder also gets `+5..10` vs MainHero (:406) | :404–408 |
| **new lord ↔ any other NPC lord** | **nothing. Zero. No vanilla code writes a single row here.** | absence verified by reading every call above |
| new lord's clan ↔ NPC lords | also nothing: `ApplyByGift` and the clan creation contain no relation writes | `ChangeOwnerOfSettlementAction.ApplyInternal`, `CreateCompanionToLordClan` |

Effective-relation consequence (Q21): while he was a companion, every third party's "opinion of him" was the **player's own number** (pair (lord, companion) collapses to (lord's clan leader, MainHero)); after conversion he stands for himself and every such row starts at 0 + personality terms — vanilla never seeds new lords (`CharacterRelationCampaignBehavior.UpdateFriendshipAndEnemies` runs only at campaign start over then-existing lords). So the SPEC R3 "making a non-noble a lord costs relation with the other lords" fills a genuine vanilla gap; nothing to deduplicate against. The 0.7× relation inheritance in `DefaultDiplomacyModel.GetRelationChangeAfterClanLeaderIsDead` (`:925`) belongs to the succession path only — the conversion does not route through `ChangeClanLeaderAction`.

**4. Mod hook for the `noble`-based relation penalty.** Recommended: **`CampaignEvents.OnClanCreatedEvent`, filtered `isCompanion == true`** — verified as an exact discriminator: the only raiser passing `true` is `Clan.CreateCompanionToLordClan` (rebels `CreateSettlementRebelClan` and `CampaignCheats:2057` pass `false`; Q39's row lists all raisers), and its only live caller is the grant flow. At the event the leader, `Kingdom`, tier, `IsNoble` and fief are already final, and the hero already has `Occupation.Lord` / `IsPlayerCompanion == false`. Write the penalty with the Q21 lord↔lord API: `ChangeRelationAction.ApplyRelationChangeBetweenHeroes(newLord, otherLord, −N[, showQuickNotification])` (the 4-arg overload, `ChangeRelationAction.cs:35`; negative changes are not charm-scaled, Q21) over the **clan leaders** of the target set — `clan.Kingdom.Clans` other than PlayerClan and the new clan (per design, other kingdoms too); always write against leaders because `GetHeroesForEffectiveRelation` maps non-leaders to their `Clan.Leader` (Q21). Do **not** use `ApplyPlayerRelation` — it hard-codes `Hero.MainHero` as the source. Safety: the mod's own relation-event guard (`HarmonyPatches.cs:155`) and the vanilla −10 break-up listener are unaffected — `IsPlayerCompanion` is already false, and `ApplyRelationChangeBetweenHeroes` between two lords cannot re-trigger the companion exit check. Alternative if more of the post-factory state is needed (party, founders, gold): a Harmony postfix on the public static `Clan.CreateCompanionToLordClan` — it returns after every step of the factory; but per project policy prefer the event, deferring any state the event cannot see.

"is now a lord" feedback: **vanilla has none.** No listener of `OnClanCreatedEvent` posts a notification (`DefaultNotificationsCampaignBehavior` subscribes ~40 events but not this one; `MapTrackerProvider.cs:276` only removes the old party tracker entry; `CampaignFactionManagerBehaviour` refreshes the at-war list). Even the fief toast is absent — `DefaultNotificationsCampaignBehavior.OnSettlementOwnerChanged` (:864) posts quick info only for `detail == BySiege` (`:872`), and `ByGift` falls through. The player currently sees only the companion-leave toast (Q33/Q34: `ByTurningToLord` is ordinal 3, which the notification behavior includes), the +50 relation toast and the gold-transfer toast. The mod should raise its own line in the `clanCreated` handler via the Q17 API (`InformationManager.DisplayMessage`), optionally `MBInformationManager.AddQuickInformation`-style text (that toast API is used by the notification behavior, `:876`, and not otherwise mapped in this document).

**5. What survives conversion — detection recipe.** The **same `Hero` instance** persists; nothing is killed and recreated (contrast Q19's dismissal).

| Field | After conversion | Use for detection |
|---|---|---|
| `Hero.Id`, `Hero.StringId` | unchanged — StringId was fixed at hire/creation (`HeroCreator.cs:294` seeds it from the template StringId, then `FindNextUniqueStringId<Hero>` at construction, `Hero.cs:1474/1485`) and never re-assigned | store the id at hire; exact match keeps working |
| `Hero.Template` (= `CharacterObject.OriginalCharacter`, `Hero.cs:298`) | intact | `ModRuntime.IsModHero` and `hero.Template.StringId == id` keep matching the registry |
| `Occupation` | `Lord`; `IsWanderer` false, `IsLord` true (`Hero.cs:399`) | occupation check |
| `CompanionOf` | null → `IsPlayerCompanion` false (`Hero.cs:333`) | "was, no longer" |
| PlayerClan caches | removed from `Companions` *and* `Heroes` (`Clan.OnCompanionRemoved`, `Clan.cs:1220`) | roster test flips |
| `Clan` / `IsClanLeader` | the new clan; `Clan.Leader == hero` → `IsClanLeader` true (`Hero.cs:617`) | leader test |
| new clan | `IsNoble == true`, `Tier == 2`, `Kingdom ==` player's kingdom (at creation), `StringId` starts with `<MainHero.MapFaction.StringId>_companion_clan`, `Name` = player-typed clan name | heuristic only — rely on the hero fields above, not on the StringId suffix (see Uncertain) |
| fief | `Town.OwnerClan == new clan`, `IsOwnerUnassigned` cleared; `GovernorOf` cleared by `RemoveCompanionAction` | cross-check |
| name shown in UI | surname/full name follow the new `Clan.Name` | cosmetic |

**6. Adding mod options to the vanilla lord conversation without touching vanilla lines.** The lord conversation graph routes every `UsesLordConversations` NPC (true for `Occupation.Lord`, `LordConversationsCampaignBehavior.cs:123`) through the **same hub token `hero_main_options`**: greeting `lord_start` → hub (`hero_ask_4`, :240, unconditioned), and after each exchange `lord_pretalk` → `hero_pretalk_2` (:767) → hub again. So the mod never edits or replaces vanilla lines: `starter.AddPlayerLine(<new unique id>, "hero_main_options", <new output token>, text, condition, consequence[, priority])` — exactly the Q7 mechanism the mod already uses (`CompanionDialogs.cs:110/117`), optionally also on `lord_start`/`lord_pretalk` for greeting-time options; priorities control ordering (Q18/Q20; the mod uses 105 on the hub). The converted hero *will* sit at the vanilla hub: his vanilla companion-only options self-hide (their conditions require `IsPlayerCompanion` / `HeroHelper.IsCompanionInPlayerParty`), and vanilla lord options appear normally. The mod's own hub options also still show — `IsThisCompanion()` is `ModRuntime.IsModHero(hero) && hero.Template.StringId == id`, both template-registry based and immune to the conversion; the hire chain self-hides (its condition requires `PartyBelongedTo == null` and the new lord has a party), while `ask_backstory` and the intro family keep firing, which the mod may want to occupation-gate (`hero.IsLord`) or gate on a mod-side state flag — this is exactly the "go stale — decide" row of Q33.

## Q41 — Campaign events catalog 7 (time, lifecycle, quests)

Status: DRAFT

### Answer

All 32 members are `public static` `IMbEvent<…>` (or bare `IMbEvent`) properties on `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.CampaignEvents` — declaration range lines 593–941 of `CampaignEvents.cs`; the `CampaignEventReceiver` overrides that `Invoke` the statics sit in the same file (lines 1428–2313). Fan-out and subscription are exactly as in Q8/Q23 (`CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance.OnX(…)` → the `CampaignEvents` override → static event; `CampaignEvents.X.AddNonSerializedListener(this, handler)` in `RegisterEvents`), so they are not repeated per row. Raise sites were grepped in `TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem*`, `SandBox*`, `StoryMode*` only (never NavalDLC); **no member here is DLC-only**, but the two tutorial members fire only in a StoryMode campaign — their sole raiser `GauntletTutorialSystem` (SandBox.GauntletUI) is started by `StoryModeGauntletUISubModule` (:21) and never by SandBox alone. Eight traps. (1) **Dispatcher method names differ from the event names**: `OnSessionStart`→`OnSessionLaunchedEvent`, `OnAfterSessionStart`→`OnAfterSessionLaunchedEvent`, `Tick(dt)`→`TickEvent`, `AiHourlyTick`/`TickPartialHourlyAi`→`…Event`; and one member has no `Event` suffix at all (`GameMenuOpened`, :747). (2) The three `OnNewGameCreated*` members all come out of **one** override, `CampaignEvents.OnNewGameCreated` (:2077–2086): main event, then a hard-coded `for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++)` of follow-ups (the const `OnNewGameCreatedPartialFollowUpEventMaxIndex = 100` lives at :295), then the End event; the chain runs only on the new-campaign path (`Campaign.cs:1585`, reached from :1694), never on a save load (:1666–1671) — see **Q8** for the whole load/new-game ordering. (3) Three raisers are written as a cast, `((CampaignEventReceiver)CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance).OnX(…)` (`SandBoxGameManager.OnLoadFinished` :177, `MissionBoardGameLogic.SetGameOver` :314, `GauntletTutorialSystem`), so grepping only `CampaignEventDispatcher.Instance.OnX` misses them. (4) `AiHourlyTickEvent` **never** fires for the player party (`mobileParty != MobileParty.MainParty` gate, `AiPartyThinkBehavior.PartyHourlyAiTick` :65) while `TickPartialHourlyAiEvent` **does** — the main party has no party component and therefore lands in `_partiesWithoutPartyComponent` (`CampaignObjectManager.AddPartyToAppropriateList`, :549–587), which has its own partial-AI ticker (`CampaignPeriodicEventManager` :280). (5) Except for those two AI members, **nothing in this catalog carries a party/clan/hero subject**, so "is the player involved" must be derived inside the handler from `Hero.MainHero` / `MobileParty.MainParty` / `Clan.PlayerClan`. (6) `OnTradeRumorIsTakenEvent`'s second parameter is optional and the only non-DLC raiser omits it (`CaravansCampaignBehavior` :1972) → `sourceSettlement` is always `null` outside NavalDLC. (7) The portrait pop-up pair is pure UI and the `CampaignEvents` overrides themselves stop/unstop time (`TimeControlMode = Stop` + `SetTimeControlModeLock`, :2229–2243), and the *closed* member takes **no arguments**, so you cannot tell which portrait closed. (8) `QuestLogAddedEvent`/`IssueLogAddedEvent` are **journal-line** events (raised by `AddLog`/`AddDiscreteLog`/`AddTwoWayContinuousLog`), not quest/issue acceptance, and `CollectAvailableTutorialsEvent` is a per-frame `ref`-list collector, not a one-shot. Rows that are already analysed in verified sections cite them (Q8 lifecycle, Q27 time) and add only the raise site and the BEFORE/AFTER answer.

#### Campaign time — global clock ticks

| Member | Arguments (types, in order) | When it fires — raising call site, BEFORE/AFTER the outcome | Player party / clan test | Usefulness → trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Gate: `mobileParty.Ai.HourCounter % num == 0 && mobileParty != MobileParty.MainParty` (:66, `num` normally 6) + early-out on `Ai.IsDisabled \|\| Ai.DoNotMakeNewDecisions` (:49-52) | never the player: the raiser excludes `MobileParty.MainParty` by construction; otherwise `mobileParty.IsLordParty`/`mobileParty.OwnerClan` | not useful — AI-internal scoring hook, and the player party is filtered out |

One call per party per game hour, **BEFORE** the AI decides (its consumer is `AiPartyThinkBehavior` above) | `mobileParty == MobileParty.MainParty` — the main party DOES get it (no party component ⇒ `PartiesWithoutPartyComponent`, `CampaignObjectManager.AddPartyToAppropriateList` :549-587) | not useful — AI scheduler plumbing; for a per-hour main-party beat use `HourlyTickPartyEvent` (Q37/Q40) |

#### Game and campaign lifecycle (see Q8 for the full ordering)

| Member | Arguments (types, in order) | When it fires — raising call site, BEFORE/AFTER the outcome | Player party / clan test | Usefulness → trigger |
